结直肠ESD术后迟发性出血预测模型的系统评价与批判性评估
Prediction Models for Delayed Bleeding After Colorectal Endoscopic Submucosal Dissection: A Systematic Review and Critical Appraisal.
DEN Open · 2027-04 · Miao D, Hou Z, Ge Y, Qi H
意义与启示：现有结直肠ESD术后迟发性出血预测模型均存高偏倚风险且外部验证效能欠佳，提示需开发更稳健模型以指导围手术期抗凝管理。
等级评估：B（单中心回顾性或机制研究） ｜ IF：1.5 ｜ 类型：系统综述/Meta ｜ 系统综述纳入仅5项观察性研究且全部高偏倚风险，外部验证AUC仅0.634，尚不足以改变临床实践。 ｜ 评分：42/100
展开英文原题摘要与原文链接
ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Although many predictive models have been developed or validated for delayed bleeding after colorectal endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD), their methodological quality and clinical utility remain uncertain. We systematically reviewed and critically appraised all available predictive models for this outcome. We searched five databases through March 2026 for observational studies that developed or validated prediction models or scoring systems for delayed bleeding after colorectal ESD in adults (≥18 years). Two reviewers independently extracted data and assessed risk of bias using PROBAST. Of 25,177 records screened, five studies reporting five predictive models were included. The incidence of delayed bleeding ranged from 2.9% to 9.9%. The most commonly used predictors were lesion location and lesion size. Discrimination in derivation cohorts ranged from 0.726 to 0.890, internal validation areas under the curve [AUCs] ranged from 0.739 to 0.870, and the externally validated model achieved an AUC of 0.634. All studies were judged to have a high risk of bias, mainly because of inadequate reporting in the predictor, outcome, and analysis domains, although most had low concerns regarding applicability. This systematic review identified five predictive models for delayed bleeding after colorectal ESD. Lesion location and size were the most frequently reported predictors. Discriminative performance varied across derivation and validation cohorts, with suboptimal external-validation results. All models had a high risk of bias per PROBAST (low concerns regarding applicability); therefore, their findings should be interpreted cautiously.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Curative-intent management of locally recurrent rectal cancer (LRRC) generally comprises neoadjuvant therapy and surgery. In patients with unresectable LRRC, where surgical intervention is not feasible, management is limited to non-operative bimodality therapy with systemic therapy and radiotherapy. Evidence guiding the optimisation of non-operative management remains limited. In this context, the therapeutic goal is to achieve prolonged local control while minimising treatment-related adverse events and preserving quality of life. Radiotherapy dose escalation has been proposed as a potential strategy to achieve this balance. However, its feasibility and safety in the non-operative management of unresectable LRRC have not yet been established. As such, this study aims to evaluate the feasibility and safety of this radiotherapeutic approach, and to determine its impact on both symptom control and oncological outcomes. This prospective, multicentre, single-arm feasibility study will enrol 30 patients with unresectable or inoperable LRRC without distant metastases, or with (oligo)metastatic disease not requiring immediate systemic therapy. Previously irradiated patients will undergo reirradiation with stereotactic body radiotherapy (re-SBRT; 5 × 9 Gy) when feasible, or, alternatively hyperfractionated chemo-reirradiation (50.4 Gy in 1.2 Gy twice-daily fractions with concurrent capecitabine). Radiotherapy-naïve patients will receive chemoradiotherapy with a simultaneous integrated boost (25 × 2.6 Gy, EQD2Gy This protocol describes the STEP-UP study, which will determine the feasibility of radiotherapy dose escalation in unresectable LRRC. If feasible and safe, this approach could provide an effective treatment intensification strategy to improve local control and symptom burden in patients with unresectable LRRC, addressing a major unmet clinical need. ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT07721181Overview of Medical-Scientific Research in the Netherlands (OMON) Registry: NL-011150.International Clinical Trial Registry Platform (ICTRP): NL-OMON61161.

展开英文原题摘要与原文链接
ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) is involved in colorectal cancer (CRC) pathogenesis. Curcumin (CUR) is widely used in the treatment of CRC. Polystyrene nanoparticles (PS-NPS) have a high specific affinity and have an inhibitory effect on cell proliferation. Therefore, the purpose of this study is to investigate the mechanism of inhibition of EMT in colorectal cancer mice by preparing curcumin polystyrene nanoparticles (CUR-PS-NPS). This study aimed to construct CUR-PS-NPS and investigate their mechanism in inhibiting CRC EMT via the miR-186/PI3K/AKT/Twist axis. CUR-PS-NPS were prepared and characterized. In CRC mice intervened with CUR-PS-NPS, the tumor volume was reduced by 50%, the expression of mir-186 was up-regulated by 2.5 times, the phosphorylation level of PI3K/AKT was decreased by 40%, the expression of Twist protein was down-regulated by 35% and the expression of the EMT marker E-cadherin was increased. The expressions of N-cadherin, Vimentin and Snail decreased significantly. CUR-PS-NPS can effectively delay the EMT process of CRC by up-regulating mir-186, inhibiting the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway and the expression of Twist. This discovery provides a new strategy for targeted therapy based on nanocarriers and its application potential in clinical practice can be further explored in the future.

Safety and sustainability of potable tap water irrigation in endoscopy in Canada: an interrupted time series study.
Lancet Regional Health. Americas · 2027-01 · Ahn HS, Moloo H, Kelly K, Zhang L, Dube C, Rostom A, et al.
意义与启示：大规模准实验证实自来水冲洗不劣于无菌水，为修订内镜指南、降低成本与碳排放提供依据，对肠镜筛查实践有直接启示。
等级评估：S（顶刊 IF≥15 或可能改变临床实践） ｜ IF：7.6 ｜ 类型：前瞻/干预性(非随机) ｜ 多中心大样本准实验设计（近3万例）达非劣效，直接挑战现行指南推荐，具实践改变潜力。 ｜ 评分：51/100
展开英文原题摘要与原文链接
ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
International guidelines recommend sterile water for endoscopic irrigation despite limited evidence. Single-use plastic sterile water bottles generate substantial costs, greenhouse gas emissions, and microplastics. We sought to estimate whether replacing sterile water with potable tap water for endoscopic irrigation affected clinical outcomes. This quasi-experimental study involved an interrupted time series design at a multi-campus tertiary care academic health system (The Ottawa Hospital, Canada). All adults undergoing esophagogastroduodenoscopy, colonoscopy, flexible sigmoidoscopy, enteroscopy, ileoscopy, or pouchoscopy between February 2024 and August 2025 were included. A system-wide switch to tap water took place on February 10, 2025. The primary outcome was a composite of emergency department visits, unplanned admissions, or deaths within 7 days post-procedure. Infectious complications within 30 days constituted secondary endpoints. Data were obtained from validated institutional databases. Segmented regression modeled the weekly outcome proportion to estimate the step change post-implementation, with a non-inferiority margin of <0.5% absolute risk increase. A total of 29,522 procedures were performed on 29,423 patients (18,863 pre-implementation; 10,560 post-implementation). Patient and procedural characteristics were comparable. The weekly proportion experiencing the primary outcome was 1.6% in both phases. The post-implementation step change was -0.40% (95% confidence interval [CI] -1.16 to 0.35), with the upper boundary of the 95% CI below the pre-specified non-inferiority margin of 0.5%. Results were similar for infectious complications (step change -0.23%, 95% CI -0.75 to 0.29). Potable tap water was non-inferior to sterile water for endoscopic irrigation with respect to clinical outcomes. These findings provide an evidence base for revising current guideline recommendations that mandate sterile water for endoscopic irrigation. This project was supported by the 2024 Canadian Society of Colorectal Surgeons Research Operating Grant.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
It is recommended that patients receiving emergency surgery and with 'high-risk' of morbidity and mortality should be transferred directly from theatre to critical care. Using a national, population-based cohort study, we estimated the effect of direct transfer to critical care on 90-day mortality after emergency colorectal cancer resection, and the variation amongst English NHS hospitals. Patients who underwent emergency colorectal cancer resection between December 2016 and November 2019 according to Hospital Episodes Statistics, National Bowel Cancer Audit or National Emergency Laparotomy Audit were included. Patients were identified as having a direct transfer to critical care through linkage with the Intensive Care National Audit and Research Centre Case Mix Programme. Multivariable logistic regression and propensity score methods were used to measure the effect of direct transfer to critical care on 90-day mortality. In total, 10,441 patients underwent an emergency colorectal cancer resection. Unadjusted 90-day mortality was higher in the direct transfer to critical care cohort (10.9%) than in patients without direct transfer to critical care (3.7%) (odds ratio [OR]: 3.16, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.65-3.77). There was no evidence of an association after risk adjustment (adjusted OR: 1.16, 95% CI: 0.94-1.43) or after propensity score analysis (weighted OR: 0.94, 95% CI: 0.69-1.27). For patients at high risk with a predicted mortality ≥5%, the proportion of patients with a direct transfer to critical care varied widely amongst hospitals (interquartile range 68%-92%; median 83%). Our findings suggest that apparent higher postoperative mortality in patients having direct transfer to critical care can be mostly explained by characteristics of patients, tumours, physiology and surgery. However, the extent to which direct transfer to critical care is used varies widely amongst hospitals. Further work to understand this variation has the potential to improve patient outcomes after emergency colorectal cancer resection.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a major clinical challenge due to the persistence of epithelial cell adhesion molecule (EpCAM) positive (+) cancer stem cells (CSCs), which drive tumour relapse, metastasis, and immune evasion. This review highlights a modular nanomedicine construct, EpAb2‑6‑AuNPs‑PPBa, designed for targeted photodynamic therapy (PDT) in CRC. By integrating EpCAM‑specific antibodies (EpAb2‑6), gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) synthesised through plant extracts, and photosensitiser (PS) such as pheophorbide‑a (PPBa). Upon near‑infrared activation, PPBa generates reactive oxygen species (ROS), inducing immunogenic cell death (ICD) characterised by calreticulin exposure, ATP release, and HMGB1 secretion. The system also incorporates surface‑enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) tags for real‑time imaging and circulating tumour cell (CTC) capture. Green synthesis provides biocompatibility and scalability, and antibody guidance enhances tumour specificity. By critically evaluating antibody selection, AuNPs synthesis strategies, and photosensitiser performance, this review situates EpAb2‑6‑AuNPs‑PPBa within the broader perspective of CRC nanotheranostics. Although rigorous in vivo validation and translational studies are necessary, the construct exemplifies a sustainable, multifunctional approach to precision oncology.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Inflammatory bowel disease‑associated colorectal cancer (IBD‑CRC) arises in the setting of long‑standing chronic intestinal inflammation, in which immune dysregulation cannot be readily attributed to the dominance of a single inhibitory pathway or to global immunosuppression. Persistent inflammatory signaling sustains a state of prolonged immune engagement, yet with constrained effector output, potentially compromising antitumor immune surveillance and limiting the clinical benefit of immunotherapy. The present review synthetises the accumulated knowledge on the long‑term immunological alterations induced by chronic inflammation, including the integration of immune signaling, shifts in activation thresholds, metabolic reprogramming, and functional polarization of immune cells. These changes are discussed in the context of both tumor initiation and tumor maintenance to delineate the immunological evolution of IBD‑CRC. The review further examines the relationship between inflammation‑induced response constraints and the limited efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors, and summarizes the mechanistic barriers to immunotherapy in IBD‑CRC. Collectively, these observations suggest that relieving inhibition through a single target may be insufficient to restore effective antitumor immunity. Finally, the potential value of natural plant‑derived interventions characterized by multi‑component, low‑intensity, and long‑term modulation is discussed, particularly with respect to reducing inflammatory burden and improving immune metabolic states, thereby providing a conceptual basis for the development of combination immunotherapeutic strategies.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Pituitary metastases are uncommon, and most cases originate from breast or lung cancer. Tumor-to-tumor metastasis, in which one neoplasm metastasizes into another, is particularly rare in the sellar region. We report a 66-year-old man with metastatic sigmoid colon adenocarcinoma treated with modified FOLFOX6 (5-fluorouracil, L-leucovorin, and oxaliplatin) plus panitumumab; extracranial disease was controlled, whereas a sellar mass initially suspected as a pituitary adenoma slowly enlarged over 2 years. Endocrine testing showed anterior hypopituitarism without arginine vasopressin deficiency. Endoscopic transsphenoidal surgery was performed for continued enlargement and diagnostic uncertainty. Histopathology demonstrated a gonadotroph pituitary adenoma infiltrated by colorectal adenocarcinoma, with extensive intermingling of the 2 components rather than discrete nests, favoring tumor-to-tumor metastasis over a collision tumor. The metastatic component consisted of viable tumor cells without necrosis or convincing treatment effect despite prolonged chemotherapy. This case underscores that metastatic tumor within a pituitary adenoma may enlarge despite favorable systemic therapy outcomes. Metastasis should therefore remain a key differential diagnosis for a sellar mass radiologically suggestive of a pituitary adenoma.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Long-standing cooperative oncology groups are uniquely positioned to generate high-quality real-world data in diverse tumor types. The Hellenic Cooperative Oncology Group (HeCOG), a nonprofit scientific organization, has established a multi-institutional clinical database and biobank to support translational cancer research and precision oncology initiatives. Our aim was to describe the structure, governance and operation of HeCOG Biobank and patient registry. The HeCOG clinical database is a centralized, web-based platform that supports interventional, observational, real-world and translational studies across affiliated institutions. Clinical data are linked to biospecimens stored in the HeCOG Biobank, preserved at the Laboratory of Molecular Oncology. Biospecimen collection, processing, storage, and data handling are governed by standardized operating procedures. To date, the registry includes >54 000 patients with diverse tumors, enrolled retrospectively and prospectively. The associated biobank comprises >17 000 formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tumor tissue samples and >6000 blood-derived specimens. The largest tissue collections are from breast, colorectal, and lung cancer. Molecular and histopathological biomarker data are also available for several thousand patients within the registry. Biospecimens are uniquely coded and linked to pseudonymized longitudinal clinical, histopathological, and molecular data. Ongoing expansion includes digital pathology and radiological imaging datasets, further enhancing the translational potential of the resource. The HeCOG Biobank and the accompanying clinical database have evolved into a valuable resource for translational cancer research in Greece. Through the ongoing integration of digital pathology, imaging data, and artificial intelligence-based approaches it provides a strong basis for precision oncology and collaborative national and international research.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Treatment of depression in patients with cancer requires individualized decision-making considering physical symptoms, drug interactions, adverse effects, treatment burden, and acceptability. We report a patient with persistent depression after colorectal cancer treatment, in whom pharmacotherapy was constrained by insufficient efficacy and tolerability, improvement with modified electroconvulsive therapy (mECT) was temporary, and reintroduction of mECT was difficult. She subsequently received repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS). A woman in her 60s developed depression after emergency surgery for lower gastrointestinal perforation caused by descending colon cancer and later developed chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) after postoperative chemotherapy. Pharmacotherapy produced insufficient improvement. Although 10 mECT sessions led to improvement, symptoms recurred after discharge. Reintroduction of mECT was not possible because of strong fear of the treatment and general anesthesia. She was referred to our hospital and received 27 rTMS sessions without changes in psychotropic medication. Her 17-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale and Clinical Global Impressions-Severity (CGI-S) scores improved from 19 to 8 and from 4 to 1, respectively, whereas the pain Numerical Rating Scale score remained 8. Behavior and daily functioning also improved. Six months after treatment, limb discomfort persisted, but she could still perform household chores and go out. The referring physician rated the CGI-S score as 1. When pharmacotherapy for depression after cancer treatment is constrained by insufficient efficacy or tolerability, and the benefit of mECT is transient or its reintroduction is difficult, rTMS may be considered as a treatment option.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Xanthine dehydrogenase (XDH) is involved in the progression of various cancer. This study aimed to investigate its potential in colorectal cancer (CRC). Gene expression was determined using RT-qPCR, Western blot, immunohistochemistry, and immunofluorescence. Cell behaviors were analyzed using CCK-8, colony formation, wound healing, transwell migration, TUNEL, PI staining. In vivo assay was conducted to verify the role of XDH in CRC. Histological analysis was performed using HE staining. We found that XDH was downregulated in CRC. XDH overexpression suppressed proliferation and aggressiveness of CRC cells, whereas XDH knockdown exerted opposite effects. XDH selectively increased purine metabolites and promoted impairment of mitochondrial metabolism. Mechanistically, XDH activated NCOA4-dependent ferritinophagy signaling and drove CRC cells to ferroptosis, which was reversed by 3-MA. Taken together, XDH inhibits the progression of CRC via mediating ferritinophagy and ferroptosis. Therefore, XDH/ferritinophagy may be a potential target for CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
In the personalized management of stage II colorectal cancer (CRC), traditional TNM (Tumor, Node, Metastasis) staging has limited ability to accurately stratify the risk of postoperative recurrence. Consequently, oncologists frequently face a major therapeutic dilemma when determining the use of adjuvant chemotherapy in these patients. Although tumor budding (TB) has been incorporated into international clinical guidelines as an independent prognostic marker associated with invasive potential, the conventional International Tumor Budding Consensus Conference classification system is primarily based on routine hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining. Furthermore, this framework classifies tumors with 0-4 buds into a single low-risk category termed Bd1. This classification may obscure important biological differences between tumors with complete absence of cellular dissociation and those already showing early invasive activity. This review proposes separate diagnostic recognition of the 'zero-budding' (Bd0) category. Recent large-scale cohort studies and retrospective analyses support that Bd0 status, particularly when confirmed by pan-cytokeratin immunohistochemistry, is associated with an extremely high negative predictive value for postoperative recurrence. At the subcellular level, the Bd0 category may reflect sustained suppression of the epithelial-mesenchymal transition process. Mechanistically, this relatively non-invasive category may be maintained by preservation of the EBP50 scaffold, which stabilizes the membranous E-cadherin/beta-catenin complex and suppresses nuclear translocation of Wnt/beta-catenin. Bd0 is also strongly associated with the deficient mismatch repair microenvironment, in which high tumor mutational burden may promote enhanced CD8

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colonoscopy is central to colorectal cancer prevention and early detection, yet Australia lacks a national mechanism to aggregate and benchmark colonoscopy quality data. The Colonoscopy Clinical Care Standard establishes local monitoring of key quality indicators, which can identify service-level problems, but cannot show whether variation is isolated, systemic, improving over time or concentrated in particular settings. This creates a national blind spot in one of the country's most common cancer-prevention procedures. Current arrangements remain fragmented across health services and do not support consistent national oversight. Since colonoscopy registry development was previously deprioritised in 2016, the Australian context has changed substantially: a national clinical care standard is now in place, cross-college governance of colonoscopy recertification has matured, endoscopy reporting software has improved structured data capture and broader national clinical quality registry frameworks now support more coordinated registry development. A national colonoscopy clinical quality registry could build on existing local data collection, and support coordinated national quality assurance by enabling confidential benchmarking, identifying unwarranted variation, strengthening clinical governance, and informing accreditation, training and service improvement.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Segment Anything Model (SAM), a prompt-guided foundation model, exhibits substantial potential for medical image segmentation by incorporating prior knowledge through user-defined prompts. However, the application of SAM in radiotherapy target delineation remains limited. This study proposes a feasible prompt-guided interactive delineation workflow driven by an optimized SAM. A total of 100 rectal cancer neoadjuvant radiotherapy cases were collected (60 for training and 40 for testing). This study utilized bounding-box prompts to guide SAM for GTV segmentation. Physicians manually draw box prompts on certain slices, while box prompts for the remaining slices are automatically generated using an interpolation strategy. Four fine-tuning strategies for SAM training were evaluated, and the impact of prompt numbers and placements was assessed as well. The performance of the finalized workflow with optimized SAM was compared with five state-of-the-art (SOTA) models, and its robustness to prompt variations in middle-slice selection and box-prompt margins was analyzed. Compared to other fine-tuning methods, freezing the image encoder obtained the most stable performance. Prompts on only 3 slices achieved accuracy comparable to prompts on all slices. The placement of the middle-slice prompt exhibited negligible impact (p > 0.05). The finalized SAM-driven workflow outperformed end-to-end baseline models both visually and quantitatively (3D DSC: 0.92 vs 0.80; 3D HD95: 2.73 vs 12.70; IoU: 0.86 vs 0.67; Sensitivity: 91.20% vs 85.98%; Precision: 93.65% vs 79.23%), while maintaining stable performance across certain prompt variations. The proposed SAM-driven interactive workflow with as few as 3 box prompts achieves favorable accuracy of GTV segmentation for rectal cancer neoadjuvant radiotherapy.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Portal vein embolization (PVE) is routinely used before major hepatectomy to induce hypertrophy of the future liver remnant (FLR) and reduce post-hepatectomy liver failure. Conventional PVE relies on permanent embolic agents, resulting in irreversible portal occlusion, which may be associated with complications and may limit subsequent therapeutic options in patients who do not ultimately undergo resection. Whether transient portal deprivation alone can induce clinically relevant liver regeneration remains unknown. We evaluated the efficacy and safety of temporary selective PVE using an absorbable gelatin agent. EMBORES was a multicenter prospective single-arm phase II trial conducted in six French hepatobiliary centers. Between May 3, 2018, and May 3, 2021, adult patients requiring major hepatectomy and preoperative PVE were included. Selective portal branches were embolized using powdered absorbable gelatin sponge. The primary endpoint was FLR hypertrophy assessed by computed tomography (CT) volumetry 4-6 weeks after PVE. Secondary endpoints included feasibility, morbidity, portal vein recanalization, and surgical outcomes. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT02945059. 34 patients were enrolled and 32 underwent temporary PVE. Mean age was 63.4 years (standard deviation [SD] 8.9), and colorectal liver metastases accounted for 18 (56%) of 32 indications. Technical success was achieved in all patients. One major complication occurred (1 [3.1%] of 32 patients), while liver function remained preserved. Complete and partial portal vein recanalization were observed in 17 (53%) and 9 (28%) of 32 patients, respectively. Mean FLR volume increased from 580 (SD 169) mL to 690 (SD 188) mL, corresponding to a mean hypertrophy ratio of 9.5% (SD 10.2). Five patients required repeat embolization using a permanent agent because of insufficient hypertrophy. Overall, 23 (71.8%) of 32 patients underwent major hepatectomy, with no postoperative mortality. Temporary PVE using an absorbable embolic agent is feasible, safe, and capable of inducing clinically meaningful liver hypertrophy before major hepatectomy, supporting the concept that transient portal vein occlusion may be sufficient to stimulate liver regeneration in selected patients. The EMBORES study was funded by the French Ministry of Health through a national hospital clinical research program grant awarded in 2015 (Programme Hospitalier de Recherche Clinique National, PHRC-15-15-0201).

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Endoscopy remains the most common modality by which screen-eligible adults are up-to-date with colorectal (CRC) screening. For the Area-Level Estimates of Cancer Screening (ALECS) study, we leveraged multi-payor claims data to generate small-area estimates of the prevalence of being up-to-date with colorectal cancer (CRC) screening among continuously insured screen-eligible adults in North Carolina (NC). First, we created bespoke small areas at the intersection of counties and ZIP codes, which enabled linkages with aggregated claims data using patients' residential ZIP codes and counties. Using a 10-year lookback period, we then defined the cohort as near-continuously insured screen-eligible adults age 50-74, who did not have a prior diagnosis of CRC or a total colectomy as of December 2020. Statewide, from 2012 to 2020, 79.8-81.2% of continuously insured screen-eligible adults aged 50-75 were up-to-date (UTD) on CRC screening. In 2020, at the small area level, the mean prevalence of being UTD with CRC screening was 79.6% (Standard Deviation: 9.5). Diagnostic tests of an Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) model indicated a significant degree of spatial dependence of the error terms (I = 0.1540; p<.00001), suggesting the need for spatial models. We thus fit a Conditional Autoregressive (CAR) Bayesian generalized linear model with a logistic link function and Leroux priors, accounting for spatial autocorrelation, and found an inverse association between the minimum distance to access an endoscopy facility and the prevalence of being up to date with CRC screening among continuously insured screen-eligible adults across NC (Point Estimate: - 0.0645; Credible Interval: - 0.1156 - 0.0103).

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Crohn's disease (CD) is rapidly emerging in Asia, yet endoscopic and histopathological characteristics at diagnosis remain poorly described in Southeast Asia. We aimed to describe baseline endoscopic and histologic features in Vietnamese adults with newly diagnosed CD. We conducted a descriptive cross-sectional study of consecutive adults newly diagnosed with CD from June 2019 to June 2024 at a tertiary inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) center in Vietnam. Ileocolonoscopy with segmental biopsies was performed in all patients. Endoscopic findings, histopathology, and Montreal classification were systematically recorded. Eighty patients (median age 34.5 years, 62.5% male) were included. The median time from symptom onset to diagnosis was 12 months (IQR 2-24); 78.8% had ≥ 1 prior inconclusive colonoscopy, and 25% had undergone intestinal resection before confirmed diagnosis. Ileocolonic disease (L3) predominated (71.3%). At diagnosis, 28.8% of patients had stricturing and 28.8% had penetrating disease behavior. Endoscopically, terminal ileal involvement was observed in 77.6%, cecal involvement in 56.6%, and skip lesions in 72.4%. Aphthous ulcers were seen in 13.2%, longitudinal ulcers in 14.5%, and cobblestoning in 6.6%. Luminal narrowing and fistulous openings were seen in 32.9% and 5.3%, respectively. The overall endoscopic impression was consistent with CD in 46.1%, non-specific in 35.5%, suggestive of colorectal cancer (CRC) in 13.2%, and suggestive of intestinal tuberculosis in 3.9%. Histologically, chronic inflammation was universal and non-caseating epithelioid granulomas were identified in 31.6%. The pathologist's conclusion was consistent with CD in 67.1% and non-specific in 30.4%. In this tertiary-center cohort of Vietnamese adults with newly diagnosed CD, the median time from symptom onset to diagnosis was 12 months. At diagnosis, 57.5% had stricturing or penetrating behavior, and 25.0% had already undergone intestinal resection. Longitudinal ulcers, cobblestoning, and epithelioid granulomas were each found in a minority of patients, and histopathology was nonspecific in 30.4%. These descriptive data provide a baseline for future comparative studies and for evaluating standardized diagnostic criteria in Vietnam.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Background The spatial organization of cellular lineages within the tumor microenvironment governs disease progression and therapeutic response, but multiplexed spatial profiling remains costly, technically complex, and tissue-destructive. Routine hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) histopathology is inexpensive and widely available but lacks explicit molecular information. This study aims to determine whether single-cell, biomarker-informed cellular states can be inferred directly from H&E images to enable scalable, non-destructive spatial biology across cancer types and clinical endpoints. Methods We present CellPlexer, a deep learning framework trained on more than 36 million co-registered cells from paired H&E and multiplex immunofluorescence images to jointly segment nuclei and classify each cell into one of 15 hierarchically defined biomarker states. A spatially aware transformer integrates single-cell embeddings with patch-level histomorphology through attention-based multimodal fusion, generating a multi-scale whole-slide representation for clinical prediction. We validated CellPlexer across four independent cohorts spanning lung, breast, and colorectal cancer. Results Here we show that CellPlexer consistently outperformed morphology-only baselines across recurrence, treatment response, survival, and mutation prediction tasks, achieving an AUC of 72.19% for pathological complete response prediction in triple-negative breast cancer (75.06% with clinical variable integration) and 83.09% for BRAF mutation prediction in colorectal cancer. Conclusions These results demonstrate that morphologically inferred, single-cell biomarker states capture clinically and biologically meaningful tumor microenvironment organization, providing a scalable, non-destructive framework for extracting proteomic-level insights from widely available clinical histopathology archives.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Current recommendations limit the use of menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) principally to the management of menopausal symptoms, largely because of concerns regarding increased breast cancer (BC) risk. The impact of MHT use on systemic biological aging and blood methylome and its overlap with that of menopause timing remains incompletely understood. In females (N=78,209) of the Prostate, Lung, Colorectal and Ovarian (PLCO) Cancer Screening Trial, we used Cox models to assess the associations of menopause timing (ordinal age at menopause; binary early-M [<45 years] vs non-early-M [≥45 years]) and MHT use with BC incidence, mortality, and survival. In a nested case-control subset with blood DNA methylome (DNAm; 758 cases, 745 controls), we related both exposures to epigenetic clocks and DNAm-based telomere length (DNAmTL) and used polygenic instruments to test both causal directions. Ever MHT use was associated with higher BC incidence (aHR 1.17, 95% CI 1.10-1.24), particularly for hormone-receptor positive (HR+) subtypes (1.19, 1.11-1.27), whereas early-M was associated with lower HR+ incidence (0.88, 0.81-0.96) but not with overall incidence after adjustment (0.94, 0.88-1.01). However, ever MHT use was associated with lower BC mortality (0.72, 0.62-0.83) and better overall survival (0.87, 0.81-0.95). In the DNAm subset, non-early-M was associated with slower epigenetic aging and longer DNAmTL particularly in cases. Higher cumulative aging and pace-of-aging markers predicted worse survival and partially mediated the early-M associations. Genetic analyses supported shared polygenic architecture between menopause timing and DNAm aging biomarkers rather than simple causation. MHT showed no broad epigenetic age acceleration and its profound methylome and immune-marker signatures largely did not overlap with those of menopause timing. Ever MHT use was associated with lower BC mortality and better overall survival despite higher BC incidence. Systemic aging detected more than a decade after menopausal transition correlates with early menopause. MHT use shows molecular signatures distinct to those seen for menopause timing.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Sporadic colorectal cancers (CRCs) form following initiating APC mutations, inducing constitutive β-catenin/TCF signaling. Similarly, the guanylyl cyclase C (GUCY2C) tumor suppressor axis is universally silenced in CRC. While the GUCY2C receptor is retained, loss of its paracrine hormones guanylin (GUCA2A) and uroguanylin (GUCA2B) is among the earliest events in transformation. Mutant APC/β-catenin/TCF signaling driving CRC transcriptionally silences GUCY2C hormone expression while suppressing that oncogenic pathway reconstitutes hormone production opposing tumorigenesis. p38α opposes tumor initiation, and its loss promotes transformation in chemical and genetic mouse models of CRC. In healthy intestine, p38α supports a gradient of epithelial differentiation along the crypt-surface axis. Here, we reveal that p38α links regulation of oncogenic APC/β-catenin/TCF signaling and GUCY2C hormone expression. Regulation of p38α by APC/β-catenin/TCF signaling was defined in four genetically engineered human CRC cell lines with conditional oncogenic APC/β-catenin/TCF signaling and healthy human colon organoids. Expression of p38α was eliminated from conditional human CRC cell lines by pharmacological inhibition, RNA knockdown, and CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing. Transcriptomic analysis of these cells by RNA sequencing defined the set of genes regulated by APC/β-catenin/TCF signaling controlled through p38α. In CRC cell lines, APC/β-catenin/TCF signaling suppressed p38α phosphorylation and activity, whereas inhibition of APC/β-catenin/TCF restored p38α signaling. In the absence of APC/β-catenin/TCF signaling, inhibiting p38α repressed GUCY2C hormone expression. Inhibiting APC/β-catenin/TCF signaling enriched phosphorylated p38α at the GUCA2A promoter. In that context, analysis of the CPTAC proteomic database revealed that phosphorylation of p38α and its upstream kinases MKK3 and MKK4 was reduced in human CRC. Finally, transcriptomic analysis revealed that p38α is a critical signaling node controlling the expression of a substantial subset of APC/β-catenin/TCF-regulated genes in human CRC cells and patient tumors. APC/β-catenin/TCF signaling inhibits p38α phosphorylation and transcriptional activity, suppressing GUCA2A and GUCA2B expression and functionally silencing the retained GUCY2C receptor. These findings identify p38α as a signaling intermediary integrating oncogenic APC/β-catenin/TCF activity to extinction of the GUCY2C tumor-suppressor axis and reveal a broader p38α-dependent component of the APC/β-catenin/TCF-regulated transcriptome.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Multimodality (physical, dietary, psychological) prehabilitation is associated with a disease-free survival advantage after colorectal cancer surgery; however, the underlying mechanism is unknown. We measured the effects of a western-style diet on gut dysbiosis, antitumor immunity, and cancer progression in a surgical mouse model of metastatic colorectal cancer and attempted to mitigate its effects with isolated dietary prehabilitation. Before surgery and tumor induction, mice were given either a western-style diet for 6 weeks, chow for 6 weeks, or 4 weeks of a western-style diet followed by 2 weeks of chow. Expelled stool was collected for analysis of the fecal microbiome. Four weeks after surgery, tumors were quantified and collected for analysis with an immunofluorescence panel. The western-style diet was obesogenic. Fecal microbiome analysis illustrated that the western diet induced a severe and lasting dysbiosis as measured by alpha diversity metrics, pathogenic overgrowth and Firmicutes to Bacteroidetes ratio, which was partially rescued by prehabilitation. Mice fed the western diet demonstrated increased tumor bulk and decreased intratumoral immune cell infiltrate compared with chow-fed mice. prehabilitation rescued the intratumoral immune effects, but not tumor bulk. An obesogenic, no fiber western-style diet increased gut dysbiosis and tumor bulk while decreasing antitumor immunity in our mouse model, which was partially rescued by prehabilitation. Microbiome-targeted prehabilitation for colorectal cancer surgery is a promising paradigm and further translational research is warranted.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Systemic inflammation drives cancer progression. We investigated the clinical utility of five routine complete blood count (CBC)-derived inflammatory biomarkers, neutrophil-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), monocyte-lymphocyte ratio (MLR), systemic inflammation response index (SIRI), and systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), in colorectal cancer (CRC) patients. We performed head-to-head case-control and prognostic analyses of five indices in 2305 CRC patients and 78,281 health‑screening controls, with replication in 1031 CRC patients. Analyses included propensity score matching, Cox regression, restricted cubic splines, and Harrell's concordance index. Population reference intervals were derived, and cross‑population transferability was assessed using the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES). All indices were elevated in CRC patients and independently associated with survival. MLR retained diagnostic and prognostic significance in Stage I disease and was replicated. Dose-response trends were observed across quartiles, with non‑linear threshold effects for MLR and SIRI. Incremental prognostic gains beyond stage were modest. Reference intervals showed substantial overlap between CRC and healthy populations, limiting screening utility. NHANES comparison revealed non‑uniform transferability. CBC‑derived indices demonstrated reproducible diagnostic and prognostic relevance, with MLR particularly informative in early‑stage CRC. Reference intervals contextualise abnormality but should not be interpreted as CRC screening or treatment thresholds.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
An iodinated hydrophobic oil containing the 2,3,5-triiodobenzoate moiety was encapsulated in biodegradable poly(lactic acid)-based polymer particles using a solvent emulsion-evaporation technique that provided control over particle size. The hydrophobic iodinated oil served a dual function as radiopaque contrast agent for particle quantification using dual-energy x-ray computed tomography (DECT) imaging and furthermore as solvent for the chemotherapeutic drug paclitaxel (PTX), establishing a novel theranostic system. Release kinetics of PTX was studied in fetal bovine serum over seven days demonstrating sustainable drug release over the entire period, with cumulative release mainly depending on particle diameter. Intraperitoneal administration of a therapeutic dosage of radiopaque spheres in mice provided sufficient iodine contrast to track biodistribution and clearance over 18 days. Importantly, imaging showed unexpected particle aggregation in vivo with about 50% clearance over 18 days, emphasizing the value of real-time distribution assessment as a complementary method to conventional ex-vivo histology. A proof of concept of longitudinal dual imaging using single-photon emission CT (SPECT)/DECT was demonstrated in a mouse model of colorectal cancer with intraperitoneal metastases following a single intraperitoneal dose of PTX or PTX-loaded particles. Treatment response was monitored using SPECT, while particle distribution was tracked by DECT. This theranostic approach integrates controlled intraperitoneal drug delivery with non-invasive quantitative DECT-based imaging and may improve treatment precision and therapeutic outcomes.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The modern management of locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC) involves sequential radiotherapy and chemotherapy, termed Total Neoadjuvant Therapy (TNT). Although TNT significantly improves tumour regression and achieves complete response rates of approximately 30 %, treatment efficacy remains limited in part by tumour-intrinsic resistance to apoptosis. We therefore sought to investigate the effects of radiotherapy on TNFα-associated apoptotic signalling in rectal cancer and evaluate whether inhibition of Inhibitor of Apoptosis Proteins (IAPs) could enhance treatment response. Transcriptomic profiling was performed on rectal tumour biopsies obtained before and after two weeks of neoadjuvant radiotherapy (n = 42). Gene Set Enrichment Analysis was used to identify pathways altered following radiotherapy. The clinically relevant IAP antagonist, tolinapant, was evaluated in rectal cancer models to assess effects on cIAP1/2 degradation, radiation- and chemotherapy-induced apoptosis, and formation of 5-fluorouracil (5FU)-induced drug-tolerant persister (DTP) cells. Mechanistic studies were performed in the presence of TNFα, and in vivo efficacy was assessed in SW837 xenograft models. Radiotherapy induced robust upregulation of TNFα/TNFR1 signalling and apoptosis-associated gene sets. Gene Set Enrichment Analysis confirmed enrichment of both "TNFα signalling via NFκB" and "Apoptosis" pathways. Upregulation of TNF, TNFRSF1A, RIPK1, TRADD, and CFLAR (FLIP) was observed alongside downregulation of DIABLO, suggesting that radiotherapy primes tumours for TNFα-mediated apoptosis but that elevated antiapoptotic signalling may suppress this response. Tolinapant degraded cIAP1/2 and significantly enhanced radiation-induced apoptosis in rectal cancer models. Co-treatment with TNFα further amplified apoptosis through a caspase-8-dependent mechanism. The combination of tolinapant and radiation was well-tolerated in vivo and reduced SW837 xenograft tumour volume compared to radiation alone; however, this difference did not meet statistical significance. Tolinapant also potentiated chemotherapy-induced apoptosis and prevented the emergence of 5FU-induced DTP rectal cancer cells. These findings identify TNFα-associated apoptotic signalling as a potential radiation-induced vulnerability in rectal cancer and provide a mechanistic rationale for combining radiotherapy with IAP antagonists. Tolinapant also enhanced apoptosis induced by chemotherapy whilst suppressing drug-tolerant persisters, supporting further investigation of IAP antagonism as a strategy to improve TNT efficacy in the neoadjuvant management of rectal cancer.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Trifluridine-tipiracil (FTD-TPI) plus bevacizumab is the standard treatment for refractory metastatic colorectal cancer. However, the conventional schedule is frequently associated with haematological and gastrointestinal toxicity, which is clinically significant and relevant to patients. A simplified 14-day schedule has been proposed to reduce toxicity, but whether this treatment preserves survival has not been established in a randomised trial. We therefore aimed to assess whether the 14-day schedule is non-inferior to the conventional schedule for overall survival. PRABITAS was a pragmatic, multicentre, open-label, randomised, phase 3, non-inferiority trial conducted in 178 hospitals in Japan. Patients with refractory metastatic colorectal cancer were randomly assigned (1:1) using a minimisation algorithm, stratified by Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status, RAS mutational status, and institution, to FTD-TPI (35 mg/m Between Dec 26, 2023, and May 20, 2025, we randomly assigned 972 patients, of whom 970 (99%) constituted the intention-to-treat population after two were excluded because they were randomly assigned before site approval (486 [50%] to the 28-day treatment group, 292 [60%] men and 194 [40%] women]; and 484 [50%] to the 14-day treatment group, 264 [55%] men and 220 [45%] women). Median follow-up was 17·9 months (IQR 14·3-22·6). Median overall survival was 10·3 months (95% CI 9·5-11·6) in the 28-day group and 11·3 months (10·2-12·5) in the 14-day group (stratified hazard ratio 0·93 [95% CI 0·80-1·08]). The 12-month overall survival rates were 44·0% (95% CI 39·5-48·5) in the 28-day group and 47·5% (42·9-52·0) in the 14-day group. Neutropenia grade 3 or worse was reduced in the 14-day group (13% vs 39%; absolute difference 25 percentage points [95% CI 20-31]), as was anorexia grade 2 or worse (15% vs 26%; absolute difference 11 percentage points [6-16]). Two treatment-related deaths occurred in the 14-day group and none in the 28-day group. A 14-day schedule of FTD-TPI plus bevacizumab was non-inferior to the conventional 28-day schedule for overall survival, while reducing haematological and gastrointestinal toxicity. These findings support this simplified schedule as the new standard for FTD-TPI plus bevacizumab in refractory metastatic colorectal cancer. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Fruquintinib is a standard later-line treatment for advanced colorectal cancer (aCRC) after oxaliplatin- and irinotecan-based chemotherapy. Prospective studies of fruquintinib-based programmed cell death protein-1 (PD-1) inhibitor strategies in aCRC reported as mismatch repair-proficient (pMMR) or microsatellite-stable (MSS) have yielded heterogeneous outcomes. We summarized observed survival and response outcomes using reconstructed individual-level records. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and CENTRAL were searched from inception through January 26, 2026. Published Kaplan-Meier curves were digitized and converted to reconstructed individual-level time-to-event records with IPDfromKM in R. Merged Kaplan-Meier curves were treated as patient-weighted descriptive composites. Objective response rate (ORR) and disease control rate (DCR) were synthesized with random-effects models. Sensitivity analyzes excluded the prospective observational study and restricted the evidence to pharmacologic fruquintinib plus PD-1 doublets. Five prospective studies enrolled 150 patients; 147 contributed to reconstructed overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) analyzes. Median OS and PFS were 11.7 and 5.4 months, respectively. Reconstructed duration of response included 14 responders from three studies and had a median of 8.8 months. In the aggregate response dataset (149 observations), ORR was 19% and DCR was 82%. In the doublet-only sensitivity analysis, median OS and PFS were 14.8 and 6.9 months, respectively. These results descriptively summarize small, heterogeneous, uncontrolled studies and do not estimate a common treatment effect or the added benefit of PD-1 blockade. The overall composite should not be used as a uniform doublet benchmark or as the sole basis for clinical decisions or trial sizing.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Older adults with colorectal cancer (CRC) are at higher risk for cerebrovascular diseases (CeVD) due to shared risk factors and treatment effects. Despite CeVD being a leading global cause of death, its mortality burden in older CRC patients in the US remains underexplored. We analyzed CDC WONDER multiple-cause-of-death records from 1999 through 2020 for US decedents aged ≥65 years. CeVD (ICD-10 I60-I69) was the underlying cause of death and CRC (C18-C20) was a multiple or contributing cause. We calculated age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) overall and by sex, race and ethnicity, region, and urbanization; age-specific analyses used crude mortality rates. Joinpoint regression estimated annual percent changes (APCs) and average annual percent changes (AAPCs). We identified 10,185 CeVD-related deaths involving CRC. The AAMR declined from 2.06 per 100,000 in 1999 to 0.67 in 2020 (AAPC, -5.95%; 95% CI, -6.52% to -5.46%; P < 0.000001). Men had a higher AAMR than women (1.31 vs 0.99); mortality declined in both groups (AAPC, -6.33% and -5.67%, respectively; both P < 0.000001). AAMRs were 1.21 in non-Hispanic Black and 1.17 in non-Hispanic White individuals (AAPC, -6.59% and -5.75%; both P < 0.000001). Non-metropolitan areas had a higher AAMR than metropolitan areas (1.33 vs 1.07; AAPC, -4.80% vs -6.25%; both P < 0.000001). Adults aged ≥85 years had the highest crude rate (4.21); AAPCs for ages 65-74, 75-84, and ≥85 years were -5.70%, -7.05%, and -5.65%, respectively (all P < 0.000001). CeVD-related mortality involving CRC among US adults aged ≥65 years declined from 1999 to 2020, although higher population-level rates persisted among men, non-Hispanic Black individuals, non-metropolitan residents, and residents of the Midwest.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Although widely used in chemotherapeutic treatments, platinum (Pt)-based drugs -namely cisplatin (Cis), oxaliplatin (Ox), and carboplatin- encounter several drawbacks that significantly limit their clinically applicable doses, such as the development of various side effects. These toxicities, including nephrotoxicity and neurotoxicity associated with Cis and Ox, respectively, arise from the lack of selectivity of these drugs toward cancer cells. While numerous alternative treatments -some employing a Pt(IV) prodrug strategy- have been investigated in preclinical settings for their anticancer activity, studies evaluating their systemic toxicities remain scarce. However, assessing these toxicities is crucial for the development of improved therapies. This study aimed to evaluate the systemic toxicities induced by PtC5Mn, a novel Pt(IV)-Mn(II) prodrug reported to exhibit anticancer activity in both in vitro and in vivo models of colorectal cancer, as well as Mn1C5, its corresponding Mn(II) complex that mimics superoxide dismutase (SOD) activity, in combination with Ox. Additionally, their potential protective effects against Ox-induced peripheral neuropathy were explored through behavioral studies and mapping of Pt localization in sciatic nerves sections by Synchrotron-based Scanning X-Ray Fluorescence microscopy. Our results support the use of Pt(IV) prodrugs and redox modulation by SOD mimics for the mitigation of oxaliplatin-associated off-target effects.

Restorative colorectal surgery after emergency stoma formation is challenging because of adhesions, altered anatomy, and pelvic dissection. Fecal incontinence is defined as the involuntary or inappropriate passage of liquid or solid stool. It is a distressing condition, resulting in both physical and psychological problems that affect quality of life. The objective of this study is to assess the effectiveness of medially based gluteus maximus muscle flap in the control of anal incontinence and compare it with other methods of gluteus maximus flap. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Recent advances in direct rat sarcoma (RAS) inhibition and downstream pathway targeting have created novel therapeutic strategies which can be utilized in gynecologic oncology. This review examines RAS biology, lessons learned from other malignancies, and emerging strategies for gynecological malignancies. KRAS G12C inhibitors in lung cancer established the clinical feasibility of direct RAS targeting, while colorectal cancer studies demonstrated the importance of lineage-specific combinations. KRAS G12D inhibitors, targeted protein degraders, and multiselective RAS(ON) inhibitors represent the next frontier in RAS inhibition, expanding therapeutic options across both gynecologic and nongynecologic tumors. In recurrent low-grade serous ovarian cancer, therapeutic advances have centered on inhibiting the downstream RAS-mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase (MEK)-extracellular signal-regulated kinase signaling pathway using MEK or combined RAF/MEK and focal adhesion kinase inhibitors, rather than direct RAS inhibition, demonstrating encouraging clinical responses, leading to accelerated approval for KRAS-mutant disease. RAS-pathway directed therapy requires consideration of tumor lineage, specific alleles, and functional pathway dependence. Although clinical progress in gynecologic oncology is most relevant in low-grade serous ovarian cancer, emerging non-G12C therapies warrant further evaluation across gynecologic malignancies. Novel combinations and integrated biomarkers will be necessary to improve patient selection and overcome therapeutic resistance.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Iron deficiency anemia may signal underlying gastrointestinal pathology in adults. This study aimed to evaluate endoscopic and histopathological findings in adults undergoing upper gastrointestinal endoscopy and colonoscopy for iron deficiency anemia and to compare selected lesion frequencies between age groups. This retrospective study included 328 adult patients who underwent upper gastrointestinal endoscopy for iron deficiency anemia between January 2024 and December 2025; 285 also underwent colonoscopy. The mean age was 61.2 ± 14.8 years, and 62.5% of patients were male; 64.3% were older than 50 years. Pangastritis (30.5%) and antral gastritis (23.8%) were the most common upper gastrointestinal findings. Among biopsied patients, Helicobacter pylori positivity was 54.2%, intestinal metaplasia 14.6%, and atrophic gastritis 7.5%. On colonoscopy, hemorrhoids were most common (32.3%), followed by colonic polyps (24.6%); colorectal adenocarcinoma was found in eight patients (2.8%), all older than 50 years. Tubular adenoma with low-grade dysplasia was the most frequent polyp histopathology. Gastric polyps (P = 0.013) and colonic polyps (P = 0.041), which were not uniformly subclassified histologically, were significantly more frequent after age 50, whereas intestinal metaplasia (P = 0.051) and colorectal cancer (8/190 vs. 0/95; P = 0.055) did not differ significantly between age groups. In this descriptive, single-group cohort, bidirectional endoscopy identified premalignant and malignant lesions in adults with iron deficiency anemia. As no nonanemic control group was included, these findings describe the diagnostic yield within this population and do not establish the clinical benefit of combined endoscopic evaluation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Psychological stress can cause or exacerbate irritable bowel syndrome (IBS). According to the Rome V framework, functional gastrointestinal disorders, including IBS, are classified as gut-brain interaction disorders. These disorders involve information processing by the central nervous system. Therefore, to understand IBS pathophysiology, it is necessary to focus on the central neural circuits regulating visceral sensation and colorectal motility. In this review, we first outline the autonomic outflow that controls the colorectum and then focus on descending neural pathways that modulate spinal visceral sensory processing and colorectal autonomic outflow, as well as the hypothalamic, midbrain, limbic, and cortical regions that regulate these processes. Finally, we outline their effects within the context of stress.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Identification of individuals with hereditary cancer syndromes may play a role in cancer prevention and reduce the incidence of advanced-stage cancers. This review investigated the economic value of hereditary cancer testing. Following PRISMA methodology, we conducted a systematic literature review by searching PubMed-Medline and Embase to identify manuscripts published between January 2013 and December 2024 that assessed outcomes associated with GGT. This analysis describes articles assessing the economic value of GGT in individuals with and without cancer. The search identified 27,087 unique articles, of which 56 were included. Considerable heterogeneity existed regarding the GGT strategies, uptake assumptions, and comparators used. Thirty-three (59%) examined the value of GGT in breast, prostate, endometrial, pancreatic, ovarian, colorectal cancer. Forty-seven (83.9%) articles provided author-determined willingness-to-pay thresholds. Of those, 76.6% (n=36) found base-case GGT analyses to be cost-effective/cost-saving. Of the 11 studies that failed to demonstrate base-case cost-effectiveness, 54.5% found at least one GGT scenario that was cost-effective. In addition to patient benefits, there is economic value in using GGT to make clinical decisions. Existing evidence shows GGT use can be cost-effective among people with cancer, those with suspected hereditary predisposition, and identification of cancer predisposition in those with unknown risk.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
'Route to diagnosis', the clinical pathway through which a cancer is first identified, is associated with stage at presentation in colorectal cancer (CRC), but recent regional data in the UK describing this relationship following the wider adoption of symptomatic faecal immunochemical testing (FIT) is limited. This study describes contemporary routes to diagnosis among patients aged ≥ 50 years with CRC in a single Welsh health board and compares unadjusted stage distribution between routes. A retrospective cohort study was conducted across three secondary care sites within Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board, North Wales, including patients aged ≥ 50 years with newly diagnosed primary colorectal cancer between 1 January 2023 and 31 December 2024. Routes were Bowel Screening Wales (BSW), asymptomatic FIT, symptomatic FIT, symptoms only, emergency presentation, and incidental detection. Stage was the pre-treatment tumour, node, and metastasis (TNM) stage where available; otherwise, pathological stage. Stage was compared across routes using Pearson's chi-square test, with four pre-specified pairwise comparisons of advanced-stage (III-IV) disease. The asymptomatic FIT group was described only. Of 976 patients, two (0.2%) were diagnosed via asymptomatic FIT. Among the remaining 974, symptomatic FIT was the most common route (506, 52.0%), followed by BSW (172, 17.7%), symptoms only (131, 13.4%), emergency presentation (112, 11.5%), and incidental detection (53, 5.4%). Overall, 515/974 (52.9%) had advanced-stage disease, and stage differed by route (p < 0.001). Advanced disease was lowest in BSW (37.8%), intermediate in symptomatic FIT (51.8%), higher in symptoms-only (60.3%) and emergency (60.7%) diagnoses, and highest in incidental diagnoses (77.4%). Compared with BSW, the proportion with advanced disease was 22.9 percentage points higher in emergency presentations (95% CI 11.3-34.5) and 39.6 points higher in incidental diagnoses (95% CI 26.2-53.0). The difference between symptomatic FIT and emergency presentations (8.9 points, 95% CI -1.1 to 19.0) was not statistically significant. In this unadjusted analysis, which may partly reflect differences in age, tumour location and staging method, screening-detected cancers had the lowest proportion of advanced disease and incidental diagnoses the highest. Just over half of cancers diagnosed after a positive symptomatic FIT were stage III-IV; as only diagnosed patients were included, this does not assess FIT effectiveness. These findings provide a regional benchmark and identify pathways where the reasons for late-stage diagnosis warrant further investigation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Tumor-associated monocytes and macrophages are abundant in the tumor microenvironment (TME) and can influence the therapeutic accessibility of antibody drugs. However, the impact of macrophage-mediated antibody sequestration on the therapeutic efficacy of anti-epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) therapy remains unclear. This study aimed to assess whether monocytes and macrophages attenuate anti-EGFR therapeutic efficacy by sequestering antibodies. We established a transwell-based co-culture platform using human THP-1 monocytes or macrophages and EGFR-positive DiFi colorectal cancer cells to evaluate macrophage-associated antibody sequestration. In vivo xenograft assays, flow cytometric uptake analyses and inhibitor-based functional studies were performed using the anti-EGFR monoclonal antibodies cetuximab and panitumumab. Xenograft models co-implanted with THP-1 cells demonstrated attenuated responses to anti-EGFR antibodies compared to tumor-only models. Monocytes and macrophages significantly reduced the growth-inhibitory effects of cetuximab and panitumumab in co-culture. Antibody uptake was increased in THP-1 cells and THP-1-derived macrophages. Fc receptor blockade and uptake-associated inhibitors partially suppressed antibody uptake and restored antibody-mediated anti-tumor activity, suggesting the involvement of FcγR-dependent and FcγR-independent pathways. Monocyte- and macrophage-mediated antibody sequestration attenuates anti-EGFR therapeutic efficacy by reducing antibody accessibility to tumor cells. The established co-culture platform provides a useful bioanalytical assay system to screen and evaluate antibody accessibility and macrophage-associated sequestration during the preclinical development of antibody therapeutics.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Somatic alterations in the RAS-RAF-MAPK and PI3K pathways are key in colorectal cancer (CRC), yet their distribution, co-occurrence patterns, and clinical significance remain incompletely defined. We characterized RAS/MAPK- and PI3K-pathway alterations in a large cohort and assessed their prognostic implications. We analyzed whole-exome sequencing data from 1243 paired samples from patients with CRC. Somatic variants in KRAS, NRAS, HRAS, BRAF, and PIK3CA were analyzed to quantify frequencies, codon-level distributions, and co-occurrence patterns. Descriptive somatic mutation status and demographic and clinical characteristics were evaluated using chi-square or Fisher exact tests, and associations with overall survival (OS) were evaluated using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models. Any RAS-family mutation was detected in 507 tumors (40.8%); KRAS, NRAS, and HRAS mutations occurred in 35.3%, 5.4%, and 0.6%, respectively. BRAF V600E was detected in 85 tumors (6.8%), PIK3CA in 221 (17.8%), and KRAS G12C in 38 (3.1%). KRAS codon 12 was the dominant RAS hotspot. KRAS-PIK3CA co-mutations occurred in 126 tumors (10.1% overall; 28.7% of KRAS-mutant tumors), whereas KRAS-BRAF and KRAS-NRAS co-mutations were uncommon, consistent with MAPK pathway mutual exclusivity. RAS-mutant tumors were enriched in right-sided and microsatellite-stable disease (p < 0.001 for both). KRAS, BRAF V600E, and PIK3CA mutation frequencies were higher in right-sided than left-sided tumors. In unadjusted analyses, Hispanic patients had lower KRAS, BRAF V600E, and PIK3CA mutation frequencies than non-Hispanic patients. After adjustment for age, sex, tumor location, and MSI status, the associations with KRAS and PIK3CA were attenuated, whereas the lower frequency of BRAF V600E among Hispanic patients persisted (p < 0.01). Mutation status was not significantly associated with 5-year overall survival. RAS/MAPK and PI3K pathway alterations in CRC varied primarily by tumor subtype and molecular context, with clinically relevant co-mutation patterns and a targetable KRAS G12C subset. These findings may support future clinical trials targeting the BRAF-RAS axis.

tRNA-derived small RNAs (tsRNAs) regulate gene expression and cellular stress responses in cancer, but their roles in colorectal cancer (CRC) progression and chemotherapy response remain incompletely understood. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Abdominal tuberculosis (TB) and colorectal malignancy have overlapping clinical, endoscopic, and radiological features leading to difficulty in diagnosis. We describe a case of abdominal TB mimicking colon cancer, with the added dramatic complication of false-positive positron emission tomography (PET)-computed tomography (CT) findings. Our patient is a 76-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes mellitus, chronic kidney disease, and ischemic heart disease, describing a 2-month history of vomiting and loose stools, with symptoms of anorexia, weight loss, and progressive abdominal distension. Colonoscopy revealed circumferential ulceroproliferative growth at the transverse colon with luminal narrowing. On PET-CT scan, there were fluorodeoxyglucose-avid epiphrenic lymphadenopathy and peritoneal deposits suggesting metastatic colonic carcinoma. However, colonoscopic biopsy showed granulomatous ulcero-inflammatory change with multinucleated giant cells and positive acid-fast bacilli (AFB), but ruled out malignancy. GeneXpert MTB/RIF on sputum and ascitic fluid was negative. Ascitic fluid analysis revealed a low serum-ascites albumin gradient with high protein, consistent with tuberculous peritonitis. Antitubercular therapy (ATT) was initiated. At 8-week follow-up, the patient gained weight, and ascites had substantially regressed. This case highlights the critical importance of tissue biopsy with special staining in elderly patients from TB-endemic countries presenting with colonic lesions and PET-CT findings that mimic disseminated malignancy. AFB staining of colonoscopic biopsies should be a routine component of the diagnostic workup in such settings, and a negative GeneXpert should not exclude abdominal TB.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Minimally invasive approaches have transformed right cancer surgery, with robotic platforms enhancing challenging techniques like complete mesocolic excision (CME). While traditionally performed using the da Vinci® Multiport system (MP), the introduction of the Single Port™ platform (SP) offers a valuable alternative. This study aims to evaluate the technical feasibility and pathologic surrogates of resection adequacy of robotic right colectomy with CME performed with the daVinci SP® compared to the daVinci Xi® platform in selected patients. From February 2024 to February 2025 consecutive patients who underwent robotic right colectomy and CME either with MP or SP platform were enrolled in the study. The two populations of patients were compared with particular attention to number and location of lymph nodes harvested as a surrogate outcome for oncologic adequacy. From February 2024 to February 2025, 52 consecutive patients were enrolled in the study. There were no differences in population characteristics with the exception for BMI, which was lower in the SP group. Operative times were longer in the SP group. No differences were noticed in either postoperative outcomes such as length of stay (LOS) or complications rate nor in pathological findings, especially in the number of apical lymph node harvested. SP robotic right colectomy with CME appears feasible and achieves pathologic surrogates of resection adequacy comparable to MP surgery in highly selected patients.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colonoscopy is the most effective method for colorectal cancer screening; however, successful insertion requires a high level of operator skill and may cause patient discomfort or injury. To address these challenges, self-propelled colonoscopy robots that generate propulsion at the distal tip have been actively investigated. In our previous work, we developed a self-propelled colonoscopy robot using a worm-gear mechanism; however, the use of rigid gears posed a potential risk of excessive contact force on the colonic wall. In this study, we propose a self-propelled colonoscopy robot enabled by soft gears that combine compliant contact with gear-based power transmission. By reinterpreting the crawler-based propulsion concept as a soft spur gear driven by a worm-gear mechanism, the proposed design allows elastic deformation of the gear teeth under load, providing adaptive traction through compliant deformation of the gear teeth. Gear parameters were optimized using gear-design software, and four soft-gear configurations were fabricated to investigate their propulsion characteristics. The prototypes were fabricated using stereolithography 3D printing and evaluated using a colonoscopy training model. The robot achieved a maximum propulsive speed of 9.6 mm/s and a propulsive force of 1.5 N in straight sections. Gears with larger modules produced higher propulsion performance. In addition, the proposed coaxial double-worm-gear architecture enabled traversal of curved sections of the colon model under manual steering. These results demonstrate the mechanical feasibility of using soft gears as a propulsion mechanism for self-propelled colonoscopy robots. Although the evaluation was limited to a colonoscopy training model, the proposed design demonstrated stable propulsion in a colonoscopy training model while maintaining compliant contact with the intestinal wall. The simple and compact mechanical structure provides a promising proof of concept for future minimally invasive robotic endoscopy, although further ex vivo and in vivo validation will be required.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) is an important and significant reason for cancer-related morbidity and mortality globally. Treatment remains challenging due to recurrence, metastasis, and chemoresistance. Evidence shows that oxidative stress, ongoing inflammation, and cancer stem cells (CSCs) play essential functions in CRC development and progression. Nrf2 is a master regulator of cellular redox balance through the Keap1-Nrf2-is signalling pathway. Normal activation of Nrf2 protects colonic cells from oxidative DNA harm and inflammation during initial carcinogenesis. However, sustained Nrf2 activation in tumours encourages chemoresistance, metabolic reprogramming, and CSC upkeep, showing a dual role. Traditional medicine and dietary phytochemicals (curcumin, sulforaphane, resveratrol, EGCG, berberine) can modulate Nrf2 while interacting with NF-κB, Wnt/β-catenin, and Notch pathways. This review synthesises mechanistic and translational evidence on Nrf2 modulation in CRC chemoprevention, stressing conventional medicine-derived agents in modern approaches. It moreover highlights difficulties, limitations, and future viewpoints for precision chemoprevention and personalised interventions.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Direct RAS targeting has progressed from pharmacologic proof of concept to routine treatment for selected KRAS G12C-mutant cancers. KRAS G12C inhibitors and KRAS G12C-EGFR combinations established allele- and lineage-specific treatment paradigms. More recently, the multiselective RAS(ON) inhibitor daraxonrasib became the first FDA-approved direct RAS-targeted therapy for metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma, while the KRAS G12D-directed degrader setidegrasib remains investigational. Target engagement alone, however, does not ensure durable disease control, and the same drug class can perform differently across tumor lineages. This Review develops an adaptive RAS signaling ecosystem model in which allele and isoform biology, membrane organization, feedback architecture, mutant-wild-type RAS crosstalk, co-mutation patterns, chromatin state, epithelial-mesenchymal plasticity, metabolism, spatial heterogeneity, the tumor microenvironment and treatment delivery jointly determine pathway dependence and therapeutic escape. Comparisons among pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, colorectal cancer, lung adenocarcinoma and NRAS-mutant melanoma show how related oncogenic RAS nodes acquire different vulnerabilities in distinct tissue contexts. We integrate direct RAS inhibition with mechanism-guided vertical and horizontal strategies directed at feedback rebound, bypass signaling, cell-state persistence, stromal protection, metabolic adaptation and immune exclusion. We then translate this model into a biomarker-integrated development framework that links serial circulating tumor DNA, modality-matched pharmacodynamic assays, paired tissue sampling, spatial profiling and toxicity-aware scheduling to prespecified, falsifiable treatment hypotheses. RAS dependence is conditional rather than absolute. Durable control will require strategies that match the RAS allele and tumor lineage to the dominant adaptive circuitry, verify that target and pathway suppression persist over time, and maintain sufficient dose intensity to exert biologically effective pressure without disabling antitumor immunity or normal-tissue function.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Early-onset colorectal cancer (EOCRC), defined as CRC diagnosed before age 50, is rising globally despite declining incidence in older adults, representing a growing public health concern. This review synthesizes current evidence on EOCRC epidemiology, molecular features, etiologic hypotheses, and clinical implications, with an emphasis on life-course risk. Epidemiologic data demonstrate a strong birth cohort effect, implicating generational exposures in disease pathogenesis. Younger patients more often present with symptomatic, advanced-stage disease and show a predominance of distal and rectal tumors. Molecular analyses reveal modest differences from late-onset CRC, including lower BRAF mutation rates and predominance of microsatellite-stable, chromosomal instability tumors, without a defining molecular signature. Current evidence supports a multifactorial etiologic model involving metabolic dysfunction, Western dietary patterns, microbiome disruption, antibiotic exposure, and environmental factors. These exposures likely interact with genetic and epigenetic susceptibility over time to accelerate established colorectal carcinogenesis pathways rather than produce a distinct biologic entity. Among these, obesity and diet have the strongest epidemiologic support, while other contributors remain under investigation. Clinically, EOCRC highlights limitations of age-based screening and the need for improved symptom recognition, earlier diagnosis, and risk-stratified screening approaches. Prevention strategies should extend beyond midlife screening to target modifiable exposures earlier in life. EOCRC may often reflect accelerated carcinogenesis within established pathways, although conflicting molecular findings and potential biologic subsets warrant further investigation.
