ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Gegenqinlian Decoction (GQD) has been used as a folk remedy for gastrointestinal diseases in China over thousands of years, and demonstrates significant efficacy against inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). We previously showed that the active components alignment of GQD inhibits nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB) p65 signal transduction and plays a key role in preventing and treating IBD. With growing insights into the gut microbiota and its metabolites, the molecular mechanisms underlying therapeutic effects of GQD against IBD require further elucidation. This is particularly relevant given the previously reported relationship between the host NF-κB pathway and the gut microbiota. To explore the therapeutic mechanisms of GQD and its aligned active components against IBD, with a focus on microbiota-involved regulation of the host sphingosine kinase 1 (SphK1) /sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P) / NF-κB signaling pathway, using both 2,4,6-Trinitrobenzenesulfonic acid (TNBS)-induced rat colitis and dextran sulfate sodium salt (DSS)-induced mouse colitis models and cultured cells. In this research, the therapeutic effect of GQD on TNBS-induced colitis rats was evaluated through the measurement of body weight, colorectal length, disease activity index (DAI), colon length and hematoxylin-eosin staining. 16S rRNA gene sequencing and untargeted metabolomic analyses were performed to evaluate the restoration of gut microbial and metabolic homeostasis by GQD. Network pharmacology and molecular docking were then utilized to explore the potential relationships between specific targets and the active components alignment (ACA) of GQD on IBD treatment. To further validate the in vivo effects of the ACA, a dextran sulfate sodium salt (DSS)-induced mouse colitis model was established, and body weight, DAI, colorectum length, histopathology, S1P levels, and SphK1/S1PR1 expression were assessed. Experimental validation in LPS-stimulated RAW264.7 macrophages and NCM460 colonic epithelial cells was subsequently conducted to determine whether this active components alignment suppressed the SphK1/S1P/NF-κB pathway via molecular and cellular assays, including cell metabolomics, ELISA, Western blot, and immunofluorescence staining. GQD significantly relieved symptoms, colonic inflammation, and intestinal damage in TNBS-induced colitis rats. It partially reversed gut microbiota dysbiosis, modulated sphingolipid metabolic pathways, and downregulated the expression of sphingolipid-related Sphk1 and S1PR1 proteins, as well as S1P levels, in colon tissues (p < 0.05). In the DSS-induced mouse colitis model, the ACA of GQD significantly alleviated body weight loss, DAI, colorectum shortening, and histopathological damage, and reduced S1P levels and SphK1/S1PR1 expression in colon tissues (p < 0.05 or p < 0.01). In vitro, the ACA of GQD attenuated LPS-induced inflammatory responses in RAW264.7 macrophages and NCM460 colonic epithelial cells, as reflected by significant reductions in the levels of NO, ROS, and pro-inflammatory cytokines such as IL-6, TNF-α, and IL-1β, and S1P production (p < 0.05 or p < 0.01). Mechanistic dissection revealed that this ACA of GQD suppressed SphK1 expression and S1P production, inhibiting IκBα degradation and NF-κB p65 nuclear translocation, as directly evidenced by immunofluorescence staining, thus repressing the transcription of downstream pro-inflammatory genes and alleviating intestinal inflammation. GQD restored gut microecological homeostasis and rectified sphingolipid metabolic disturbances. Its active components alignment afforded anti-inflammatory and colitis-protective effects, partially via modulation of the SphK1/S1P/NF-κB signaling pathway. The consistent therapeutic and mechanistic effects observed in both TNBS-induced rat colitis and DSS-induced mouse colitis support that the eight-component alignment largely recapitulates the key effects of the complete GQD formulation. These findings provide novel mechanistic insights and a scientific rationale for the clinical application of GQD in the management of IBD.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
A comprehensive characterization of surgical trends, facility-level variation, and potential health equity gaps among patients undergoing rectal cancer surgery is lacking within Veterans Health Administration - the nation's largest integrated healthcare system serving a population underrepresented in other cancer registries. We characterized national temporal and facility-level trends in rectal cancer surgery and evaluated whether race and ethnicity independently predict treatment. This was a retrospective study of veterans who underwent oncologic resection for rectal cancer in Veterans Health Administration from 2014-2024. Receipt of minimally invasive and surgery sphincter-preserving surgery were measured. We identified 2,758 veterans who underwent resection for rectal cancer across 91 facilities; the cohort was predominantly male (95.9%) with a mean age of 65.2 years and included 72.4% non-Hispanic White and 16.4% non-Hispanic Black veterans. Open surgery declined from 69.7% to 33.9%, driven by a five-fold increase in robotic-assisted procedures, which rose from 9.0% to 50.0% (p<0.001). Sphincter-preserving surgery rates remained stable, (73.3% to 72.0%, p<0.001). Facility-level heterogeneity was wide - median facility robotics utilization was 4.8% (range 0-67.1%) and sphincter-preserving surgery use was 75.0% (range 25.0%-100%). Veterans in the most deprived neighborhoods experienced reduced odds of minimally invasive surgery (odds ratio 0.60, 95% confidence interval 0.42-0.85). Race and ethnicity were not predictors of outcomes. Robotic-assisted rectal cancer surgery increased five-fold within Veterans Health Administration, while sphincter-preserving surgery remained stable. Race and ethnicity did not independently predict receipt of either procedure. However, lower odds of minimally invasive surgery in deprived neighborhoods and facility-level heterogeneity suggest structural disparities.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Expeditious discharge following colorectal cancer (CRC) surgical resection has been associated with improved outcomes, reduced costs and resource utilization, and appears to be safe without increasing readmission rates. Despite these established advantages, the impact of sociodemographic, clinical, and regional factors on early postoperative discharge is not clear. We used the National Cancer Database (2010-2022) to perform multinomial logistic regression for odds of early (<3 days) and late (≥7-30 days) discharge versus standard (3-6 days) following surgical resection for patients with Stage I-III colon or rectal adenocarcinoma. We incorporated several sociodemographic, clinical, and regional characteristics; colon and rectal cohorts were analyzed separately. Among 278,004 patients with colon cancer and 56,712 patients with rectal cancer, the strongest independent predictor of early discharge was robotic surgery (colon: OR=3.29, 95%CI=3.18-3.40; rectum: OR=1.32, 95%CI=1.23-1.41). However, Black patients (colon: OR=0.91, 95%CI=0.88-0.95; rectum: OR=0.91, 95%CI=0.87-0.95), those living rurally (colon: OR=0.94, 95%CI=0.90-0.98; rectum: OR=0.97, 95%CI=0.93-1.00), and non-privately insured patients were less likely to undergo robotic surgery. Compared with the privately insured, Medicaid (colon: OR=1.65, 95%CI=1.58-1.72, rectum: OR=1.43, 95%CI=1.33-1.53), Medicare (colon: OR=1.42, 95%CI=1.38-1.46; rectum: OR=1.34, 95%CI=1.26-1.43), and uninsured (colon: OR=1.52, 95%CI=1.44-1.61; rectum: OR=1.33, 95%CI=1.20-1.48) patients were more likely to be discharged late. Early discharge was associated with lower odds of 30-day readmissions (colon: OR=0.87, 95%CI=0.83-0.91; rectum: OR=0.73, 95%CI=0.65-0.82). Increased uptake of robotic surgery and more equitable distribution of minimally invasive surgical approaches may increase opportunities for early discharge among marginalized patient populations.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Organ preservation strategies, particularly the watch-and-wait (W&W) approach in rectal cancer, have gained increasing international interest in recent years. However, their implementation remains heterogeneous across institutions. The aim of this study was to evaluate the degree of use of W&W in hospitals across Spain. A cross-sectional observational study was conducted through a national survey addressed to general surgeons involved in rectal cancer management. The questionnaire was designed using Google Forms® and distributed through the Spanish Association of Surgeons (AEC) and the Spanish Association of Coloproctology (AECP). The development of the survey followed the methodological recommendations of the Checklist for Reporting Of Survey Studies (CROSS). The statistical analysis included descriptive statistics and a univariate analysis to identify factors associated with the use of W&W. A total of 154 valid responses were obtained. Among respondents, 102 surgeons (66%) considered W&W a safe strategy. Seventy (45%) reported offering W&W in a protocolized manner, while 40 (26%) applied it without a formal protocol. Forty-four participants (29%) did not offer this option, and opposition from the multidisciplinary tumor board was the main limiting factor (30 cases, 60%). Univariate analysis showed that W&W use was associated with specialized colorectal units (P = .001), national accreditation as a colorectal unit (P = .01), and higher case volume (P = .02). Most survey participants (92.3%) emphasized the need for further education and training in W&W and rectal cancer. The implementation of W&W in Spain remains limited and heterogeneous. Enhanced training and standardized criteria may facilitate broader implementation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a major global health burden, with approximately 2 million new cases and 1 million deaths annually. The growing resistance to conventional chemotherapy highlights the need for new therapeutic strategies against drug-resistant CRC. In this study, platinum(II) complexes of the general formula [PtCl(Ln)]CF3SO3, based on substituted 2,2':6',2″-terpyridines (Pt1) and 2,6-bis(thiazol-2-yl)pyridines (Pt2), were synthesized and evaluated for anticancer activity. Their antiproliferative effects were assessed in doxorubicin-sensitive and doxorubicin-resistant CRC cell lines, as well as primary dermal fibroblasts. Among the tested complexes, Pt1a showed the highest potency, exhibiting strong cytotoxicity against HCT116-DoxR cells (IC50 = 0.7 μM). Mechanistic studies revealed that Pt1a increases reactive oxygen species levels, binds DNA, disrupts cell cycle progression, and induces apoptosis and autophagy. Pt1a also displayed anti-metastatic and anti-angiogenic activities, showed favourable interaction with bovine serum albumin, and exhibited no detectable toxicity in a chicken embryo model.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Porous supramolecular metal-organic frameworks (SMOFs) are versatile functional materials for controlled drug delivery and tailored water vapor sorption whose properties are deeply dependent on their specific internal microenvironment. Precisely tuning the internal pore environment of a coordination framework without perturbing its underlying topology remains a fundamental challenge in crystal engineering. Herein, we address this challenge in a family of water-stable copper-adenine supramolecular metal-organic frameworks (SMOFs). By systematically varying the monocarboxylate counterion, fine control over the accessible void space (ranging from 12 to 29%) was achieved, which dictates their water vapor sorption behavior through the simultaneous modification of steric hindrance and hydrophobicity. Furthermore, this work introduces a nondestructive magnetic sustentation technique that leverages the room-temperature paramagnetic nature of these frameworks to quantify the loading of highly insoluble drugs (5-fluorouracil, cycloserine, and gabapentin). In this context, drug uptake and release act as complementary experimental probes to validate our structural design. The structurally optimized Cu7Bz material achieved a notable 31.4% loading of 5-fluorouracil. Finally, in vitro assays on HCT116 colorectal cancer cells reveal that the compact pore architecture of 5-FU@Cu7Bz effectively mitigates the toxic "burst-release" effect, providing a sustained and potent antiproliferative response. These results establish counterion-directed pore engineering as a practical strategy for the design of advanced solid-state materials and introduce magnetic sustentation as a robust tool for evaluating complex host-guest systems.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Exosomes, nanoscale extracellular vesicles carrying native membrane proteins, play crucial roles in intercellular communication and are critically involved in colorectal cancer progression and drug resistance, thereby offering a biologically relevant platform for targeted drug discovery. In this study, we developed an innovative immobilized exosome affinity screening platform (Exo@SiO2-NH2) using HT-29 cell-derived exosomes to selectively capture antitumor bioactive compounds from Sophora flavescens. Through UHPLC-MS/MS analysis, four compounds─Kushenol I, Kurarinone, 2'-O-MethylKurarinone, and Isoxanthohumol were successfully enriched and identified. To explore potential exosome-associated targets, systematic molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations were conducted on representative exosome-enriched proteins against these four compounds. Further combinatorial alanine scanning mutagenesis within the predicted binding pockets (<5.0 Å) suggested CD81 and HSP90 as probable protein targets. Subsequent functional validation via siRNA-mediated knockdown of CD81 and HSP90, combined with IC50 determination via CCK-8 assays, confirmed target-dependent alterations in drug responsiveness, supporting their role as key functional mediators. Together, this integrated strategy provides a practical and novel approach for discovering anti-colorectal cancer molecules targeting exosome-associated protein interfaces.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
We aimed to develop a clinic-molecular prognostic nomogram for patients with microsatellite stable and BRAF wild-type metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) using comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP) and clinical data taking advantage from a prospectively maintained dataset at three Italian Institutions and three randomized trials. The overall cohort was split into development and validation sets. The prognostic model was built on the development set using prespecified landmark intervals. Genomic and clinical predictors were identified within a stability-selection framework based on an L1-penalized Cox model and subsequently incorporated into a stratified Cox model with metastasectomy modeled as a time-dependent covariate. The overall cohort included 1071 patients. Stability selection identified RAS (SST: 98%) and SMAD4 (SST: 92%) as the only genomic alterations providing additional prognostic information beyond the prespecified clinical model. In the overall population, patients with RAS/SMAD4 double wild-type tumors had the most favorable overall survival, whereas RAS mutations, SMAD4 alterations, and RAS/SMAD4 co-alterations were associated with inferior outcomes. The final nomogram integrated RAS/SMAD4 with clinical variables and metastasectomy. In the development cohort, time-dependent AUCs were 0.723 and 0.736 at 1 and 4 years, respectively. In the validation cohort, AUCs were 0.657 and 0.711 at the same time points. These findings suggest that prognostically relevant genomic information in MSS, BRAF wild-type mCRC may be captured by targeted NGS panels including RAS and SMAD4. By integrating these alterations with clinical variables and time-updated information on metastasectomy, this clinic-molecular nomogram provides individualized dynamic survival estimates.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The incidence of early-onset colorectal cancer (EOCRC) has increased over the past three decades. Diagnoses coincide with formative emotional and social life stages, creating challenges for patients overlooked by survivorship guidelines. This study explored the emotional and psychosocial impacts of EOCRC. We conducted interviews with 63 patients with EOCRC at seven academic medical centers. Interviews focused on emotional and psychosocial needs and were analyzed using thematic analysis. Five themes were identified: (1) emotional and psychosocial distress; (2) dealing with uncertainty; (3) coming to terms with a "new normal"; (4) managing distress; and (5) role of medical providers. Patients described disruptions to life events and access to EOCRC-specific mental health and informational resources was an unmet need. EOCRC profoundly impacts emotional and psychosocial well-being. Individuals experienced difficulties adjusting to a "new normal" affecting identity formation, family planning, and career progression. Access to tailored support services was lacking.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Recent studies have shown that G protein-coupled P2Y6 receptor (P2Y6R) can play a promoting or inhibitory role in some tumors, but the functional effect of P2Y6R on the migration and invasion of colorectal cancer (CRC) is still poorly understood. Therefore, this study comprehensively investigated whether the P2Y6R plays a promoting or inhibiting role in the migration and invasion of CRC. Public databases were used to investigate the intrinsic association between P2Y6R and CRC tissue. Functional experiments was used to investigate the effects of P2Y6R activation or inhibition on CRC migration, invasion, cytoskeleton and glycogen accumulation. The results showed that high expression of P2Y6R was negatively correlated with overall survival and prognosis of CRC patients. The P2Y6R agonist (UDP) opened the function of the pore on the cell membrane and increased the influx of calcium ions, while antagonistic to its activation could produce a significant inhibitory effect. UDP promoted the migration and invasion capabilities of CRC cells, enhanced the fibrin stress capabilities of the cytoskeleton, and promoted the glycogen accumulation capabilities of cells. However, the P2Y6R antagonist MRS2578 or MRS4853 significantly inhibited these changes induced by UDP. Moreover, the P2Y6R had a clear correlation with AKT/mTOR in patients with CRC tissues. UDP increased the protein expression levels of p-AKT and p-mTOR in CRC cells, while P2Y6R antagonists decreased the protein expression levels of p-AKT and p-mTOR by inhibiting P2Y6R activity. In addition, based on P2Y6R activation, the application of AKT/mTOR pathway inhibitor BGT226 inhibited UDP-induced migration, invasion, cytoskeleton and glycogen accumulation of CRC cells. Combined intervention of P2Y6R antagonists and BGT226 produced additive inhibitory pharmacological effects. These data reveal that high expression of P2Y6R contributes to poor overall survival outcomes in patients with CRC. Activation of P2Y6R promotes the migration, invasion and glycogen accumulation of CRC cells, and the mechanism may be related to the AKT/mTOR pathway. This also reveals that the P2Y6R can be used as another important target for the prevention and treatment of CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Acquired resistance remains a major limitation to the sustained efficacy of mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase (MEK) inhibition in colorectal cancer (CRC), but the molecular adaptations associated with this phenotype remain incompletely defined. This pilot study investigated the association of Caveolin-1 with acquired resistance to the MEK1/2 inhibitor selumetinib, and epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) signaling. Selumetinib-resistant derivatives of HT-29 and SW480 CRC cells were generated by prolonged drug exposure. CAV1 mRNA and Caveolin-1 protein expression were assessed by reverse transcription-quantitative PCR and western blotting, respectively, and the functional relevance of Caveolin-1 was examined using independent short hair RNA-mediated knockdown approaches. CAV1 mRNA and Caveolin-1 protein expression were consistently upregulated in selumetinib-resistant cells compared with their parental counterparts. Caveolin-1 depletion impaired proliferation of resistant cells and, in the presence of selumetinib, further reduced cell viability and enhanced apoptotic responses, as evidenced by increased caspase-3/7 activity and cleavage of PARP and caspase-3. In HT-29/SR cells, Caveolin-1 depletion was associated with altered EGF-induced EGFR and GSK-3α/β phosphorylation. These findings identify Caveolin-1 upregulation as a feature of the experimentally established selumetinib-resistant phenotype and suggest a functional association between Caveolin-1 and cellular responses to sustained MEK inhibition. However, the signaling observations were limited to HT-29/SR cells and do not establish EGFR-dependent causality. Further validation in independently derived resistant populations and physiologically relevant models is required to determine the mechanistic and translational significance of these findings.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Metabolic reprogramming and innate immune signaling are closely involved in colorectal cancer (CRC) progression, but the effects of extracellular mitochondria-derived vesicles (MDVs) on these processes remain unclear, partly because of their low natural yield. In this study, we overexpressed MDV formation-related genes in mesenchymal stem cells and identified OPA1 and PINK1 as regulators that increased the recovery of extracellular MDVs. The resulting OPA1- and PINK1-MDV preparations were characterized and then incubated with LOVO and SW480 CRC cells to assess their uptake, metabolic effects, inflammatory signaling, and antitumor activities. OPA1-MDVs contained a TOMM20-positive/PDHE1α-positive vesicle population and shifted CRC cell metabolism away from glycolysis toward oxidative phosphorylation, as shown by reduced glycolytic enzyme activity and lactate production, together with increased oxygen consumption, respiratory-chain activity, and mitochondrial membrane potential. These changes were accompanied by reduced reactive oxygen species levels and impaired CRC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion. In contrast, PINK1-MDVs impaired mitochondrial function, increased reactive oxygen species production, and were associated with activation of cGAS-STING-related inflammatory signaling, possibly through the delivery of mitochondrial DNA. Both MDV preparations suppressed tumor growth in an immunocompetent syngeneic MC38 tumor model. These findings suggest that MDVs derived from OPA1- or PINK1-overexpressing cells suppress CRC growth through distinct metabolic and innate immune mechanisms and provide a potential strategy for engineering extracellular mitochondrial vesicles for cancer research.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Total mesorectal excision (TME) is standard for low rectal cancer (≤5cm from anal verge) but causes permanent stomas, functional impairments and surgical risks. Local excision (LE) suits early tumors (cTis-T1N0) but has higher recurrence in cT2+; watch-and-wait (WW) after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy risks residual disease. Total neoadjuvant therapy (TNT) improves outcomes, but prior LE trials had limitations. To evaluate TNT combined with planned LE for organ preservation in selected low rectal adenocarcinoma patients. Prospective single-arm phase 2 trial (June 2022-March 2024, tertiary center) enrolled 57/60 patients (cT1-3N0M0 nonmucinous adenocarcinoma, etc.). TNT: 50 Gy + 2 cycles of CapoX (standard capecitabine + oxaliplatin) + 4 consolidation CapoX. Clinical complete response (cCR)/near-complete clinical response (ncCR) patients had LE; others got TME. Patients with high-risk residual disease after LE also had additional TME. Median age was 61 years (28-79); 66.7% were male. cT3 tumors were present in 78.9%, and 78.9% had tumors ≤3 cm from the anal verge. After TNT, 47.4% achieved cCR and 38.6% achieved ncCR. Among surgically treated patients, the pathological complete response (pCR) rate was 68.6%; in the overall population, with WW counted as non-pCR, it was 61.4%. The total complete response rate, including pCR and cCR managed with WW, was 68.4%. Sphincter preservation was 94.7%. LE was associated with lower median blood loss (7 vs 50 mL; P<0.001) and shorter median hospitalization (7 vs 14 days; P=0.001) than TME. Grade 3 adverse events occurred in 22.8%, most commonly lymphocytopenia; no grade 4 or 5 events occurred. Low anterior resection syndrome (LARS) scores were assessed after TNT and at 1, 3, and 6 months postoperatively. At 6 months, LARS outcomes favored LE (80.0% vs 53.8% reporting no LARS; P=0.027). Wexner incontinence scores did not differ significantly between groups at any time point. TNT with planned LE is feasible in cT1-3N0M0 low rectal cancer, yielding a pCR rate of 61.4% in the overall population, 94.7% sphincter preservation, and acceptable toxicity. However, the non-randomized design and immature 3-year organ-preservation endpoint limit this study to a feasibility assessment and do not permit conclusions regarding comparative effectiveness versus WW. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Evidence for cold snare endoscopic mucosal resection (CS-EMR) in 10-19-mm nonpedunculated colorectal polyps is scarce. We conducted a multicenter randomized controlled trial (RCT) to compare CS-EMR against hot snare EMR (HS-EMR) in this setting. We enrolled patients with 10-19-mm nonpedunculated colorectal polyps from 15 centers. Eligible polyps were individually randomized (1:1) to CS-EMR or HS-EMR. The primary outcome was histologic complete resection, analyzed in modified intention-to-treat (mITT) and per-protocol (PP) populations (noninferiority margin -10%). Secondary outcomes included en bloc resection, intraprocedural and delayed adverse events, and resection time. 216 patients with 233 eligible polyps were included (CS-EMR 116; HS-EMR 117). In the mITT analysis, complete resection was 90.4% in the CS-EMR group and 93.2% in the HS-EMR group (difference -2.7%, 95%CI -9.8 to 4.3), showing noninferiority of CS-EMR vs. HS-EMR. PP results were consistent (CS-EMR 93.3%; HS-EMR 93.2%; difference 0.2%, 95%CI -6.7 to 7.1). CS-EMR was noninferior for 10-14-mm polyps (94.3% vs. 94.0%; 95%CI -6.8 to 7.2) but not for 15-19-mm polyps (78.6% vs. 90.9%; 95%CI -30.4 to 5.8), although interaction was not significant. En bloc resection rates and resection time were similar between groups. Intraprocedural bleeding was more frequent with CS-EMR (19.1% vs. 3.4%), whereas delayed bleeding was rare (0.0% vs. 0.9%), and no perforation occurred in either group. CS-EMR was noninferior to HS-EMR for histologic complete resection of 10-19-mm nonpedunculated colorectal polyps, but its applicability to 15-19-mm lesions remains uncertain.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Microsatellite-stable (MSS) colorectal cancer (CRC) is a molecularly complex and clinically challenging disease subtype, lacking effective targeted therapies. Leveraging multiomic data from ∼2,000 tumor samples (including 316MSS CRCs not previously profiled) representing ∼4,500 molecular profiles and 195,246 single cells/nuclei, we uncover complex biology and therapeutic vulnerabilities. Application of a multiomic-phenomic integrative framework, including iPhenMap (a machine-learning tool), reveals complex molecular programs, including replication stress, right-sided biology, glutaminolysis-driven metabolic reprogramming, and MYC-E2F transcriptional networks governing epigenetic remodeling and perineural invasion. Focusing on RAS-mutant MSS CRC, functional validation in state-of-the-art patient-derived tumoroid and matched xenograft models confirms focal adhesion kinase (FAK), phosphoinositide-dependent kinase (PDK)1/2, and proteasome inhibition as potential therapeutic strategies when combined with mitogen-activated protein kinase (MEK) blockade. This work underscores the power of integrated multiomic profiling and functional modeling to refine potential treatment approaches in MSS CRC patient populations.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Gastrointestinal cancers (GICs) remain a major global health burden due to late-stage diagnosis, limited therapeutic efficacy, and poor prognosis. Conventional diagnostic and treatment strategies are often invasive, costly, and lack real-time monitoring capabilities, highlighting the need for the innovative and patient-centered approaches. This review critically examines the recent advances in microfluidic chip technologies for the diagnosis, modeling, and treatment of GICs, including gastric, colorectal, liver, pancreatic, and esophageal cancers. Microfluidic platforms enable the precise manipulation of microscale fluids, offering advantages such as reduced reagent consumption, high sensitivity, and integration of multiplexed assays into portable systems. Notably, recent studies demonstrate diagnostic performance with area under the curve (AUC) values exceeding 0.90 and sensitivities approaching 90%, while detection limits for key biomarkers such as ctDNA and proteins have reached attomolar (10⁻¹⁸ M) and picogram-per-milliliter levels. Applications discussed include circulating tumor cell (CTC) isolation, exosome and ctDNA detection, tumor-on-chip models, and microfluidic drug delivery systems. In addition, advances in materials, fabrication techniques, and fluid dynamics are evaluated for their role in optimizing device performance. Emerging integrations with machine learning further enhance diagnostic accuracy and predictive capability. Despite these promising developments, challenges related to standardization, scalability, and clinical validation remain. Overall, microfluidic technologies represent a transformative platform for enabling rapid, minimally invasive, and highly sensitive approaches to cancer diagnosis and personalized therapy in gastrointestinal oncology.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Intussusception of bowel in adults is relatively rare and most commonly secondary to gastrointestinal malignancies. We present the case of an 80-year-old man with rectosigmoid adenocarcinoma evaluated via 18F-FDG PET/CT. Imaging revealed rectosigmoid intussusception with a characteristic "target sign" on both PET and CT images involving the invaginated bowel, alongside synchronous FDG-avid lung metastases. Subsequent MRI confirmed the anatomical findings. This case highlights the unique utility of hybrid 18F-FDG PET/CT in simultaneously delineating both malignant and nonmalignant metabolic and anatomical changes and providing critical whole-body staging to guide clinical management.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
We present [18F]AlF-NOTA-FAPI-04 PET/CT findings of an incidentally detected benign phyllodes tumor in a 68-year-old woman with prior colon cancer. Routine contrast-enhanced CT revealed a right breast nodule with moderate enhancement, and subsequent PET/CT demonstrated intense focal FAPI uptake (SUVmax: 6.63). Histology confirmed the presence of a benign phyllodes tumor. This case highlights that FAPI-avid lesions in cancer survivors may represent benign entities with fibroblast-rich stroma, underscoring the importance of considering benign diagnoses and obtaining histologic confirmation to avoid unnecessary treatment.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
ALDH1B1 is a mitochondrial aldehyde dehydrogenase required for the survival of stem-like colorectal and pancreatic cancer cells. Isoform-selective guanidinyl antagonists of aldehyde dehydrogenases (IGUANAs) have been developed for ALDH1B1, and here we describe structure-activity relationship (SAR) studies of three scaffold components: the bicyclic guanidine core, a substituted aryl ring that engages the catalytic site, and a biaryl group that interacts with flanking residues. We further show that previously reported IGUANAs are metabolically labile and rapidly effluxed from intestinal epithelial cells. To address these limitations, we have explored bioisosteres of the biaryl moiety and modifications of the guanidine core. These investigations have yielded the aryl-alkyl ether derivative IGUANA-5, a potent ALDH1B1 inhibitor that selectively blocks the growth of colon and pancreatic cancer spheroids and exhibits enhanced in vitro and in vivo pharmacological properties. Our findings establish a new class of ALDH1B1 inhibitors that could inform the advancement of anti-cancer therapies.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The relaxin family peptide receptor 4 (RXFP4) is a promising therapeutic target for constipation owing to its critical role in regulating gastrointestinal motility. However, the development of selective small-molecule RXFP4 agonists remains challenging because of the high structural homology between RXFP4 and RXFP3 and the difficulty of achieving gut-restricted exposure. Herein, guided by the cryo-electron microscopy structure of RXFP4, we report the structure-guided design and optimization of a novel series of tetrahydroisoquinoline-based RXFP4 agonists. Structure-activity relationship studies identified compound 44 as a potent RXFP4 agonist with excellent selectivity over RXFP3 and a gut-restricted pharmacokinetic profile with an approximately 500-fold ileum-to-plasma exposure ratio. In a loperamide-induced constipation mouse model, oral administration of compound 44 significantly enhanced colorectal propulsion and alleviated constipation-related symptoms. Collectively, this work establishes a structure-guided strategy for optimizing receptor subtype selectivity and gut-restricted exposure, providing a promising lead and a framework for the development of RXFP4-targeted therapeutics.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Dietary supplement use is common in the general population, but literature addressing supplement use throughout the disease trajectory in colorectal cancer (CRC) survivors is limited. Data from the COLON study, a prospective cohort among participants diagnosed with stage I-IV CRC, were used. Participants were asked to fill out a dietary supplement questionnaire at diagnosis (n = 1934), 6 months post-diagnosis (n = 1769), 2 years post-diagnosis (n = 1533), and 5 years post-diagnosis (n = 1198) containing questions on type, brand, frequency, and doses of supplements. Participants were considered regular supplement users if they used ≥ 1 supplement(s) at least once a week. Supplement use was reported in 43% of participants at diagnosis, 42% at 6 months post-diagnosis, 45% at 2 years post-diagnosis, and 53% at 5 years post-diagnosis. Multivitamins, vitamin D, and vitamin C were most often reported. Almost half of the participants (48%) with data across all timepoints (n = 1146) changed their dietary supplement use at least once during the 5 years post-diagnosis, whereas 26% were consistent users and 26% consistent non-users. The tolerable upper intake level was exceeded for 1-2% of vitamin D users, 7-13% of vitamin B6 users, 4-5% of folic acid users, 14-32% of magnesium users, and 6-23% of iron users. Across all timepoints, female and higher educated participants were more likely to use supplements. Participants diagnosed with stage III/IV CRC (versus I/II) and those receiving adjuvant treatment (versus not receiving) were less likely to use supplements at 6 months and 2 years post-diagnosis. Dietary supplement use is common among CRC survivors. Given the regular use of supplements, the potential impact of (high-dose) supplement use on clinical outcomes warrants further investigation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The progression of colon cancer from benign adenoma to malignant tumors that invade and spread underscores the critical need for accurate and less invasive biomarkers. The primary objective of this work was to assess the diagnostic potential of combining immunological biomarkers and optical polarimetric characteristics in colorectal cancer. We specifically aimed to evaluate serum cytokine profiles as potential diagnostic tools and to explore tissue optical signatures in a preliminary analysis. Secondary objectives included examining postoperative immune changes and exploring the involvement of immune checkpoints in cancer progression. Serum levels of IL-8, IL-17 A, IL-37, CTLA-4, and CCR7 were measured using ELISA in 75 colon cancer patients (37 preoperative and 38 postoperative) and 15 healthy controls, whereas tissue properties were analyzed through Mueller matrix polarimetry. Compared with healthy controls, preoperative patients had significantly higher levels of IL-8, IL-17 A, CTLA-4, and CCR7 and lower levels of IL-37 (all P < 0.001), and all five markers discriminated preoperative patients from controls in ROC analysis (AUC 0.939-1.000). Postoperative patients showed intermediate levels, consistent with partial normalization of these markers after surgery. In a preliminary polarimetric analysis of a limited number of tissue sections, cancerous tissue showed higher total depolarization than normal tissue, whereas total retardance and diattenuation varied widely and overlapped between the two tissue types. These findings support serum cytokine and immune-checkpoint profiling as a promising, less invasive approach for colorectal cancer detection and monitoring, whereas the diagnostic value of Mueller matrix polarimetry needs to be confirmed in a larger number of tissue samples with formal statistical evaluation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer remains a major global health burden, and although population-based screening is beneficial, current programs have notable limitations. Risk-stratified screening has been proposed, yet existing prediction models vary in performance and in the inclusion of predictors. Data-adaptive modeling (machine learning) may strengthen risk prediction but depends on high-quality input data. Expert consensus methods offer a structured way to identify clinically meaningful variables for future tools. To establish expert consensus on the selection of relevant variables and refinement of self-reported questionnaire items for next-generation colorectal cancer risk-prediction tools. A modified Delphi study was conducted with seventeen internationally recognized experts. The process consisted of anonymized, email-based rounds aimed at refining a questionnaire for colorectal cancer risk prediction. Across three iterative rounds, experts rated item relevance, proposed revisions, and identified missing domains while reviewing group-level summaries of ratings and comments. Items not meeting predefined thresholds were removed, and validated lifestyle-related items were incorporated. Consensus was defined as 15 of 17 experts rating an item within a similar three-point range. All seventeen experts completed all rounds. The final I-CRC-RISK Questionnaire comprises 23 items across seven categories: Demography, Health Status, Family Health History, Dietary Patterns, Physical Activity, Smoking, and Alcohol Consumption. Expert consensus was reached for 19 items. The I-CRC-RISK Questionnaire provides an expert-informed set of self-reported variables to support future risk prediction efforts. It offers a structured basis for further validation and psychometric testing before prospective data collection may be undertaken. This foundational work could enhance the predictive performance of both traditional and machine-learning approaches by improving the consistency and relevance of input data.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Tobacco smoking is prevalent among patients with rectal cancer, yet its effect on pathologic response to total neoadjuvant therapy (TNT) remains unknown. This study evaluated the association between smoking status and pathologic response to TNT in locally advanced rectal cancer, using the neoadjuvant rectal (NAR) score and pathologic complete response (pCR) rate. This retrospective cohort study used the National Cancer Database to identify adults diagnosed in 2023 with clinical stage Ⅱ-Ⅲ rectal adenocarcinoma who received TNT followed by proctectomy. Smoking status at diagnosis was categorized as never, current, or former. Primary outcomes were favorable NAR score (< 8) and pCR (ypT0N0). Among 1767 patients, 49.7% were never smokers, 30.5% former, and 19.8% current smokers. Rates of favorable NAR score and pCR were highest among never smokers (33.4 and 21.7%), intermediate among former smokers (28.8 and 19.9%), and lowest among current smokers (25.5 and 16.3%). On multivariable analysis, current smoking was associated with lower odds of favorable NAR score than was never smoking (odds ratio 0.59; 95% confidence interval 0.40-0.86). A similar trend was seen for pCR, though this did not reach statistical significance (odds ratio 0.58; 95% confidence interval 0.34-1.00). Former smoking was not significantly different from never smoking in terms of a favorable NAR score or pCR. Current smoking status was independently associated with lower rates of response to TNT in locally advanced rectal cancer, whereas former smoking was not when compared with never smoking. These findings identify active tobacco exposure as a potential modifiable risk factor.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Chemokine receptor CXCR2 and plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 (PAI-1) are incipient biomarkers across various cancers. Despite their seemingly antithetical effects in the immune microenvironment, CXCR2 and PAI-1 have yet to be explored in tandem in colorectal adenocarcinoma (CRC). We compared their peritumoral expression by immunohistochemistry (IHC) to prognostic features in CRC, in both treated and untreated settings. CXCR2 and PAI-1 IHC were performed on representative sections from 192 untreated and 48 treated CRC resection specimens. The extent of peritumoral inflammation on H&E (score 0-3), CXCR2 staining in peritumoral inflammatory cells (score 0-3), and PAI-1 staining in stroma (high vs. low) and tumor (positive vs. negative) were compared to each other and to clinicopathologic features. Survival analyses used Kaplan-Meier estimation. In both untreated and treated CRC, increased peritumoral inflammation was associated with lower pT/pN stage, fewer positive lymph nodes, and higher CXCR2 scores. In untreated CRC, higher CXCR2 scores correlated with absence of tumor deposits, lower clinical stage, and fewer positive lymph nodes. High stromal PAI-1 correlated with higher tumor bud count/score and positive lymph nodes. In treated CRC, high stromal PAI-1 was associated with higher CXCR2 scores, a trend also seen in a subset of untreated tumors with favorable prognostic features. Patients with greater inflammation scores showed longer recurrence-free survival. CXCR2 expression is associated with favorable prognostic features regardless of prior therapy. In untreated CRC, stromal PAI-1 expression is associated with less favorable features. These findings are notable, as anti-PAI-1 small molecule inhibitors are under investigation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC), one of the most prevalent and lethal malignancies worldwide, is driven by complex genetic and molecular alterations. In this study, we aimed to identify the functional role of spindle and kinetochore associated complex subunit 1 (SKA1) and uncover its novel mechanism that promotes CRC progression. Bioinformatic TCGA analysis, paired clinical tissue detection and immunohistochemistry confirmed the elevated SKA1 expression in CRC lesions; high SKA1 expression correlates with unfavorable overall survival in CRC patients. Besides, SKA1 overexpression expedited proliferation, accelerated cell cycle G1/S transition, and enhanced migration and invasion, while suppressing apoptosis in CRC cells, which could be reversed by SKA1 silencing. In vivo, SKA1 silencing suppressed tumor growth in a LoVo cell subcutaneous xenograft nude mouse model, whereas SKA1 overexpression accelerated tumor progression in those derived from SW480 cells. Furthermore, ribosomal protein L8 (RPL8) was identified to interact with SKA1 and mediate the tumor-promoting effects. Silencing RPL8 abolished SKA1-driven proliferation and survival advantages, indicating its downstream role. Subsequently, our studies validated that TATA-box binding protein associated factor 1 (TAF1) directly binds to the SKA1 promoter and transcriptionally activates SKA1 expression. Loss of TAF1 attenuated CRC cell proliferation and invasion, whereas SKA1 overexpression rescued these inhibitory effects. Besides, the truncation mutation of the TAF1 N-terminal TAND domain abolished its binding to the SKA1 promoter and eliminated its transactivation capacity. Collectively, our findings define a novel TAF1/SKA1/RPL8 regulatory axis that critically drives CRC progression, highlighting SKA1 as a potential target and providing new insights into the mechanisms underlying CRC development and progression.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The mechanisms of resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) in microsatellite-stable (MSS) colorectal cancer (CRC) have 3 interconnected levels, which provide information to guide different biomarker strategies. There is a critical clinical need, as objective response rates continue to be < 10%. We suggest a biomarker stratification model on the basis of clinical actionability. POLE/POLD1 mutations, recommended by the NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology for Colon Cancer (Version 1.2025), represent true genomic "hard" indicators. While the benefit of ICI-containing combination regimens was predicted by the Immunoscore-IC in the AtezoTRIBE trial, the ANICCA-class II study recently questioned the value of anti-PD-1 monotherapy. Defects in homologous recombination repair HRR), ctDNA kinetics and subtyping of CMS1 show promise but need to be prospectively validated. TMB, however, has shown no consistent value as a single biomarker, and MSIs, such as transcriptomic signatures or PD-L1 combined positive scores, have not been proven to be useful. Future prospects involve multiomics algorithms that integrate immune profiling and stromal determinants, liver-directed sensitizing approaches and serial ctDNA monitoring of acquired resistance as viable strategies for further patient selection. These data collectively pave the way toward moving away from the "cold tumor" paradigm and toward dynamic, host-integrated testing for precision immunotherapy in MSS CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Oxaliplatin-induced peripheral neuropathy (OIPN) is a dose-limiting adverse effect of FOLFOX chemotherapy in colorectal cancer (CRC) patients. We aimed to evaluate the protective effect of N-acetylcysteine (NAC) against OIPN. Additionally, we investigated its mechanistic effects on serum biomarkers including total antioxidant capacity (TAC), interleukin-6 (IL-6), and neurotensin. Forty-six patients with stage III or high-risk stage II CRC receiving adjuvant modified FOLFOX-6 chemotherapy were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to receive either oral NAC 1200 mg (effervescent tablets or granules) or placebo one hour before each oxaliplatin infusion for four cycles. Serum levels of TAC, IL-6, and neurotensin were measured before and after treatment. Neuropathy was assessed using the FACT/GOG-NTX-12 and NCI-CTCAE scales, and pain was estimated by using the Brief Pain Inventory-Short Form. Neurotensin was significantly decreased in the NAC group compared to controls after treatment (P < 0.001), and was significantly lower post-treatment versus pre-treatment in the NAC group (P = 0.001). IL-6 was significantly reduced in the NAC group versus controls after treatment (P < 0.001), and significantly decreased post-treatment in both groups (P < 0.05). FACT/GOG-NTX-12 and NCI-CTCAE scores were significantly lower in the NAC group at the end of the first two cycles and at the end of treatment (P < 0.05). Pain interference, but not pain severity, was significantly reduced in the NAC group at both time points (P < 0.001). NAC administration during FOLFOX chemotherapy significantly reduced OIPN severity, pain interference, and serum levels of IL-6 and neurotensin, suggesting both clinical and mechanistic neuroprotective effects. The study was is registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (ID: NCT07391163).

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To evaluate the prognostic impact of chemotherapy dose intensity and frailty indices-including the laboratory-based Frailty Index (FI-Lab)-on survival in older adults with stage II-III colon cancer receiving adjuvant chemotherapy. This retrospective study included 94 patients aged ≥ 65 years with stage II (high-risk) or stage III colon cancer treated with adjuvant chemotherapy after curative surgery. Frailty was assessed using FI-Lab with a predefined cut-off of 0.25. Measures included the G8 geriatric screening tool, modified 5-item Frailty Index (mFI-5), and Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI). Patients were categorised as optimal dose completed, optimal dose started with subsequent reduction, or not started at the optimal dose. Overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS) were analysed using Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression models. With a median follow-up of 70 months, 28 recurrences (29.8%) and 22 deaths (23.4%) occurred. FI-Lab ≥ 0.25 independently predicted inferior OS (HR: 3.73; p = 0.023) and DFS (HR: 2.81; p = 0.029). G8, mFI-5, and CCI were not independently associated with survival. Dose initiation strategy was also independently associated with outcomes. Compared with the optimal dose completed group, patients not started at the optimal dose had worse OS (HR: 14.41; p = 0.011) and DFS (HR: 5.16; p = 0.013), whereas dose reduction after optimal initiation was not associated with survival. Laboratory-based frailty and initial dose intensity independently predicted survival in older adults receiving adjuvant chemotherapy for colon cancer. These findings support individualised treatment strategies integrating biological reserve and early treatment intensity.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Stoma outlet obstruction (SOO) is a notable complication following diverting loop ileostomy (DLI) for colorectal cancer. However, no definitive risk factors for SOO have been identified. This study aimed to determine the risk factors associated with SOO. This retrospective study included 167 consecutive patients who underwent elective colorectal cancer surgery with DLI at Chiba University Hospital between January 2010 and October 2024. We evaluated the patient, tumor, and surgical factors along with the computed tomography-based anatomical measurements. These included rectus abdominis muscle (RAM) thickness, subcutaneous adipose tissue (SAT) thickness, stoma penetration angles, penetration site through the RAM, and proximal limb orientation measurements. SOO occurred in 21 (12.6%) patients. A univariate analysis demonstrated that central penetration of the RAM (P = 0.01) and caudal orientation of the proximal limb (P = 0.02) were significantly associated with SOO length. A multivariable logistic regression analysis indicated that stoma penetration through the central portion of the RAM was an independent risk factor for SOO (odds ratio, 3.38; 95% CI], 1.26-10.1; P = 0.02). Central RAM penetration was an independent risk factor for SOO. As the penetration site is a modifiable technical factor, avoiding the central RAM when creating the DLI may reduce the risk of SOO.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Patient and general population health state values (HSVs) often diverge, yet evidence on the updated SF-6D is scarce. This study compared HSVs for identical SF-6Dv2 health states elicited from cancer patients and the general population using the composite time trade-off (cTTO) method. Data were drawn from two valuation studies in Quebec, Canada: a general population sample completing an online panel (n = 1,179) and patients with breast or colorectal cancer first assessed via face-to-face interviews and subsequently online (n = 202). HSVs for 156 SF-6Dv2 health states were elicited using the cTTO method. Differences in HSVs were examined across health state severity categories using multivariate regression methods, both unadjusted and adjusted for sociodemographic characteristics. Sample-type and dimension-level analyses were also conducted. Cancer patients reported lower mean HSVs than the general population (0.320 vs. 0.384), with a significant raw mean difference of -0.063 and a significant adjusted mean difference of -0.076. For mild and moderate health states, patients assigned slightly higher utilities, but differences were not statistically significant after adjustment, whereas for severe and worst health states, patients reported substantially lower HSVs (adjusted differences -0.330 and -0.319, respectively). Sample-type analyses showed that, on average, cancer patients assigned HSVs 0.080 lower than the general population in the full sample. In the restricted sample of pre-chemotherapy observations with complete sociodemographic data, the difference was 0.115 before adjustment and 0.107 after adjustment. Patients had larger utility decrements across all levels of social functioning (SF), mental health (MH), and vitality (VT). However, the differences were statistically significant only for the two estimable social functioning contrasts (SF4 and SF5) and one vitality level (VT3), with no statistically significant differences observed for MH. The range of estimated SF-6Dv2 HSVs was narrower for the general population (-0.353 to 1) than for cancer patients (-0.575 to 1). Significant differences in SF-6Dv2 HSVs were observed by sample type and across health state severity levels. Economic evaluation outcomes may differ when using general population versus patient HSVs, depending on the specific health-related quality of life dimensions targeted by the intervention.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Faecal extracellular vesicles (EVs) provide disease-relevant molecular information for non-invasive colorectal cancer (CRC) analysis. However, sensitive EV surface protein profiling remains challenging because low-abundance targets are obscured by heterogeneous vesicles and complex matrices. Here, an integrated cascade-amplified microfluidic biosensor was developed for reconfigurable profiling of EV surface proteins, combining EV capture, signal amplification, and fluorescence detection in a single workflow. CD63 aptamer-functionalized Y-shaped micropillar arrays capture EVs. Target-specific aptamer-initiator conjugates convert protein recognition into nucleic-acid outputs to trigger entropy-driven catalysis (EDC) and DNAzyme amplification. After magnetic removal of residual probes, output strands activate secondary DNAzyme-mediated amplification in the detection chamber to generate amplified fluorescence signals. Based on this modular target-trigger design, the platform enables reconfigurable multi-marker profiling of EpCAM, EGFR, and HSP70, with limits of detection at 98, 115, and 103 particles mL

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Circumferential resection margin (CRM) involvement after intersphincteric resection (ISR) is uncommon but clinically important. We evaluated the association of CRM status and adverse histopathologic features with recurrence after ISR following neoadjuvant concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CCRT). From 2011 to 2022, 520 patients underwent ISR for ultra-low rectal cancer (≤3 cm from the anal verge) at a single tertiary center. Among them, 326 who received CCRT were analyzed. Clinicopathologic variables were evaluated in relation to disease-free survival (DFS), local recurrence-free survival (LRFS), and distant recurrence-free survival (DRFS). Multivariable Cox regression evaluated adjusted associations. CRM involvement occurred in 8 patients (2.5%). Fifty-four patients (16.6%) developed recurrence: 17 local only, 34 distant only, and 3 both. Five-year DFS, LRFS, DRFS, and overall survival were 74.8%, 87.5%, 85.5%, and 91.4%, respectively. CRM involvement was associated with inferior DFS (45.0% CRM involvement was associated predominantly with poorer local control after ISR following CCRT, whereas adverse microscopic features, particularly perineural invasion, showed broader associations with both local and distant recurrence. The combined assessment of CRM status and microscopic tumor invasiveness may therefore provide complementary prognostic information after ISR for ultra-low rectal cancer.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
This study aimed to interrogate the functional role of hyaluronan-mediated motility receptor (HMMR) in modulating proliferative, migratory, and invasive phenotypes of colorectal cancer (CRC) cells, with an emphasis on its relationship with the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling cascade. Protein expression levels of HMMR and components of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway were comparatively analyzed in an exploratory paired tissue series of colorectal tumors and adjacent non-neoplastic tissues (n = 5) via Western blotting and immunohistochemistry. Functional perturbation was achieved through RNA interference and plasmid-mediated overexpression of HMMR in HCT-15 cells. Cellular behaviors were quantitatively assessed using Cell Counting Kit-8 viability assays, flow cytometric analysis of cell cycle distribution, and motility/invasion assays. The functional involvement of the PI3K pathway was examined through fixed-dose pharmacological modulation using an inhibitor and an agonist. HMMR expression was elevated in the paired CRC tissues relative to adjacent controls, accompanied by increased phosphorylation of PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway components. Silencing of HMMR significantly reduced HCT-15 cell viability over a 24-72 h interval (p < 0.01), induced G1-phase arrest (p < 0.05), and attenuated migratory and invasive phenotypes (p < 0.01), whereas ectopic HMMR expression produced the opposite pattern. Pharmacological pathway modulation attenuated or partially rescued HMMR-associated phenotypes, supporting functional involvement of PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling. Within the experimental scope of this study, HMMR acts as a functional contributor to malignant phenotypes in HCT-15 CRC cells and is associated with PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway activation. These findings support a mechanistic relationship between HMMR expression and pathway activity without establishing a direct physical interaction between HMMR and individual pathway proteins.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The current American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC8) manual grades colorectal adenocarcinoma (CRC) based on the percentage of gland formation. The World Health Organization 5th ed (WHO5) and 6th ed (WHO6) grade based on the least differentiated component; WHO6 specifies a minimum 0.196 mm Five gastrointestinal pathologists reviewed 100 scanned CRC slides and graded each slide per the provided criteria in (a) WHO5, (b) WHO6, (c) AJCC8 and (d) their clinical practice. A post-survey questionnaire was also provided. The Fleiss multirater kappa among the five reviewers was similar using WHO6 (0.730, P < 0.001) and two-tiered (low vs. high) AJCC8 (0.731, P < 0.001) and was higher than WHO5 (0.655, P < 0.001) grading criteria; the agreement was substantial for all 3 grading systems. Significantly more tumours were called high-grade when using WHO6 (average: 34.4 cases) and WHO5 (average: 33.6 cases) as compared to AJCC8 (average: 11.8 cases) grading criteria (P < 0.01). All reviewers were unanimous in handling certain scenarios (e.g. discounting invasive front tumour buds with WHO grading), but were discordant on certain scenarios (e.g. assessment of stroma-rich areas). While inter-observer agreement improved with WHO6 versus WHO5, the persistent upgrading of tumours using the WHO scheme may affect treatment algorithms. Synchronization of grading criteria with validation in prospective studies with clinical outcomes is crucial.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Astragali Radix (HQ) and Curcumae Rhizoma (EZ), collectively termed AC, are commonly used as an herb pair in Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) for colorectal cancer (CRC). Although AC has been used as an adjuvant to chemotherapy, the molecular basis by which it enhances the efficacy of 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) remains incompletely defined. The antitumor effect of AC alone and in combination with 5-FU was evaluated in a HCT116 xenograft mouse model and in CRC cell lines with different genetic backgrounds. Potential systemic toxicity was assessed using serum biochemical markers. Transcriptomic changes induced by AC were analyzed by RNA sequencing and integrated with network pharmacology and The Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) (GSE17536, GSE17537, GSE41258, GSE20916). Key targets were validated by Western blotting and immunofluorescence. Cell viability, drug interaction, apoptosis, cell-cycle distribution and DNA damage were assessed using CCK-8 assays, Synergy Finder analysis, flow cytometry, and γ-H2AX staining. Bioavailable AC-derived constituents were characterized by UPLC-QTOF-MS, and candidate active compounds were further evaluated by molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, cellular thermal shift assay, and functional validation. AC potentiated the antitumor efficacy of 5-FU in vivo and did not exacerbate 5-FU-associated hepatic or renal biochemical toxicity under the tested conditions. In vitro, AC-containing serum extracts inhibited CRC cell viability, induced reversible G2/M-phase arrest, and enhanced 5-FU sensitivity in HCT116, CT26, and HCT15 cells. AC treatment caused limited early apoptosis, whereas delayed apoptosis was observed after prolonged exposure, suggesting that cell-cycle arrest represents the primary early response. RNA-seq and integrative analyses showed that AC suppressed pathways associated with DNA replication, mismatch repair, ribosome biogenesis, and cell-cycle progression. AC downregulated key regulators involved in cell-cycle control, DNA repair, and stress-survival signaling, including PLK1, CDK1, CCNB1, CDC25A, c-JUN, MSH2, BRCA1, and p-AKT. Combination treatment further increased γ-H2AX accumulation and reduced cell-cycle regulatory proteins. Functional validation indicated that c-JUN overexpression partially attenuated AC-mediated 5-FU sensitization, whereas pharmacological AKT inhibition partially mimicked the sensitizing effect of AC. Among the serum-exposed constituents, Demethoxycurcumin and Kumatakenin were identified as bioavailable active compounds that partially recapitulated the effects of AC by inducing G2/M-phase arrest and enhancing the antiproliferative activity of 5-FU. Molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and CETSA supported their target engagement with cell-cycle regulators, particularly CCNB1 and CDK1. AC enhances the therapeutic efficacy of 5-FU in CRC by weakening DNA repair-cell-cycle coordination and stress-survival signaling, thereby increasing 5-FU-induced DNA damage and promoting cell-cycle arrest. Demethoxycurcumin and Kumatakenin may represent important bioavailable contributors to this chemosensitizing effect, although the complete AC extract likely acts through multi-component and multi-target mechanisms. These findings provide mechanistic support for the use of AC as an adjunctive strategy to improve 5-FU-based chemotherapy in CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The purpose of this study was to evaluate Emergency Department (ED) utilization and associated outcomes among patients with gastrointestinal (GI) cancers during the first year following diagnosis. This retrospective study was conducted at a comprehensive cancer center and included patients with GI cancers diagnosed between 2018 and 2022 who received chemotherapy. Data collected included baseline characteristics, cancer type and stage, initial treatment plan, and prescribed chemotherapy with number of cycles received. Also, we evaluated ED visits frequency, presenting complaints, hospital admissions, and 1-year mortality. During the study period, a total of 2278 patients were diagnosed with GI cancers and received chemotherapy. The mean age was 57 ± 12.4 (SD), 57.6% were males, and 23.6% were smokers. The majority had colon cancer (n = 769, 33.7%) and rectal cancer (n = 630, 27.6%). The most common Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) stage was distant (43.7%). Renal and hepatic dysfunction at baseline were recorded in 5.6% and 2.8%, respectively. Surgery combined with chemotherapy was the most common treatment plan (43.2%), and patients received a median (IQR) of 8 (5-12) chemotherapy cycles. Among those patients, 2007 (88.1%) required at least one ED visit, with a median (IQR) of 3 (1-6) visits/patient, and 1971 (86.5%) required at least one hospital admission. The most frequently reported chief complaints were musculoskeletal/pain, GI symptoms, and infections. The 1-year mortality rate was 48.8%. In a large cohort of patients with GI cancers, the majority required ED visits within the first-year following diagnosis, many of which resulted in hospital admissions. Most visits were for musculoskeletal/pain and GI symptoms.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
In restorative total mesorectal excision (TME), transanal rectal transection and single-stapled anastomosis (TTSS) provide an access route that enables transanal NOSE before anastomosis. We evaluated wound complications and postoperative pain associated with SS-NOSE strategy compared with conventional double-stapled anastomosis and transabdominal specimen extraction. This single-center, retrospective, propensity score-matched (PSM) cohort study included patients undergoing TME for low rectal cancer, as defined by the Low Rectal Cancer Development Program (LOREC), between January 2017 and January 2023. The primary endpoint was the 30-day wound complications rate in the control and in the SS-NOSE groups. Secondary endpoints included differences in postoperative pain at 24, 48, and 72 h, measured using the Numerical Rating Scale (NRS), and the need for opioid rescue therapy during hospitalization. The unmatched analysis included 303 patients (104 SS-NOSE and 199 controls). After PSM, 208 patients were compared. The 30-day wound complications was lower in the SS-NOSE group (2.9% vs. 14.4%; p = 0.003). SS-NOSE was an independent protective factors against wound complications at multivariable analysis (OR: 0.17; 95% CI 0.05 to 0.62; p = 0.007). Postoperative pain was improved at 24 and 48 h (0 [0-1] vs. 1 [0-3]; p = 0.005; 0 [0-1] vs 0 [0-2]; p< 0.0001) and comparable at 72 h after surgery (0 [0-0] vs. 0 [0-0]; p = 0.583). No significant difference was found in opioid rescue therapy requirements and overall postoperative complications. Transanal NOSE, enabled by TTSS, was associated with fewer wound complications and lower early postoperative pain compared with conventional double-stapled anastomosis and transabdominal specimen extraction following restorative TME for low rectal cancer.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
In patients with RAS/BRAF wild-type (WT) metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC), anti-epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) monoclonal antibodies combined with chemotherapy represent an established first-line option and may provide clinically meaningful tumor shrinkage. However, acquired resistance may develop through the emergence of mechanism/s of acquired resistance. After progression to first- and second-line regimens, the prognosis of patients with mCRC remains poor. Available later-line options exhibit a cytostatic activity and are associated with limited objective response rate (ORR). Of note, the dynamic decay of resistant subclones after withdrawal of EGFR blockade supports the rationale to explore anti-EGFR rechallenge therapy. ROMANCE trial is a multicenter, randomized phase II study. Overall, 150 patients with mCRC with circulating tumor RAS/BRAF/EGFR/PIK3CA exon 20/MAP2K1/MET WT and HER2 nonamplified (negative hyperselected tumors) mCRC, at baseline liquid biopsy, will be randomized 1:1 to irinotecan plus cetuximab rechallenge compared with trifluridine/tipiracil plus bevacizumab as third-line therapy. The primary endpoint is ORR assessed by Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors 1.1 by blinded independent central review; secondary endpoints include progression-free survival, overall survival, safety, and quality of life. Given the limited ORRs achieved with currently available options after second-line treatment for refractory mCRC, strategies capable of inducing clinically meaningful tumor shrinkage are urgently required. ROMANCE will evaluate whether cetuximab plus irinotecan retreatment can improve ORR compared with standard third-line trifluridine/tipiracil plus bevacizumab in patients with circulating tumor DNA-negative hyperselected mCRC and will clarify the role of anti-EGFR rechallenge in the continuum of care of refractory mCRC. This trial is registered at clinicaltrials.gov (NCT07381764).

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Primary liver tumors such as hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), and colorectal cancer liver metastases, can be treated with liver thermal ablation (LTA). Current evidence comparing percutaneous LTA (P-LTA) and laparoscopic LTA (L-LTA) is inconclusive, and data on lesions in the posterosuperior (PS) liver segments are scarce. This study aimed to compare early local recurrence rates between percutaneous and laparoscopic thermal ablation, with a focus on PS liver segments. This single-centre retrospective study included all consecutive patients treated with P-LTA or L-LTA between 2010 and 2024. The primary outcome was early local recurrence (≤ 6 months); secondary outcomes were subgroup analyses of HCC nodules and microwave ablation-treated nodules. The study included 101 nodules in 69 patients. Overall morbidity was higher after L-LTA, whereas chronic liver disease was more common among P-LTA patients. Early local recurrence was significantly lower after L-LTA (7% vs. 25%), and this difference was accentuated in the PS liver segments (4% vs. 33%). Multivariable analysis identified the percutaneous approach and a lesion size > 3 cm as predictors of early local recurrence. L-LTA appears more effective in reducing early local recurrence, particularly in the PS segments, although P-LTA remains less invasive. Prospective multicentre studies are needed to validate these findings.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Large (≥10cm) near-circumferential and circumferential colorectal endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) carries substantial stricture risk, with no established prophylactic strategy. We describe a reconstructive suturing technique for immediate defect closure and report its feasibility and clinical outcomes. Consecutive patients undergoing reconstructive endoscopic suturing after ESD of colorectal lesions ≥10 cm with ≥90% circumferential involvement were analyzed. Closure was performed in patients who consented to suturing. Primary outcomes were technical feasibility in defects elected for closure, adverse events, and symptomatic stricture requiring dilatation. Secondary outcomes included post-polypectomy syndrome, delayed bleeding, perforation, length of hospital stay, resection outcomes, and dissection speed. Nineteen patients underwent suturing (median specimen length 153 mm; 36.8% fully circumferential). Technical feasibility was 100% in those elected to be closed, with a median of 11 anchors and a median suturing time of 23 minutes (IQR: 14-27). En-bloc and R0 resection were 100%. No delayed bleeding, perforation, suturing-related adverse events, or symptomatic strictures occurred during a median follow-up of 30 months (planned follow-up completed in all patients). Median hospital stay was 3 days. In a contemporary (≥2019) reference comparison, symptomatic stricture occurred in 0/19 sutured versus 8/15 (53.3%) non-sutured patients, whose lesions were larger. Reconstructive endoscopic suturing was feasible and safe in defects selected for closure within an exceptionally high-risk cohort and showed a promising signal against post-ESD stricture, warranting prospective multicenter validation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Neoadjuvant immune checkpoint blockade induces high pathological response rates in patients with locally advanced mismatch repair-deficient (dMMR) colon cancer, yet long-term survival outcomes have not been established. Previously, we reported safety (a primary endpoint) and pathological response (a secondary endpoint) data from the NICHE-2 trial. Here, we report the primary efficacy endpoint of 3-year disease-free survival and the exploratory endpoint of 5-year overall survival. In this single-arm, multicentre, phase 2, NICHE-2 trial, patients with previously untreated, clinical stage 2 or 3, resectable dMMR colon cancer received a single dose of intravenous ipilimumab (1 mg per kg) on day 1, and two doses of intravenous nivolumab (3 mg per kg) on days 1 and 15, followed by surgery in one of the six participating hospitals in the Netherlands. Here, we report the independent primary efficacy endpoint of 3-year disease-free survival (time from surgery until disease recurrence or death from any cause) and the secondary endpoint of circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) analysis. Overall survival (time from study enrolment until death from any cause) is reported as an exploratory post-hoc analysis. All endpoints were assessed in the per-protocol population (patients who met the eligibility criteria and received at least one cycle of therapy). The study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT03026140, and has completed accrual. From July 4, 2017, to July 18, 2022, 123 patients were screened, of whom 115 were treated and 111 were included in the per-protocol population. At the data cutoff (June 19, 2026), the postoperative median follow-up was 58·7 months (IQR 49·0-72·9). The 3-year disease-free survival was 100% (97·5% CI 100-100). After a median follow-up of 60·4 months (IQR 50·6-74·1), calculated from time of study enrolment, the 5-year overall survival was 100% (95% CI 100-100). In patients with available plasma samples, ctDNA was detected in 99 (92%) of 108 patients at baseline, and ctDNA clearance was observed in 44 (45%) of 98 patients after the first cycle in week 2 and in 80 (82%) of 97 patients after the second cycle before surgery. In patients with a pathological near-complete response and complete response, presurgery ctDNA clearance was observed in 19 (70%) of 27 patients and 60 (92%) of 65 patients, respectively. Assessment for minimal residual disease after surgery revealed that all patients were ctDNA negative. In patients with locally advanced dMMR colon cancer, treatment with ipilimumab and nivolumab before surgery resulted in a 3-year disease-free survival and 5-year overall survival of 100%. These findings support neoadjuvant nivolumab plus ipilimumab as a potential standard of care for patients with locally advanced dMMR colon cancer. Bristol Myers Squibb.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
It is unknown whether the preoperative anesthesiological risk assessment interacts with patient age in colorectal cancer (CRC) to increase the risk of early postoperative mortality beyond that explained by the independent effects of age and anesthesiological risk assessment. We conducted a nationwide cohort study (2014-2023) of all Danish non-metastatic CRC patients (UICC pathological TNM I-III) aged 70 or more years at time of surgery (n = 15,673). To analyse perioperative risk, we used the American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) Physical Status Classification system score. The study cohort was stratified by age at CRC surgery (70-79, 80+) and ASA classification (I, II, III). We estimated mortality rates per 1000 person-days, and calculated interaction contrasts as a measure of the excess mortality rate not explained by the independent effects of age or ASA classification. 90-day overall survival was lower in patients aged ≥80 years compared with those aged 70-79 years (94.0% vs. 97.9%). Increasing ASA classification was associated with progressively lower survival, with 90-day survival of 98.9% for ASA I, 97.9% for ASA II, and 93.1% for ASA III. Interaction analyses demonstrated that the combined effect of age and ASA classification exceeded their independent effects, with interaction contributing 21% of the mortality rate in ASA II patients aged ≥80 years and 36% in ASA III patients aged ≥80 years. Old CRC patients assessed as ASA III have a high risk of perioperative mortality and may benefit from risk factor reductions or high intensity postoperative monitoring to reduce mortality.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer liver metastasis (CRLM) is a major cause of mortality in colorectal cancer (CRC) and develops within a heterogeneous tumor microenvironment (TME). How immune, stromal, and metabolic programs differ between primary CRC and matched liver metastases remains incompletely resolved. We analyzed publicly available single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data from GSE178318 (15 specimens from six patients: six primary CRC samples, six matched liver metastases, and three peripheral-blood mononuclear cell samples) together with bulk RNA-seq data from GSE50760 (54 samples from 18 patients spanning normal colon, primary CRC, and liver metastasis). The single-cell workflow included quality control, score-based cell-type annotation, patient-level pseudobulk differential expression, pathway/module scoring, ligand-receptor co-expression analysis, and diffusion-map pseudotime. Bulk data were assessed using within-patient paired comparisons, co-expression analysis, and program-level scoring. Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate (FDR) correction was applied for multiple testing. After quality control, 132,915 single cells were retained. Liver metastases showed higher patient-level T/NK-cell fractions and lower malignant epithelial and B/plasma-cell fractions than primary tumors. In paired single-cell pseudobulk analysis, no gene remained significant at the prespecified FDR threshold, although nominal differences suggested extracellular-matrix and metabolic changes. Glycolysis scores were modestly higher and oxidative-phosphorylation scores modestly lower in liver metastases, whereas inflammatory and glycolytic scores were not correlated at the patient-tissue level. Ligand-receptor co-expression was strongest for MIF-CD74, VIM-CD44, and HLA-A-CD8A, with CAF/stromal and myeloid/TAM populations showing high aggregate outgoing scores. Diffusion pseudotime showed increasing EMT/invasion scores and decreasing glycolysis along the inferred transcriptomic ordering; this ordering is descriptive and not a longitudinal lineage. In the bulk cohort, 654 genes differed between liver metastasis and primary tumor, while cross-platform rank concordance was weak (Spearman rho=0.106). Public single-cell and bulk datasets support compartment-associated differences in cellular composition and transcriptional programs in CRLM, with prominent stromal, myeloid, and metabolic features. However, limited patient numbers, cross-sectional sampling, weak cross-platform concordance, and the absence of experimental validation mean that the ligand-receptor and trajectory findings should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating rather than causal or clinically validated.
