ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The oxaliplatin-based therapy regimens for colorectal cancer (CRC) presents a significant challenge to clinical application owing to the severe side effects and drug resistance. To enhance the selectivity and therapeutic efficacy of oxaliplatin, we designed and synthesized a series of platinum (IV) prodrugs by conjugating NF-κB inhibitor EF24 analogs to an oxaliplatin -derived platinum (IV) complex. Among them, the platinum (IV) prodrug 6d demonstrated the most potent inhibitory effect on HCT-116/Oxa cells, 4T1 cells and CT26 cells in both in vitro and in vivo compared to oxaliplatin. Mechanistic studies indicated that 6d could induce significant DNA damage and suppress the MAPK/NF-κB signaling pathway, ultimately leading to CRC cell death. Especially, 6d induced cell death by promoting autophagy through suppressing the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway, and suppressed the expression of PD-L1. More importantly, 6d triggered autophagy to mediate immunogenic cell death (ICD) effect both in vitro and in vivo, thereby eliciting antitumor immune responses. These findings indicate that 6d may represent a potential chemotherapeutic candidate for the treatment of CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Patients undergoing colorectal cancer surgery are at increased risk for postoperative venous thromboembolism (VTE). Several societies recommend extended duration pharmacologic prophylaxis after discharge for selected high-risk patients, but real-world use is inconsistent, and the absolute benefit in the era of minimally invasive surgery and enhanced recovery remains uncertain. We performed a retrospective cohort study of adults undergoing colon or rectal resection for cancer at a single academic center between 2020 and 2023. Patients receiving therapeutic anticoagulation, those with recent VTE or nonmalignant indications for surgery were excluded. Demographic, operative, and oncologic variables were collected along with inpatient and postdischarge VTE prophylaxis practices. Primary outcomes were (1) prescription of extended pharmacologic prophylaxis at discharge and (2) 90-d symptomatic VTE incidence. A total of 177 patients met the inclusion criteria. Most operations were minimally invasive and performed within an Enhanced Recovery After Surgery pathway. Despite the presence of traditional VTE risk factors, only a minority of patients were discharged on extended pharmacologic prophylaxis. Within 90 d, two patients developed symptomatic lower extremity deep vein thrombosis (1.1%); no pulmonary emboli or VTE events were identified. Both patients had high-risk features, including advanced age and emergent surgery. Routine screening imaging was not performed, and all events were clinically detected. In this enhanced recovery after surgery-based colorectal cancer cohort, extended postdischarge VTE prophylaxis was rarely prescribed; yet, the symptomatic VTE rate was low and limited to two high-risk individuals. These findings support a risk-stratified rather than universal approach to extended prophylaxis after colorectal surgery.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Dysregulated wnt/β-catenin signaling cascades drive self-renewal, proliferation, differentiation, and therapeutic resistance in cancer stem cells (CSCs), thus contributing to their tumor aggression and poor clinical outcomes. Earlier, we demonstrated that a glucocorticoid receptor (GR)-targeted liposomal formulation carrying dexamethasone (Dex) and the wnt/β-catenin inhibitor FH535 (D1XFH) selectively sensitizes colorectal cancer (CRC) cells and suppresses tumor growth. Herein, we investigate the immuno-therapeutic potential of D1XFH, especially within colorectal CSCs and against tumor recurrence. Our results reveal that D1XFH significantly downregulates CD133 and stemness-associated transcription factors Nanog, Sox2, and Oct4 in CSCs. D1XFH induces selective cytotoxicity by enhancing ROS generation, triggering apoptosis, reducing clonogenic potential, inhibiting cellular migration, and reversing multidrug resistance in CSCs. Co-administration of D1XFH-engineered CSCs and D1XFH into subcutaneous tumor-bearing mice resulted in pronounced tumor regression, accompanied by inhibition of wnt/β-catenin signaling, reversal of EMT, and antitumorigenic immune responses, while improving long-term survival. Additionally, D1XFH treatments post-tumor resection resulted in near-zero tumor recurrence, while zero recurrence was observed even after tumor re-challenge. We observed 250 day long-term survivability with possible resurgence of immune-memory response within tumor-resected, D1XFH-treated mice. Collectively, dual targeting of GR and wnt/β-catenin-driven CSC engineering and immunomodulation is a promising strategy for colorectal cancer therapy.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Accurate real-time classification of colorectal polyps during colonoscopy is essential for risk stratification, therapeutic decision-making, and surveillance planning, with important implications for colorectal cancer prevention, health care costs, and patient burden. Despite advances in optical diagnosis techniques, including virtual chromoendoscopy and magnification, widespread adoption remains limited because of high operator dependency and variable diagnostic accuracy. Existing computer-assisted diagnosis (CADx) systems predominantly provide binary classification of colorectal lesions, thereby constraining their clinical utility for nuanced endoscopic decision-making. This study aims to develop and validate a real-time, multiclass AI-based CADx system capable of classifying colorectal lesions into 5 categories: nonneoplastic lesions, low-grade adenomas, high-grade adenomas, sessile serrated lesions (SSL), and invasive colorectal cancer. This multicenter international study consists of 2 phases: model development and proof-of-concept validation. During the model development phase, a large, diverse dataset of >17,000 deidentified endoscopic images and video frames will be prospectively collected from 8 European centers and 1 Japanese center, capturing a broad spectrum of lesion types and patient demographics. A semisupervised learning framework using contrastive representation learning (SimCLR [simple framework for contrastive learning of visual representations]) will be used to leverage both labeled and unlabeled data, enhancing feature extraction and classification performance. Expert consensus annotation will be used for labeled data. Lesion localization will be supported by an integrated computer-assisted detection (CADe) module, while model interpretability will be facilitated through gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM). Proof-of-concept validation will be conducted using 250 previously unseen lesion images that will be independently assessed by expert endoscopists. The primary outcome is multiclass diagnostic accuracy, with a predefined target accuracy threshold of 85%, alongside sensitivity and specificity for invasive cancer detection. Secondary outcomes include interobserver agreement, performance across demographic and lesion subgroups, and a qualitative analysis of misclassification patterns. All data will be securely managed within a REDCap database, with strict deidentification protocols and plans to generate an open-access research resource. Ethics approval has been obtained at all participating centres. Data transfer agreements have been executed by the majority of collaborating sites, with de-identified polyp images and videos currently being uploaded to a secure central database. This study aims to deliver a clinically applicable, real-time multiclass CADx system that extends beyond current binary AI models and supports more granular, personalized endoscopic decision-making. By integrating semisupervised learning, diverse international data, and explainable AI techniques, this approach has the potential to substantially advance the methodological foundations and clinical utility of AI-assisted optical diagnosis in routine colonoscopy, contributing to improved colorectal cancer prevention and patient care.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Purpose Death receptor (DR) agonism is a promising strategy for cancer treatment, but clinical success has been limited by insufficient efficacy and/or on-target off-tumor toxicity, particularly hepatotoxicity. We hypothesized that restricting DR4 activation to the tumor microenvironment may enhance both therapeutic efficacy and safety. Fibroblast activation protein alpha (FAPα) is overexpressed on cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) within the tumor stroma of several solid cancers, making it an attractive target for conditional activation of DR4 on tumor cells. Experimental Design DuoBody-FAPαxDR4 is an Fc-silenced IgG1 bispecific antibody that binds to DR4 on tumor cells and FAPα on CAFs. Functional activity of DuoBody-FAPαxDR4 was assessed in tumor cell lines and colorectal carcinoma (CRC) patient-derived organoids (PDOs) using viability and bioluminescent reporter assays. Toxicity was tested using human primary liver spheroids in vitro. In vivo, antitumor activity was evaluated in patient-derived xenograft (PDX) models and models for spontaneous multiorgan metastasis by implantation of CRC-derived organoids into the cecum. Results DuoBody-FAPαxDR4 localized to the fibroblast-tumor cell interface, where it induced conditional caspase-8 activation and cytotoxicity in DR4-expressing tumor cells while sparing the fibroblasts. DuoBody-FAPαxDR4 did not induce cytotoxicity in human primary liver spheroids. In vivo, DuoBody-FAPαxDR4 demonstrated potent antitumor activity in PDX models and in mouse models of multiorgan metastases of CRC. Conclusions DuoBody-FAPαxDR4 is a novel bispecific antibody that conditionally activates DR4 on cancer cells exclusively in the presence of FAPα-expressing cells, resulting in targeted apoptosis and antitumor activity. These findings supported the initiation of a first-in-human trial in patients with solid tumors.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Traditional postoperative outcomes may not fully reflect recovery after gastrointestinal (GI) cancer surgery. Days at home (DAH) is a patient-centered metric that integrates survival, complications, and health care use. To characterize and identify an optimal postoperative observation window and validate DAH after elective GI cancer surgery. This was a population-based retrospective cohort study from 2003 to 2021 in Ontario, Canada. Included were adults 18 years and older who underwent elective surgery for GI cancer. Patients were excluded if they were long-term care residents at baseline, underwent emergency surgery, or had another cancer diagnosis within a 2-year lookback. Study data were analyzed from April to November 2025. Covariates explored were age, sex, frailty, comorbidity burden, income quintile, cancer site, histology, metastatic disease, neoadjuvant therapy, procedure type, operative approach, and hospital volume. The primary outcome was DAH, defined as days alive and out of health care institutions and assessed at 30, 90, 180, and 365 days. Death during the observation window resulted in a DAH = 0. DAH after surgery at 90 days (DAH-90) was established as an optimal window, based on the proportion of zeros and variability, while considering clinical pathways in GI cancer. Exploratory multivariable quantile regression examined patient, cancer, and treatment factors associated with DAH-90. Quantile plots evaluated these associations across the distribution of DAH-90. Validity was explored through associations with major morbidity (construct validity) and 1-year mortality (criterion validity). Among 91 270 operations in 89 378 participants (mean [SD] age, 67.3 [12.2] years; 51 343 male [56.2%]), median (IQR) DAH-90 was 82 (77-85) days. DAH-90 varied across cancer site, histology, and procedure. Median (IQR) DAH-90 was lowest for esophageal cancer (76 [63-80] days) and highest for small-bowel cancer (84 [80-86] days). In multivariable quantile regression, preoperative frailty was associated with 2.6 fewer DAH-90 (95% CI, 2.3-2.9 fewer days), whereas laparoscopic approach was associated with 3.0 more DAH-90 (95% CI, 2.9-3.1 more days). DAH-90 was lower among patients with major morbidity (median [IQR], 70 [41-79] days vs 83 [80-85] days; P < .001) and among patients who died within 1 year (median, 62 [0-80] days vs 83 [78-85] days; P < .001). Results of this study suggest that DAH-90 was found to be a valid and clinically meaningful outcome after GI cancer surgery. These findings support the use of DAH-90 in patient counseling, quality assessment, and future GI cancer surgery research.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) screening is suboptimal among people in traditionally underserved populations, many of whom receive primary care at federally qualified health centers (FQHCs). Mailed fecal immunochemical test (FIT) outreach improves screening, especially in underserved populations, but questions remain about impact over time. To evaluate the effectiveness of centralized annual mailed FIT outreach delivered over 3 years to increase CRC screening in FQHCs. This cluster randomized clinical trial was conducted between June 1, 2021, and May 31, 2024. Sixteen clinics from 2 FQHCs in Southern California were randomly assigned to mailed FIT outreach or usual care for patients aged 50 to 75 years and not up to date with screening. Intervention components followed best practices for mailed FIT outreach and included educational primers, FIT kits, and telephone reminders. The primary outcome was the proportion of individuals up to date with any CRC screening after 3 years of intervention (point prevalence); screening at 2 years was a secondary outcome. Due to a resource constraint-related protocol modification, mailed FIT outreach began earlier in year 3, such that some individuals who completed screening in year 2 were not yet due for repeat FIT. Among 16 clinics serving 20 250 patients, 6 clinics serving 8334 individuals at baseline (4435 aged 55-64 years [53.2%]; 4896 female [58.7%]; 341 Asian [4.1%], 238 Black [2.9%], 2390 Hispanic [28.7%], and 4371 non-Hispanic White [52.4%]) were randomized to intervention and 10 clinics serving 11 916 individuals at baseline (6443 aged 55-64 years [54.1%]; 7250 female [60.8%]; 699 Asian [5.9%], 355 Black [3.0%], 4635 Hispanic [38.9%], and 4436 non-Hispanic White [37.2%]) were randomized to usual care. At year 3, screening was 39.4% (95% CI, 36.3% to 42.6%) in intervention clinics vs 36.5% (95% CI, 31.2% to 42.2%) in usual care clinics, which was not a statistically significant difference (2.9 percentage points; 95% CI, -3.2 to 9.0 percentage points). At year 2, screening was 37.8% (95% CI, 35.2% to 40.4%) in intervention clinics vs 27.0% (95% CI, 21.8% to 32.9%) in usual care clinics (difference, 10.8 percentage points; 95% CI, 4.9 to 16.7 percentage points). This study's findings suggest that centralized mailed FIT outreach could increase CRC screening in FQHCs serving populations with persistent disparities, although maintaining intervention fidelity and providing ongoing implementation support over time are needed for consistent impact. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The clinical course of primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC)-associated inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) after liver transplantation (LTx) varies significantly across studies. This meta-analysis aims to provide a comprehensive estimation of incidence rates (IR) for IBD-related outcomes and PSC recurrence. Online databases (January 2000-June 2025) were searched for studies on PSC patients with or without IBD at LTx. Studies reporting posttransplant outcomes of interest were included. The pooled IR were calculated with the "meta" package (R Studio [V.4.3.2]) using a random effects model. A total of 34 studies (3828 patients; 67% with IBD at transplantation) were included. The IR of preexiting IBD exacerbation was 36.1 per 1000 person-years (95% confidence intervals [CI], 23.0-56.5). Medically refractory IBD requiring colectomy occurred at an IR of 12.4 per 1000 person-years (95% CI, 8.9-17.4). The IRs of colorectal neoplasia and advanced neoplasia were 10.3 (95% CI, 6.4-16.7) and 7.7 (95% CI, 5.6-10.7) per 1000 person-years, respectively. Among posttransplant PSC-only patients, the IR of newly diagnosed IBD was 20.0 (95% CI, 12.0-33.4). PSC recurrence occurred more frequently in PSC-IBD patients (31.9; 95% CI, 25.0-40.5) than in PSC-only patients (21.4; 95% CI, 11.3-40.6), corresponding to an incidence rate ratio of 2.16 (95% CI, 1.72-2.72; P < 0.001). After LTx for PSC, patients remain at substantial risk of colorectal neoplasia and de novo IBD. PSC-IBD is associated with a higher risk of disease recurrence. These findings support continued endoscopic surveillance and close monitoring of IBD activity.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The IVOPAK II study (Interdisciplinary Care with Quality Control in Palliative Treatment of Colorectal Cancer) prospectively evaluated the risk (postoperative complications, mortality) and benefit (overall survival) of multimodal treatment with secondary metastasis resection for initially nonresectable metastatic colorectal carcinoma. A total of 40 patients from 10 centers were enrolled. Patients with quintuple wildtype (K-RAS, N-RAS, BRAF, PIK3CA, ERBB2, MSS) received FOLFIRI plus cetuximab, while patients with RAS-mutation (K-RAS or N-RAS, MSS) received FOLFIRI plus bevacizumab. CT scans were presented at two-month intervals to the interdisciplinary tumor board at the University Hospital Erlangen to assess potentially curative secondary metastatic resection. After a median follow-up of 32 months, outcomes of the multimodally (chemotherapy treatment plus metastasis resection) and the palliatively (only chemotherapy treatment) treated patients were compared. The rate of secondary metastasis resection was 45% (18/40). Overall survival was significantly longer in the multimodal treatment group compared to the palliative treatment group (median 61 vs. 22 months, p=0.002), this also applied to progression-free survival (median 39 vs. 11 months, p=0.018). Clavien-Dindo grade ≥3 morbidity occurred in 28% (5/18) of patients, and 90-day mortality was 6% (1/18). Univariate analyses revealed a significant improvement in overall survival among patients with ECOG performance status 0, solitary metastatic site and multimodal treatment. In multivariate analysis, the ECOG performance status proved to be an independent prognostic factor. Following palliative biomarker-stratified first-line treatment for nonresectable metastatic colorectal carcinoma, the multimodal approach with secondary metastatic resection demonstrated a significant survival benefit.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a major global health burden, with incidence and mortality rates continuing to rise worldwide. By 2040, CRC cases are projected to reach 3.2 million, driven by complex interactions between genetic, environmental, and lifestyle factors. While the molecular mechanisms of CRC have been extensively studied, increasing evidence highlights the critical role of non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs), including microRNAs (miRNAs), long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), and circular RNAs (circRNAs) in regulating tumor progression, immune evasion, and therapeutic resistance. Recent research reveals that ncRNAs not only influence tumor cell behavior but also modulate the tumor microenvironment (TME), particularly by regulating tumor-associated macrophage (TAM) polarization. The balance between pro-inflammatory M1 and pro-tumorigenic M2 macrophages profoundly affects CRC progression and treatment response. Dysregulated ncRNAs, such as miR-934, lncRNA RPPH1, and circPLCE1, promote M2 polarization and metastasis via PI3K/AKT, NF-κB, and STAT3 signaling pathways, while others like miR-195-5p and lncRNA GAS5 favor M1 polarization and inhibit tumor growth. These molecules act through diverse mechanisms, including exosomal transfer, ceRNA interactions, and transcriptional regulation, forming intricate communication networks between CRC cells and immune components. Understanding these ncRNA-mediated pathways provides novel opportunities for therapeutic intervention, enhancing immunotherapy efficacy, and improving diagnostic precision through circulating exosomal ncRNA biomarkers. Collectively, targeting ncRNA-regulated macrophage polarization holds promise for developing next-generation precision therapies and advancing immunomodulatory strategies in CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Late recurrence of colorectal cancer > 5 years after curative resection is uncommon, and anastomotic local recurrence occurring > 0 years postoperatively is exceedingly rare. We report a case of local recurrence presenting as a submucosal tumor (SMT)-like lesion at the anastomotic site 23 years after surgery for rectal cancer. The patient had a history of rectal cancer surgery and treatment with 5-fluorouracil 23 years prior and presented with a positive fecal occult blood test. Colonoscopy revealed a 15 mm SMT-like lesion with a central depression at the rectal anastomosis. Endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) elastography demonstrated marked stiffness, with an elasticity score of 5. EUS-guided tissue acquisition confirmed adenocarcinoma, and immunohistochemical findings supported the local recurrence. The patient subsequently underwent laparoscopic low anterior resection. Histopathological examination of the resected specimen revealed a diverticulum-like structure formed by invagination of the lamina propria into the submucosa at the previous anastomotic site, with adenocarcinoma identified within this structure; as it was similar to the histopathological findings from the initial surgery. Careful long-term follow-up may be warranted, even in patients who remain recurrence-free for > 5 years after surgery, particularly in cases requiring adjuvant chemotherapy. Furthermore, EUS elastography may be a useful diagnostic modality for SMT-like lesions.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The study aimed to assess the feasibility and safety of an exercise-based prehabilitation intervention and explore preliminary clinical outcomes in breast, colorectal, and prostate cancer patients awaiting surgery in a large regional healthcare service. Patients with breast, prostate, or colorectal cancer scheduled for surgery were recruited at a single study centre and randomised (1:1) to prehabilitation or usual care. The intervention involved supervised aerobic exercise training 2-3 days per week before surgery. Usual care involved standard cancer treatment. Feasibility was assessed through recruitment, attendance, adherence, and attrition rates. Safety was evaluated via adverse event monitoring. Exploratory analyses evaluated group-by-time changes in cardiorespiratory fitness, health-related quality of life, and fatigue from baseline to the pre-surgery and post-surgery assessment timepoints, with 30-day post-operative outcomes (complications and length of stay) also collected. Of 47 potentially eligible patients approached and screened, 23 were recruited and randomised, and completed baseline assessments. Twenty participants (prehabilitation n = 11, usual care n = 9) completed the pre- and T1 and T2 assessments. Participants attended an average of 5.25 ± 2.16 prehabilitation sessions. Attendance, adherence, completeness, and attrition rates were 91.3%, 82.6%, 85.7%, and 13%, respectively. Five adverse events were recorded in the prehabilitation group (fatigue, n = 3; muscular pain in the extremities, n = 2); all were grade 1. No significant group-by-time interactions were observed for cardiorespiratory fitness, health-related quality of life, or fatigue. Among participants who commenced prehabilitation, attendance, adherence, and completeness were 91.3%, 82.6%, and 85.7%, respectively. No serious adverse events were observed. Exploratory clinical outcome estimates were imprecise and did not support firm conclusions regarding intervention effectiveness. Recruitment limitations and the small heterogeneous sample also preclude broader conclusions regarding feasibility.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Lynch syndrome is the most common hereditary colorectal cancer syndrome, and colonoscopy remains the cornerstone of prevention. However, surveillance is limited by missed lesions, variable procedural quality, accelerated neoplastic progression, and the continued occurrence of post-colonoscopy colorectal cancers. This review examines gene-specific differences in colorectal cancer and adenoma risk, quality standards for surveillance colonoscopy, emerging artificial intelligence technologies, and complementary non-endoscopic strategies. Contemporary studies conducted in expert settings have reported higher adenoma detection rates, reflecting improvements in colonoscopy quality. At the same time, randomized trials have shown no clear additional benefit from computer-aided detection when added to high-quality colonoscopy. Among complementary strategies, fecal immunochemical testing may support prioritization and risk stratification, although its optimal threshold, testing interval, and safety for postponing colonoscopy remain uncertain. In parallel, blood-based biomarkers for cancer prediction remain exploratory. Future progress will depend on wider implementation of quality-assured surveillance and prospective validation of adjunctive tools that can safely guide colonoscopy timing and reduce the occurrence of post-colonoscopy colorectal cancers.

This retrospective single-center study examined whether PET/CT-derived SUVmax is associated with histopathological subtype and dysplasia grade in incidental colorectal polyps, and whether it can predict advanced colorectal neoplasia. The cohort included patients imaged for non-gastrointestinal indications, suspected colorectal malignancy, or prior colorectal cancer. Advanced neoplasia was defined as adenocarcinoma or advanced adenoma (≥10 mm, villous/tubulovillous histology, or high-grade dysplasia). The 12.3 cutoff is exploratory and requires prospective multicenter validation. FDG negativity does not exclude significant pathology; three adenocarcinomas occurred among PET-negative lesions.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) associated with primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) is a distinct phenotype (PSC-IBD). Data on the safety and effectiveness of advanced IBD therapies on IBD outcomes in PSC-IBD remain limited. A systematic review and meta-analysis assessed the safety and effectiveness of advanced therapies in adults with PSC-IBD. MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane databases and Web of Science were searched to July 2026. The primary outcome was IBD clinical remission. Secondary outcomes included clinical response, corticosteroid-free remission, mucosal healing, adverse event-related treatment discontinuation and colorectal neoplasia. A random-effects model was used for pooled estimates. Five retrospective case-series (n = 394) evaluating infliximab, adalimumab, vedolizumab and tofacitinib were included (median follow-up of 18.4 months). Pooled clinical remission rates were 24.7% (95% CI: 17.2%-33.0%) at 3 months and 28.6% (95% CI: 16.3%-42.6%) at 6-12 months. Corticosteroid-free remission was achieved in 45.4% (95% CI: 33.1%-57.9%) and mucosal healing in 25.6% (95% CI: 13.6%-39.5%). Tofacitinib was associated with a clinical response rate of 59.3% (95% CI: 40.0%-77.2%) and low adverse event rate, in a single available study. Adverse event-related discontinuation occurred in 9.1% (95% CI: 4.4%-15.1%), while 31.8% (95% CI: 25.5%-38.5%) experienced primary non-response or secondary loss of response. The pooled proportion of colorectal neoplasia was 10.5% (12/112; 95% CI: 5.3%-17.1%). Five patients developed colorectal cancer (5/112; 4.3%) and two (2/177; 0.8%) cholangiocarcinoma. Advanced IBD therapies demonstrate modest but encouraging effectiveness and an acceptable safety profile in PSC-IBD; however, the available evidence is limited by retrospective study designs, small sample sizes and substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity. Prospective controlled studies using standardised IBD outcomes are needed to inform optimal therapeutic strategies in this high-risk population. PROSPERO: CRD42024580296.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Oxaliplatin (OXA) is a widely used and effective first-line chemotherapeutic agent for colorectal cancer. However, its therapeutic benefits are often constrained by limited antitumor immune activation and dose-limiting peripheral neurotoxicity. Here, we report that sporoderm-removed particles from Ganoderma lucidum spores (RGLS), a naturally derived bioactive particulate system, orchestrate bidirectional regulation of PINK1/Parkin-mediated mitophagy to simultaneously enhance OXA efficacy and mitigate neurotoxicity. Sporoderm removal remodeled the particle biointerface, improved the hydrophilicity of RGLS, and facilitated the release of bioactive constituents in gastrointestinal fluids, thereby increasing their bioavailability. In tumor tissues, RGLS cooperated with OXA to intensify mitochondrial dysfunction and excessive mitophagy, leading to increased tumor cell death and amplified immunogenic cell death, as indicated by enhanced calreticulin exposure and HMGB1 release. This immunogenic remodeling promoted dendritic cell maturation, increased intratumoral infiltration of CD4+ and CD8+ T cells, and attenuated OXA-induced PD-L1 upregulation, collectively converting immune-cold tumors into immune-hot phenotypes. In contrast, in dorsal root ganglia, RGLS restored OXA-impaired PINK1/Parkin-dependent mitochondrial quality control, reduced mitochondrial reactive oxygen species accumulation, and protected neurons from chemotherapy-induced injury, thereby alleviating peripheral neuropathy. These findings establish sporoderm removal as a biointerface-modulation strategy for transforming Ganoderma lucidum spores into multifunctional therapeutic particles and highlight RGLS as a promising adjuvant platform to improve the therapeutic index of OXA-based colorectal cancer chemotherapy.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The workplace is one of the most important settings influencing adult health and may play a significant role in reducing the burden of cancer. The aim of this review was to explore the potential of workplace-based cancer prevention and to discuss the role of employers and occupational health services in the context of the recommendations of the 5th edition of the European Code Against Cancer (ECAC5). This study was conducted as a narrative literature review. The analysis was based on scientific publications identified through PubMed, as well as reports and documents issued by national and international institutions involved in cancer prevention, health promotion, and occupational health. Available evidence suggests that the workplace can support the implementation of most ECAC5 recommendations by reducing exposure to carcinogenic factors, promoting tobacco and nicotine-free lifestyles, healthy nutrition, physical activity, and limiting alcohol consumption. Studies further indicate that employer-led interventions may increase participation in cancer screening programmes for breast, cervical, and colorectal cancer. Occupational health services may play a particularly important role by providing health education and encouraging participation in secondary prevention during mandatory occupational health examinations. The number of studies directly assessing the effectiveness of workplace-based cancer prevention remains limited, particularly in the Polish setting. Nevertheless, the available evidence indicates that the workplace represents a promising environment for implementing ECAC5 recommendations. Further research is needed, along with the development of system-level solutions aimed at strengthening the role of employers and occupational health services in cancer prevention. Med Pr Work Health Saf. 2026;77(5).

Targeting both tumor cells and microenvironment is a promising anticancer strategy. FGFR1 and VEGFR2 represent important drivers of tumor progression and angiogenesis. We engineered multitarget proteins by fusing DR5‑specific TRAIL DR5-B with SRH and P9 peptides antagonizing VEGFR2 and FGFR1, respectively. SRH-DR5-B, DR5-B-P9, and SRH-DR5-B-P9 fusions demonstrated nanomolar affinity for receptors DR5, VEGFR2, and FGFR1 and reduced viability of FGFR1-positive gastric (MKN-45) and colon (HCT116, COLO 205) adenocarcinoma cells. DR5‑B-P9 and SRH‑DR5‑B‑P9 decreased phospho‑FGFR1 levels in FGF2‑stimulated NIH3T3 fibroblasts and MKN‑45 cells. In a co‑culture of MKN‑45, NIH‑3T3, and bEnd.3 cells, SRH‑DR5‑B‑P9 with gemcitabine showed greater cytotoxicity than DR5‑B. In MKN‑45 xenografts, SRH‑DR5‑B‑P9 inhibited tumor growth more efficiently and durably versus other proteins. Reduced vascular density in SRH‑DR5‑B and SRH‑DR5‑B‑P9‑treated tumors was demonstrated by CD31 immunostaining and by optoacoustic microangiography. PAS+/CD31- staining indicated suppressed vasculogenic mimicry, most pronounced with DR5‑B‑P9 and SRH‑DR5‑B‑P9. FLIM imaging revealed a glycolysis‑to‑oxidative phosphorylation shift in DR5‑B and SRH‑DR5‑B‑P9‑treated tumors, suggesting reprogrammed tumor bioenergetics. In HCT116 xenografts, SRH‑DR5‑B‑P9 suppressed tumor growth and CD31+ and PAS+/CD31- elements density more effectively than DR5‑B, confirming the results from MKN‑45 model. This supports a single‑fusion‑molecule strategy that activates DR5 while inhibiting FGFR1 and VEGFR2 for gastric and colorectal cancer therapy.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Retained rectal foreign bodies are an uncommon but clinically significant surgical emergency. We report the case of a 74-year-old male with multiple medical comorbidities who presented with progressive rectal pain and obstipation several days after an episode of suspected drug-facilitated assault. Plain radiography identified a large metallic aerosol can, and attempts to retrieve it under general anesthesia using surgical clamps and a magnetic probe failed. Intraoperative fluoroscopy demonstrated that the can had migrated proximal to the rectosigmoid junction into the left colon, precluding transanal extraction. The patient underwent exploratory laparotomy with longitudinal colotomy, permitting safe removal of the foreign body without evidence of perforation or visceral injury. This case illustrates the critical role of intraoperative fluoroscopy when digital examination fails, the indications for operative intervention in proximally migrated foreign bodies, and the importance of considering drug-facilitated assault as an etiology.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
We sought to evaluate the associations of post-diagnostic consumption of flavonoids and flavonoid-rich foods with survival among patients with stage III colon cancer enrolled in a clinical trial. We conducted a prospective observational study of 1625 patients with stage III colon cancer enrolled in the CALGB/SWOG 80702 (Alliance) randomized adjuvant chemotherapy trial who completed a self-reported food frequency questionnaire within 6 weeks of and again 14-16 months post-randomization. Intakes of flavonoids overall and by subclasses (anthocyanidins, flavanones, flavan-3-ols, flavones, flavonols, isoflavones) were computed by multiplying the consumption frequency of each dietary item by the nutrient content of its respective specified portions. Multivariable analyses for the primary (disease-free survival [DFS]) and secondary (overall survival [OS]) endpoints were adjusted for sociodemographic, clinical, dietary, and lifestyle factors. Bonferroni corrections were applied for analyses of flavonoid subclasses and flavonoid-rich foods. Over median follow-up of 5.9 years, flavonoid consumption either overall or by subclasses was not significantly associated with survival outcomes, with a hazard ratio (HR) (95% confidence interval [CI]) of 1.01 (0.75-1.37) for DFS among those in the highest relative to lowest consumption quintiles of total flavonoids. Exploratory analyses of flavonoid-rich foods intake did not demonstrate significant associations with DFS or OS after Bonferroni correction. Among resected stage III colon cancer patients who received standardized treatment and follow-up within a nationwide randomized clinical trial, consumption of flavonoids was not associated with survival outcomes.ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT01150045.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Evidence of treatment strategies in frail patients (i.e. not fit for combination therapies) with unresectable metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) is limited to dose-reduced doublet regimens or oral fluoropyrimidines (FP) with bevacizumab. We conducted a systematic review analyzing evidence for oral FPs with epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-directed monoclonal antibodies for patients with RAS wild-type (WT) mCRC across treatment lines. We searched PubMed and Cochrane Library for phase II and phase III studies evaluating oral FPs (capecitabine, S-1 or trifluridine/tipiracil (FTD/TPI)) plus EGFR-directed monoclonal antibody (panitumumab or cetuximab) in mCRC. Outcomes included efficacy and safety. Seven publications met inclusion criteria (n = 262 patients). First-line data was limited to elderly cohorts receiving capecitabine plus cetuximab or panitumumab with a median progression-free survival (PFS)/median overall survival (OS) of 7.2/17.1 months (cetuximab) and 7.5/23.7 months (panitumumab), respectively. In third-line and beyond, median PFS for the combination of FTD/TPI plus cetuximab or panitumumab ranged from 2.4 (cetuximab) to 5.8 months (panitumumab), and OS from 9.8 (cetuximab) to 14.2 months (panitumumab). S-1 plus cetuximab was associated with a median PFS of 5.5 months and OS of 13.6 months. While capecitabine should not be used together with anti-EGFR antibodies, FTD/TPI in combination with an EGFR-directed antibody appears feasible, shows promising activity and manageable toxicity profile in RAS WT mCRC potentially offering an alternative for frail patients; prospective trials are needed.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Whether maintenance immunotherapy is necessary after clinical complete response (cCR) to programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) inhibition in mismatch repair-deficient/microsatellite instability-high colorectal cancer remains unclear. We evaluated its associations with survival and treatment-related toxicity. This multicenter cohort study included patients treated at five hospitals in China between January 2018 and March 2025 who achieved cCR after PD-1 inhibitor therapy and entered non-operative management. All patients underwent endoscopy and site-appropriate cross-sectional imaging to confirm cCR; 62.0% also underwent biopsy. Patients were categorized into observation and maintenance groups according to whether they received maintenance immunotherapy after cCR, defined as at least two additional treatment cycles. The primary endpoint was disease-free survival (DFS) from cCR; secondary endpoints were overall survival (OS), locoregional regrowth, distant metastasis, and treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs). Overlap weighting addressed measured confounding, with 6-week landmark and strict per-protocol analyses assessing robustness. Among 318 patients treated with PD-1 inhibitors, 173 (54.4%) achieved cCR; 129 (74.6%) entered non-operative management (observation, n=66; maintenance, n=63), while 44 underwent surgery. The analytic cohort included 58 patients with a single rectal primary, 61 with a single colon primary, and 10 with synchronous colorectal primaries; 115 (89.1%) had stage I–III disease. Median follow-up from cCR was 32.2 months (IQR 20.4–44.4). Both locoregional regrowths occurred in the observation group within 2 years after cCR; both patients underwent salvage treatment and remained alive. No distant metastases occurred, and the only death was due to COVID-19 without recurrence. 3-year DFS was 96.2% with observation and 98.3% with maintenance (log-rank p=0.508); corresponding OS was 100.0% and 98.3% (p=0.321). Overlap weighting did not materially alter the DFS comparison (p=0.192), and sensitivity analyses yielded similar estimates. Across the entire treatment and follow-up, any TRAE was numerically more frequent in the maintenance group than in the observation group (65.1% vs 59.1%); 15.9% of patients in the maintenance group experienced grade ≥2 TRAEs during maintenance therapy. Findings suggest that discontinuation after cCR may be reasonable within a watch-and-wait strategy for rectal cancer and provide preliminary support for non-operative management of colon cancer; prospective validation is warranted.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) is the standard treatment for locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC), yet its molecular determinants of response remain unclear. We conducted longitudinal 4D-DIA proteomic profiling of pre- and post-treatment specimens from 156 patients, including 31 patients with matched pre- and post-treatment specimens, and integrated with bulk RNA sequencing, single-cell transcriptomics, and functional validation. At baseline, responders were enriched in innate and adaptive immune pathways, whereas non-responders showed proliferative and metabolic programs. Pre-treatment RAC2, elevated in responders, was positively associated with immune activation, oxaliplatin sensitivity, and survival, and was validated in GSE139255 and GSE35640 (all P < 0.05). Moreover, RAC2 demonstrated strong predictive performance (training AUC = 0.867; testing AUC = 0.857). During treatment, NAC induced fibrosis-related remodeling across all groups (all P < 0.05), while responders uniquely preserved CD8⁺ T cell infiltration (P = 0.031). Responders and RAC2-high tumors exhibited concordant pathway dynamics during NAC. Single-cell analysis further revealed that pre-treatment tumor RAC2, higher in responders, transmitted signals to CD8⁺ T cells while receiving inputs from fibroblasts (P < 0.05). In vitro and in vivo, RAC2 knockdown reduced baseline tumor growth but promoted under oxaliplatin (all P < 0.05). Overall, this study offers proteomic insights into NAC in LARC, supports therapeutic decision-making, and identifies potential targets.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed the therapeutic landscape for mismatch repair deficient (dMMR) colorectal cancer; however, primary and acquired resistance remain significant challenges in clinical practice. This review proposes a working hypothesis that resistance can be conceptualized as following an evolutionary trajectory from a dynamic spatiotemporal perspective: commencing with early immune evasion by tumor cells, progressing through an adaptive immunosuppression phase, and culminating in advanced metastatic resistance characterized by spatial heterogeneity. Within this framework, we critically evaluate combination therapeutic strategies targeting resistance signals at each stage, including dual immune checkpoint blockade, tumor microenvironment modulators, novel bispecific antibodies, and neoantigen vaccines. We further emphasize that future breakthroughs will depend on leveraging single-cell multi-omics and spatial transcriptomics technologies to unravel resistance heterogeneity. This will drive the development of dynamic, personalized sequential combination therapies, delivering sustained benefits for patients.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Precise and non-invasive cancer diagnosis remains a persistent pursuit for clinicians. DNA circuit, owing to its biocompatibility and capability for complex information processing, has been explored for cancer diagnostics. Here, we established a cancer diagnosis platform based on a novel DNA weighted summation system. Using mRNA expression profiles from The Cancer Genome Atlas, we developed diagnostic models for prostate and colorectal cancers. An effective amplification method was then optimized and employed to quasi-linearly amplify and convert trace mRNA in blood, followed by molecular computation via our DNA weighted summation system. This approach overcomes a key limitation of previous DNA computing platforms that were restricted to integer weights, enabling continuous-weight computation and achieving precise disease diagnosis within a streamlined workflow. In clinical validation with 100 blood samples per cancer type, the platform achieved robust diagnostic accuracies of 85.0% for CRC and 86.0% for PCa. As a generalizable molecular computing framework, this platform may be extended to diverse clinical applications, including cancer staging, prognosis assessment, and therapeutic response prediction.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Peritoneal metastases are present in nearly twenty-five percent of patients with synchronous metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC). Treatment related overall survival (OS) outcomes within a real-world mCRC cohort, unstratified by metastatic site, have shown controversial results compared with corresponding trials, underlining the importance of evaluating survival scenarios within a real-world population. Therefore, the current study quantified real-world survival scenarios for patients with synchronous peritoneal metastatic colorectal cancer (sCPM) for each treatment. This population-based cohort study included all patients diagnosed with sCPM between 2011 and 2020. Patients were stratified based on therapeutic approach: Cytoreductive Surgery and Hyperthermic Intraperitoneal Chemotherapy (CRS-HIPEC), Primary Tumor Resection (PTR) with or without palliative systemic therapy, Palliative Systemic Therapy (PST) and Best-Supportive Care (BSC). Primary outcomes were best, upper-typical, median, lower-typical and worst-case survival scenarios for each treatment, calculated from survival curve percentiles. Of 7038 patients, 12% underwent CRS-HIPEC, 27% underwent PTR, 30% received PST and 2200 (31%) received BSC. For CRS-HIPEC, the best, upper-typical, median, lower-typical and worst-case scenarios were: not-reached, 68, 35, 20 and 11 months. For PTR, these scenarios were 51, 26, 13, 5.9 and 1.8 months, while for PST these were 28, 17, 10, 5.3 and 2.6 months. For BSC these scenarios were 7.1, 3.4, 1.5, 0.6 and 0.2 months. Real-world treatment related OS scenarios demonstrate a considerable heterogeneity across, and within treatment modalities for patients with synchronous CPM. These findings provide more tailored treatment related expected OS. Moreover, OS outcomes are inferior to those reported in corresponding trials, emphasizing constraints of external validity in mCRC trials.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Patients with colorectal cancer or severe abdominal trauma often require a stoma and must master the self-care necessary to prevent peristomal skin complications. In this study, we developed and evaluated a mobile health (mHealth) app, called The Stoma Self-Care App, to facilitate self-care knowledge and skill acquisition alongside clinical monitoring in patients with ostomy. The app was developed following the 6 stages of the System Development Life Cycle: planning, design, development, testing, deployment, and maintenance. To evaluate usability, the app was tested in 23 patients over 4 weeks, who then completed a self-administered satisfaction questionnaire. The final version of the mHealth app received favorable clinical appraisals, with the average satisfaction score being 4.85/5.0. The findings demonstrated good usability and high user satisfaction among a small sample of patients with ostomy, indicating that the app was well accepted and easy to use. Overall, this study describes a systematic, user-centered approach to developing a mHealth app for ostomy self-care and provides preliminary evidence supporting its usability and acceptability. The app's systematic development and high user acceptance support the feasibility of a user-centered development approach for mHealth applications in ostomy care. Further studies involving larger and more diverse patient populations are warranted to evaluate the app's effectiveness and broader applicability.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Diverting loop ileostomy is commonly used to mitigate the consequences of anastomotic leakage after rectal cancer surgery. However, some patients do not undergo stoma closure, resulting in a permanent stoma that may impair quality of life. This study evaluated the closure rate, reasons for non-closure, and associated preoperative factors using multicenter prospective data. This study was a subanalysis of a multicenter prospective study conducted at 24 institutions. Patients with rectal adenocarcinoma who underwent laparoscopic or robotic low anterior resection or intersphincteric resection with planned diverting loop ileostomy between July 2015 and April 2021 were included. Stomas not closed within 1 year were classified as non-closed. Preoperative characteristics were compared between the stoma closure and non-closure groups using univariable analyses. Among 320 patients, 298 (93.1%) underwent stoma closure, whereas 22 (6.9%) did not. Reasons for non-closure were postoperative complications (n = 9), cancer recurrence (n = 6), patient preference (n = 5), and death (n = 2). In univariable comparisons, patients with stoma non-closure more frequently had ASA-PS ≥2 (86.4% vs. 63.8%, P = 0.036), stage III-IV disease (68.2% vs. 38.9%, P = 0.012), and serum albumin <3.5 g/dL (31.8% vs. 7.4%, P = 0.002) than those who underwent stoma closure. Although most diverting loop ileostomies were successfully closed, 6.9% were not reversed. Patients with stoma non-closure more frequently had ASA-PS ≥2, advanced clinical stage, and low serum albumin levels than those who underwent stoma closure. These findings may be useful for preoperative counseling. UMIN000038150.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To evaluate whether baseline multi-parametric MRI radiomics models, integrating multiple regions of interest (ROIs), can predict pathological complete response (pCR) to neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (NCRT) in locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC), and to validate performance externally. In this multicenter, retrospective cohort study, 510 patients with LARC treated with NCRT followed by total mesorectal excision were enrolled (330 for training, 83 for internal validation, and 97 for external validation). Radiomic features were extracted from three ROIs (primary tumor, mesorectal region, and lateral lymph node regions). After redundancy reduction and clustering, the top 30 features were selected using gradient boosting decision trees via cross-validation. Four classifiers, logistic regression, random forest, support vector machine, and extra trees, were evaluated, with SMOTE applied to address class imbalance. Model performance was compared across ROI combinations, MRI sequences, and algorithms using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Overall, 98 of 510 patients (19.2%) achieved pCR. The multi-ROI, multi-parametric model based on extra trees achieved an AUC of 0.717 in the external validation set. Among single-ROI models, tumor ROI yielded the highest AUC (0.630). Among MRI sequences, the ADC-based model performed best (AUC 0.629). Baseline multi-parametric MRI radiomics models integrating multiple ROIs showed modest predictive performance for pCR in LARC and demonstrated similar predictive utility in an independent external cohort. This approach may provide pre-treatment risk stratification and support future research on individualized treatment strategies and organ preservation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
FLLL32 is a curcumin analogue with reported anti-tumor activity, mainly through inhibition of signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3) signaling and induction of apoptosis. However, whether FLLL32 regulates ferroptosis in colorectal cancer (CRC) and the underlying mechanism remain unclear. Here, using a patient-derived CRC organoid screening platform, we identified FLLL32 as a potent anti-CRC compound. FLLL32 suppressed CRC organoid growth, inhibited CRC cell proliferation and migration in vitro, and inhibited xenograft tumor growth in vivo. In parallel, FLLL32 induced ferroptosis-associated iron accumulation, reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, lipid peroxidation, mitochondrial morphological and functional abnormalities. The ferroptosis inhibitor Ferrostatin-1 markedly restored FLLL32-impaired cell viability and reduced ROS, whereas the apoptosis inhibitor Z-VAD-FMK showed weaker protection. These findings suggest that ferroptosis is a major contributor to FLLL32-induced cell death, although apoptotic features are also present. Mechanistically, FLLL32 interacted with STAT3, and Glu638 and Met726 contributed to the FLLL32-STAT3 interaction. FLLL32 also suppressed STAT3 Tyr705 phosphorylation and nuclear signaling, thereby disrupting pSTAT3-mediated transcriptional regulation of glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) and solute carrier family 40 member 1 (SLC40A1), weakening lipid peroxide detoxification and cellular iron efflux, promoting intracellular iron accumulation, and enhancing ferroptosis in CRC cells. These findings define a STAT3-GPX4/SLC40A1-dependent mechanism underlying the anti-CRC activity of FLLL32 and support further investigation of STAT3-associated ferroptosis regulation as a potential therapeutic vulnerability in CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Cuproptosis and N6-methyladenosine (m6A) RNA methylation have been identified as significant factors in cancer. Consequently, we seek to uncover m6A RNA methylation-related prognostic genes that are correlated with cuproptosis-related genes (CRGs) in colorectal cancer (CRC) and develop an effective prognostic model. Based on public datasets, differential expression analysis, correlation analysis, and machine learning were conducted to identify prognostic genes. Subsequently, a prognostic model was constructed and validated. Furthermore, independent predictive markers were found through the use of clinical characteristics and risk score, to establish a prognostic nomogram. Prognostic gene expression in CRC and normal samples was evaluated using reverse transcription-quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR). According to the prognostic genes, potential drugs for CRC were predicted using artificial intelligence drug design (AIDD) and computer-aided drug design (CADD). A prognostic model was developed utilizing 7 m6A RNA methylation-related prognostic genes that were significantly correlated with CRGs (MMP1, TIMP1, SNAI1, CDC25C, XRN2, COX5A, and FBXL5) in CRC. Survival analysis uncovered a notable contrast in survival outcomes between the high- and low-risk groups. The nomogram constructed based on age, stage, T stage, and risk scores demonstrated good predictive ability. RT-qPCR results showed that MMP1, TIMP1, SNAI1, and CDC25C were upregulated in CRC samples, while COX5A was downregulated, consistent with the bioinformatics analysis results. Furthermore, 186 candidate drugs targeting COX5A were identified, 153 of which showed better predicted binding affinity than the positive-control ligand 3,5‑diiodo‑L‑thyronine. Our analysis sets the groundwork for a more comprehensive comprehension of the fundamental molecular pathways involved in CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Later-line therapy for metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) increasingly requires selection among treatments with different mechanisms, toxicity profiles, and sequencing evidence. Trifluridine/tipiracil plus bevacizumab has robust randomized evidence from SUNLIGHT, but objective response remains uncommon and hematologic toxicity can limit treatment delivery in heavily pretreated patients. Regorafenib and fruquintinib are minimally myelosuppressive oral alternatives, yet they differ in dose strategy, hepatotoxicity, hand-foot skin reaction, hypertension, and proteinuria. This narrative review updates pivotal and recent evidence and proposes an evidence-informed framework that treats hematologic reserve as a clinical fitness construct rather than a fixed laboratory threshold. We additionally examine the clinical implications of low response rates, prior anti-angiogenic exposure, emerging molecular predictors including KRAS G12, evidence in older or vulnerable patients, and recent phase III developments. Current data do not support a validated molecular biomarker for choosing among these three options, and no randomized head-to-head comparison of regorafenib and fruquintinib exists. Accordingly, treatment selection should be individualized according to prior therapies, toxicity vulnerability, organ function, tumor tempo, and patient goals. Hypertension and proteinuria are important selection factors but may also be modifiable treatment-delivery factors. The proposed algorithms and adverse-event radar chart are intended as practical visual syntheses rather than validated guidelines or formal cross-trial comparisons.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal liver metastases (CRLM) are a major cause of mortality in colorectal cancer and are characterised by a profoundly immunosuppressive tumour microenvironment in which tumour-associated macrophages (TAMs) play a central role. However, the molecular mechanisms driving TAM plasticity and maintenance remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated macrophage heterogeneity in CRLM and examined the contribution of the epigenetic regulator lysine-specific demethylase 1 (LSD1) to TAM polarisation. Analysis of patient-derived specimens by flow cytometry, immunohistochemistry and transcriptional profiling identified a population of large TAMs (L-TAMs) enriched in the peritumoral niche that displayed an immunosuppressive, M2-like phenotype and was associated with poor clinical outcome. In contrast, smaller TAMs (S-TAMs) exhibited a more inflammatory transcriptional programme, including increased IL1β expression. Tumour-conditioned media reproduced these distinct macrophage phenotypes in vitro, indicating that tumour-derived factors actively shape TAM identity. Pharmacological inhibition of LSD1 using baicalin or INCB059872 reduced the expression of CD206 and the immune checkpoint molecule PD-L1, consistent with macrophage reprogramming away from a tumour-promoting state. Collectively, these findings identify LSD1 as an epigenetic regulator of macrophage plasticity in CRLM, implicated in the maintenance of immunosuppressive TAM phenotypes, and potentially able to induce phenotypic reversion. Our findings identify LSD1 as a regulator of TAM phenotype and support further investigation of LSD1 targeting as a strategy to remodel the metastatic tumour microenvironment and potentially enhance anti-tumour immunity.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The da Vinci Xi replaced the Si with a boom-mounted architecture intended to remove the re-docking and multiquadrant limits on pelvic access. Whether it changes outcomes in rectal cancer surgery is unresolved: existing syntheses pooled rectal with colonic resection. Five databases, Google Scholar and citation graphs were searched to August 2026, without language or design restriction, for comparative studies reporting outcomes separately by platform in rectal cancer resection. Screening, extraction and risk-of-bias assessment were done in duplicate. Random-effects models with a Hartung-Knapp adjustment were used; certainty was rated with GRADE. Eight non-randomised cohorts (843 patients; 380 Xi, 463 Si) were included. Pooling all five cohorts reporting operative time, the mean difference was - 27.7 min (95% confidence interval - 80.4 to + 25.0; I² 95%); restricted to the four reporting means with standard deviations, thus conditional on excluding the largest cohort, it was - 50.6 min (- 69.4 to - 31.7). Docking time was shorter with the Xi in all three reporting cohorts, which defined it differently or not at all. The evidence is very uncertain about the effect of platform on anastomotic leak (risk ratio 0.53, 0.24 to 1.14), complications, conversion, reoperation, margin involvement and specimen quality; certainty was very low throughout. The evidence is very uncertain about the effect of the da Vinci Xi compared with the Si on perioperative and oncological outcomes in rectal cancer, and functional outcomes have not been compared. Because the platforms were compared across periods, centres and levels of experience, no estimate isolates the platform.PROSPERO registration CRD420261480007, registered 18 August 2026, before data extraction.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Lynch syndrome, one of the most common hereditary cancer predisposition syndromes, is caused by pathogenic variants in the mismatch repair genes (MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2) and the EPCAM gene. Individuals who inherit pathogenic variants in Lynch-associated genes experience increased lifetime risk of colorectal, endometrial, and several other cancer types. Risks of Lynch-associated cancers vary by the affected gene and within each gene, especially for lower penetrance genes. This poses challenges for clinicians to provide patients and families with accurate cancer risk estimates and determine individualized surveillance protocols. Compounding this challenge is that study designs and potential biases could yield different risk estimates. In this review, we present up-to-date Lynch syndrome cancer risk estimates and discuss how study design could impact these risk estimates.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Integrating nanoparticles (NPs) with living cells into a unified therapeutic system remains a major methodological challenge. Here, we describe a robust and modular bioorthogonal strategy for constructing cell-nanoparticle hybrids (CNHs) via sequential thiazolidine formation and SpyCatcher/SpyTag ligation. This two-step chemical assembly enables highly specific and covalent conjugation of structurally diverse NP payloads─including ferritin nanocages, lipid micelles, and amphiphilic polymers─onto aldehyde-presenting cell surfaces without genetic modification, ensuring broad applicability while preserving cellular functionality. The resulting CNHs exhibit enhanced nanoparticle retention and tumor penetration both in vitro and in vivo. In a colorectal cancer xenograft model, CNHs demonstrate superior antitumor efficacy compared with free drugs, unconjugated NPs, or unmodified macrophages. Mechanistic studies indicate that the enhanced tumor inhibition arises from the combined effects of chemotherapeutic drug-loaded NPs and the intrinsic properties of macrophages. Collectively, these results demonstrate a versatile chemical framework for bioorthogonal cell-nanoparticle assembly and the rational design of functional living hybrid systems.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Adolescent sleep insufficiency is increasingly prevalent, but whether repeated insufficient sleep during this developmental period promotes addiction vulnerability remains unclear. Here, we investigated the effects of chronic sleep restriction (CSR) imposed during adolescence, from 4 to 7 weeks of age, on the mesocorticolimbic dopamine (DA) system and addiction-related behaviors in mice. Behavioral and neuronal responses in the mesolimbic pathway to the psychostimulant Amphetamine (Amph) were examined. Also, DA-related molecular and structural components, including DA receptors, DA turnover, and developmental regulators such as Netrin-1/deleted in colorectal cancer (DCC), were assessed. Our results identified that adolescent CSR induces a hypodopaminergic profile characterized by reduced neuronal activity in the core regions of the mesolimbic DA circuit at baseline and upon acute Amph stimulation, downregulated striatal DA receptors, and reduced DA axon innervation in the ventral striatum. Altered Netrin-1/DCC signaling and mesocortical DA synthesis further suggest that sleep loss during adolescence disrupts ongoing maturation of DA circuitry. Furthermore, these neurobiological profiles were accompanied by enhanced Amph-induced conditioned place preference (CPP). Together, these findings indicate that chronic adolescent sleep insufficiency induces a constellation of behavioral and neurobiological adaptations relevant to addiction susceptibility. In contrast to prior acute sleep-loss paradigms that mainly capture transient DA activation, our data support a model in which repeated sleep restriction imposes cumulative allostatic load and promotes longer-term maladaptive remodeling of reward circuitry. These results identify insufficient sleep during adolescence as a potential risk factor for addiction vulnerability.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Historically viewed as a localized gastrointestinal malignancy, colorectal cancer (CRC) is increasingly recognized as a systemic pathology that actively programs distant microenvironments. This review delineates a novel mechanistic framework wherein CRC-driven dysregulation of the brain-gut-microbiota axis (BGMA) acts as a systemic architect of the breast pre-metastatic niche (PMN). We synthesize how localized intestinal oncogenic stress propagates through three convergent conduits: (1) Immune Reprogramming, where gut-derived inflammatory mediators and extracellular vesicles (EVs) recruit myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs) to the mammary stroma; (2) Neuro-ecological Conditioning, involving chronic hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis activation and sympathetic hyperactivation that drives catecholamine-mediated remodeling of breast tissue; and (3) Humoral-Metabolic Convergence, specifically via the "estrobolome" and secondary bile acids that synchronize systemic hormonal levels with local tissue receptivity. By reframing CRC progression as a systemic pathology that potentially preconditions distant, hormone-sensitive environments, we propose the BGMA as a conceptual framework for prospective "systemic interception", outlining roadmaps to neutralize metastatic cascades at their incipient, reversible stages.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Accurate optical characterization of small colorectal polyps relies on narrow-band imaging (NBI) or artificial intelligence, both of which are unavailable in resource-limited settings. We aimed to develop and validate a web-based nomogram using white-light endoscopy (WLE) and routine clinical variables to predict neoplastic polyp histology. This prospective single-center study (Vietnam, September 2020-April 2021) included 301 patients with 451 small colorectal polyps (≤10 mm). Polyps were assessed in real time using WLE and NBI before histological confirmation. Data were split at the patient level into training (254 patients, 383 polyps) and validation (47 patients, 68 polyps) cohorts. L1-penalized generalized linear mixed-effects models were used for feature selection and model development. Neoplastic histology was present in 55.9% of polyps. Four predictors were identified: sessile/pedunculated morphology (0-Is/0-Ip), age ≥50 years, polyp size >5 mm, and neoplastic WLE diagnosis. In internal validation, the WLE+3F model achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.849, outperforming WLE alone (AUC, 0.760; P = 0.009) and comparable with NBI (AUC, 0.858; P = 0.86), with sensitivity of 65.8%, specificity of 90.0%, and good calibration (Brier score, 0.160). Decision curve analysis showed clinical net benefit. A WLE-based nomogram combined with 3 clinical factors achieved performance comparable with NBI, offering an accessible tool for real-time risk stratification in resource-limited settings; external validation is warranted.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Lack of health insurance limits access to health care, leading to potentially preventable inequities in health outcomes. This modelling study estimates the impact of providing insurance to currently uninsured individuals on colorectal cancer (CRC) outcomes in the US. The MISCAN-Colon model was adapted to an uninsured population aged 40-100 during 2025-2055, using age-specific estimates from national data sources for screening, stage distribution, survival and all-cause mortality by insurance status (ages 40-64: privately insured vs. uninsured; ages 65-100: Medicare and private coverage vs. Medicare only). The effects of this uninsured population gaining health insurance coverage in 2025 were compared with the same population remaining uninsured for CRC incidence, mortality, and costs. Both groups were assumed age-eligible for Medicare coverage at 65 years. In an uninsured population, the model predicted 170 CRC cases and 73 deaths per 100,000 in 2055. If this population gained private insurance, up to 15 (8.9%) cases and 22 (30.7%) deaths per 100,000 could be averted by 2055. Although insurance gains would decrease treatment costs by $1.37 million per 100,000 (-4.8%) through prevention and earlier diagnoses, total CRC-related costs would increase by $1.29 million per 100,000 (+3.7%) due to increased screening costs ($2.66 million per 100,000, +41.7%). If the previously uninsured population gained health insurance, CRC incidence and CRC mortality could be reduced substantially because of improved access to care. Assuming analogous improvements for other cancers, this case study provides an example for the potential benefits of gaining health insurance on mitigating health disparities.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
In the era of multidisciplinary cancer care, proctectomy remains an essential procedure in treating rectal cancer. However, the current rates of optimal surgical resection in the US are unknown. This study examined the rates, hospital variation and factors associated with optimal surgical resection. Patients with clinically locally advanced (cT3-T4 and/or cN1-2) rectal adenocarcinoma who underwent proctectomy between 2021 and 2023 were identified within the National Cancer Database (NCDB). Optimal surgical resection was a composite metric defined as complete total mesorectal excision (TME), negative surgical margins and adequate lymph node yield (LNY) ≥12. Mixed-effects multivariable analyses were performed to assess the association between optimal surgical resection and overall survival, identify factors associated with optimal surgical resection and assess hospital variation. Among 6,183 patients, the optimal surgical resection rate was 59.2% (complete TME = 78.6%, negative surgical margins = 85.4%, adequate LNY = 83.7%). Optimal surgical resection was independently associated with longer overall survival (HR = 0.62, 95%CI = 0.48-0.80). Older age (p < 0.001) and Black race (p = 0.02) were independently associated with lower odds of achieving optimal surgical resection. There was wide variation in adjusted optimal surgical resection rates across hospitals (range = 30%-82%), and higher hospital volume was associated with optimal surgical resection (p < 0.001). Possible disparities in achieving optimal surgical resection were identified among older and Black patients. In addition, there is wide hospital variation in achieving optimal surgical resection along with a direct correlation between higher hospital volume and optimal surgical resection. These findings support selective referral to medium-to-high volume centres to achieve better outcomes and future research into the aetiology of these possible disparities.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Medullary adenocarcinoma is a rare colorectal carcinoma that may be difficult to recognize when inflammation dominates the presentation. A 65-year-old woman with a remote appendectomy presented with 1 month of postprandial abdominal pain, weight loss, and constipation. Repeated computed tomography demonstrated marked pericecal inflammation and a blind-ending structure interpreted as possible appendicitis despite her surgical history. Diagnostic laparoscopy identified an enlarged mesenteric lymph node, and excision unexpectedly showed metastatic medullary carcinoma of colonic origin with loss of MutL homolog 1 and PMS1 homolog 2 genes. Subsequent evaluation identified an ascending-colon primary. Right hemicolectomy confirmed a 1.5 cm poorly differentiated medullary adenocarcinoma, staged as pT2 pN1b, with negative margins. The patient remains clinically well during oncologic treatment. Persistent appendicitis-like inflammation, particularly when discordant with prior appendectomy, should prompt evaluation for cecal or ascending-colon malignancy.

Gastric schwannomas are rare, benign mesenchymal tumours that closely mimic gastrointestinal stromal tumours (GISTs) on imaging, despite fundamentally different biological behaviour. We report a 74-year-old man with a background of proctocolectomy for rectal cancer, found incidentally to have a 5 cm exophytic gastric mass on surveillance gastroscopy. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer is a leading cause of cancer-related morbidity and mortality, and the prognosis significantly depends on the diagnostic stage. Various screening initiatives have been established, among which the fecal immunochemical test (FIT) (FITFIT) which is prominent for its affordability, non-invasive approach, and wide acceptance. This study aimed to describe the spectrum of histopathological findings among patients with positive fecal occult blood test and abnormal colonoscopy findings, and to identify associated risk factors. This retrospective observational study included 172 adults with documented positive FIT and abnormal colonoscopy findings at Makassed General Hospital from January 2024 to December 2025. Statistical analysis was conducted using SPSS version 25, and associations were assessed using chi-square or Fisher's exact tests, with significance defined as A total of 172 patients were included, with a mean age of 63.88 ± 11.79 years, and 55.2% were female. The most frequently recorded indications for colonoscopy were anemia (39%) and screening (37.2%). Polyps were the most common colonoscopy finding. Histopathological examination demonstrated that neoplastic polyps represented the predominant diagnosis (65.1%), followed by non-neoplastic lesions (24.4%) and malignancy (10.5%). Patients aged 45 years and older demonstrated a higher prevalence of polyps on colonoscopy; however, the difference did not reach statistical significance. No significant association was observed between gender and colonoscopy or histopathological findings. Abdominal pain and diarrhea were both significantly associated with non-neoplastic histopathological lesions. Among patients with positive FIT and abnormal colonoscopy findings, neoplastic polyps rather than malignancy represented the predominant histopathological findings, supporting the clinical utility of FIT in detecting clinically important colorectal lesions at earlier stages. In addition, variability in the histopathology depending on the clinical presentation may contribute to clinical assessment and risk stratification. Larger prospective studies are needed to determine predictors of advanced colorectal histopathology.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) cells undergo significant alterations in glucose and glutamine metabolism to support rapid growth and migration. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying these metabolic changes remain incompletely understood. Although NUAK1 and NUAK2, members of the NUAK kinase family have been implicated in CRC tumorigenesis, their specific roles in metabolic reprogramming that drives CRC progression and metastasis have not been elucidated. In this study, we demonstrate that NUAK1 and NUAK2 are overexpressed in human CRC tissues and that their expression is associated with increased tumor metastasis and poorer patient survival. NUAK1/2 promotes CRC cell proliferation and migration, whereas their depletion markedly reduces cell growth and migratory capacity. Furthermore, knockout of NUAK1/2 disrupts key metabolic pathways, including aerobic glycolysis, pentose phosphate pathway (PPP), and glutamine metabolism. Mechanistically, NUAK1/2 facilitates mTOR-driven metabolic reprogramming and promotes CRC growth and migration by suppressing AMPK activity. Depletion of NUAK1/2 impairs metabolic function, cellular growth, and migration potential in CRC cells, effects that are further enhanced by pharmacological activation of AMPK with AICAR and inhibition of mTOR using Rapamycin. In conclusion, these findings identify NUAK1/2 as critical regulators of CRC progression and migration through AMPK/mTOR-mediated metabolic reprogramming, highlighting their potential as therapeutic targets in colorectal cancer.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Transanal surgery has advanced significantly since the introduction of transanal endoscopic microsurgery (TEM) in 1983. The single-port (SP) robotic system marks the latest technological advancement in minimally invasive transanal surgery, combining single-site access with full robotic articulation through a single 25 mm port. This is the first video dynamic manuscript and 2nd document of a four-part SAGES Colorectal Committee series outlining the foundational application of SP technology in colorectal surgery, specifically transanal minimally invasive surgery (SP-TAMIS). The SAGES Colorectal Committee SP Task Force performed a structured review of the da Vinci SP system, assessing platform features, instrumentation, and workflow considerations for transanal surgery. Task force members (subject matter experts with early experience with single-port robotic platforms) analyzed technical details, patient selection, operative workflows, and early outcomes. Representative procedural video-based techniques were detailed with emphasis on instrumentation, docking, and key operative steps specific to the SP transanal procedure. The SP platform appears to offer several technological advantages for transanal surgery: (1) natural hand-eye coordination in an inverted field, (2) enhanced visualization with an articulating cobra camera, and (3) a third arm for retraction and exposure. These features appear to improve precision, reduce collision risk and fatigue, and shorten operative time. Published early clinical data suggest low positive margin rates (≈ 4-5%) and acceptable morbidity for multiport robotic TAMIS/SP-TAMIS in selected patients. However, direct comparative evidence versus conventional TAMIS remains limited, and many comparisons are indirect across heterogeneous cohorts. Current limitations include high cost, limited distal reach, lack of dedicated energy devices, and learning curve. The learning curve appears to be shorter than for laparoscopic TAMIS. Peritoneal entry during full-thickness excision of upper rectal and anterior lesions is a recognized event in transanal surgery; the SP platform offers several features that may facilitate its management, though SP-specific incidence data are not yet available. SME early experience with SP-TAMIS suggests that it can provide a safe, effective, and ergonomically superior method for local rectal excision. Mastery of this foundational application builds the skills needed for more complex SP colorectal procedures, with the potential for single-port robotics expansion into minimally invasive colorectal surgery through enhanced precision, reduced invasiveness, and improved surgeon ergonomics.
