ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Endocytosis regulates receptor trafficking and signaling, yet its role in colorectal cancer (CRC) remains unclear. We analyzed transcriptomic data from 15,025 CRC tumors to evaluate gene expression in clathrin-mediated endocytosis (CME) and the endosomal sorting complexes required for transport (ESCRT) pathway. Pathway-level signatures were compared across consensus molecular subtypes (CMS) and examined in relation to oncogenic signaling programs, while individual endocytosis-related genes were evaluated for associations with clinical outcomes in an independent randomized trial cohort. Expression of CME and ESCRT pathways varied by CMS, with the highest expression in CMS4 and the lowest in CMS3. Endocytosis signatures correlated with multiple oncogenic signaling pathways, including MAPK, TGF-β, WNT, PI3K, NOTCH, and angiogenesis, suggesting broad links between endocytic activity and tumor biology. In the randomized phase III CALGB/SWOG 80405 trial, low expression of AP2M1-a core adaptor in the CME complex-was significantly associated with longer overall survival and progression-free survival in patients treated with anti-EGFR agents, but not in those receiving anti-VEGF agents. These findings suggest that endocytic trafficking may be associated with oncogenic signaling and differential therapeutic benefit in patients with metastatic CRC. The endocytosis pathway reflects biologically relevant heterogeneity in CRC and may help guide therapeutic stratification.

Patients with metastatic cancer at initial diagnosis have the worst prognosis. Our objective was to determine whether Primary Care Physician availability is associated with patients having metastatic cancer at initial diagnosis. This was a cross-sectional study of patients aged ≥ 18 and diagnosed with breast, colorectal, liver, lung, ovarian, pancreatic, or prostate cancer from 2015 to 2019. Population-based Texas and California cancer registries were used for patient data. The main exposure was county-level Primary Care Physician density per 3500 individuals. Additional exposures included demographic factors, insurance, rural-urban continuum codes, county poverty rates, and US State at Diagnosis. The primary outcome was adjusted odds of metastatic cancer at initial diagnosis. Subgroup analyses based on insurance type, age group, and metropolitan residence were performed. Models were stratified by cancer type. Overall, 708,451 patients were included. On combined multivariable analysis, with each additional Primary Care Physician per 3500 individuals, the odds for primary outcome decreased by 2% to 6%. In a stratified analysis using Primary Care Physician density per 3500 individuals as a categorical variable, compared with counties with < 1 Primary Care Physician, counties with 3 or more Primary Care Physicians had reduced odds of primary outcome for multiple cancer types with no statistically significant difference for counties with 1-1.9 Primary Care Physicians. Increased Primary Care Physician availability was associated with a nonlinear decrease in odds for metastatic cancer at diagnosis. Thus, increasing physician density can possibly lower the likelihood of metastatic cancer at initial diagnosis.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To quantify temporal and geographic trends in mortality and morbidity attributable to these risk factors from 1990 to 2023 and to project disease burden through 2050. Annual estimates of deaths, disability-adjusted life years (DALYs), years of life lost (YLLs), and years lived with disability (YLDs) were extracted by age, sex, and geographic region. Temporal trends in age-standardized rates were assessed using estimated annual percentage change (EAPC) derived from log-linear regression and joinpoint regression to identify inflection points. For projections through 2050, we applied an ensemble approach incorporating autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) models, exponential smoothing state-space models, and Bayesian age-period-cohort (BAPC) analysis. Between 1990 and 2023, age-standardized mortality from smoking-attributable gastric cancer declined substantially (EAPC -4.37, 95% CI -4.62 to -4.12), while declines for smoking-attributable colorectal cancer were more modest (EAPC -1.96, 95% CI -2.10 to -1.82). Alcohol-attributable colorectal cancer presented a complex pattern: although age-standardized rates decreased globally, absolute DALYs increased by 16.5%, with rising incidence in transitioning economies such as Vietnam. Males accounted for the majority of burden across all metrics. While age-standardized rates for both malignancies have declined over three decades, absolute disease burden - particularly for colorectal cancer among men - persists.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Mucosal-associated invariant T (MAIT) cells are emerging as important regulators of immunity in gastrointestinal (GI) cancers. Enriched in mucosal and hepatic tissues, MAIT cells recognize microbial-derived metabolites presented by MHC class I-related molecule (MR1) and rapidly exert effector functions, including cytokine production and cytotoxicity. Across GI malignancies, including hepatocellular carcinoma, cholangiocarcinoma, colorectal, gastric, pancreatic, and esophageal cancers, MAIT cells display context-dependent roles shaped by the tumor microenvironment, microbiome, and immune signaling pathways. While they can mediate antitumor immunity, they frequently exhibit functional exhaustion or adopt pro-tumorigenic phenotypes. Therapeutic strategies aim to enhance MAIT cell activity, reverse dysfunction, and integrate them into combinatorial immunotherapy approaches. Understanding MAIT cell biology may enable their exploitation as biomarkers and therapeutic targets in GI cancers.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Contemporary rectal cancer treatment pathways remain predominantly guided by tumour-related characteristics, including stage and histopathology, with comparatively limited objective assessment of physiological reserve for treatment planning. Aortic calcification represents a potential imaging biomarker reflecting systemic vascular disease, chronic inflammation and physiological reserve. We evaluated computed tomography (CT)-derived abdominal aortic calcification as a prognostic imaging biomarker for postoperative outcomes and long-term survival. A retrospective cohort study was conducted using the prospectively maintained Australian Comprehensive Cancer Outcomes and Research Database (ACCORD) of rectal cancer patients treated between 2013 and 2022. Pre-treatment staging CT was subjected to semi-automated volumetric quantification of calcium using 3D Slicer software. Calcification volume was assessed segmentally at vertebral levels L1-L4 and at the iliac vessels. Primary outcomes were major postoperative complications (Clavien-Dindo ≥ III) and overall survival. Cox proportional hazards modelling was performed using a prespecified parsimonious multivariable model. A total of 174 patients were included in the analysis. Increasing calcification burden demonstrated no statistically significant association with major postoperative complications (OR 1.09 per 1000-unit increase; 95% CI 0.99-1.19; p = 0.07). Increasing calcification independently predicted worse 5-year survival after multivariable adjustment (HR 1.17 per 1000-unit increase ([CI 1.08-1.28, p = 0.001]). Kaplan-Meier analyses showed separation between calcification groups, although dichotomised analyses did not reach statistical significance. Aortic calcification independently predicts long-term survival following rectal cancer surgery but not short-term postoperative complications. Quantitative CT-derived calcification assessment may provide a rapid, objective imaging biomarker that reflects physiological reserve and represents a potential adjunct to future risk stratification pathways.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
T cells recognize tumor-specific neoantigens presented by human leukocyte antigen (HLA) molecules and can mediate potent antitumor immunity. However, most neoantigens are patient-specific, limiting their broad therapeutic applicability. KRAS G12V is a recurrent oncogenic mutation found in multiple cancer types and generates a shared neoantigen presented by HLA-A*11:01. We sought to develop a T cell-engaging bispecific antibody targeting this shared neoantigen. We screened a phage display library to identify a single-chain variable fragment (scFv) recognizing the KRAS G12V/HLA-A*11:01 complex. Candidate scFvs were characterized by ELISA and flow cytometry. A bispecific single-chain diabody incorporating a neoantigen-specific scFv and an anti-CD3 binding domain was generated and evaluated for antigen-specific T-cell activation, cytokine production, and cytotoxicity using peptide-pulsed target cells and KRAS G12V-positive cancer cell lines. Antitumor activity and safety were assessed in a human peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC)-engrafted xenograft mouse model. We identified scFv2, which selectively recognized the KRAS G12V/HLA-A*11:01 complex while discriminating against wild-type KRAS and other KRAS mutant peptides. Notably, scFv2 also recognized the KRAS G12V/HLA-A*03:01 complex. The resulting scFv2-based bispecific single-chain diabody (scDb2) induced robust antigen-specific T-cell activation, cytokine release and cytotoxicity against KRAS G12V-positive cancer cells expressing either HLA-A*11:01 or HLA-A*03:01, corresponding to an estimated patient coverage of ~5–6% in pancreatic cancer and ~2% in colorectal cancer. scDb2 recognized an endogenously processed and presented neoantigen, mediated cancer cell killing, and significantly suppressed tumor growth in vivo without overt toxicity. These findings identify a T cell-engaging bispecific antibody capable of recognizing KRAS G12V presented by both HLA-A*11:01 and HLA-A*03:01, providing a framework for expanding neoantigen-targeted immunotherapies across closely related HLA alleles, potentially broadening applicability across diverse patient populations.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) is among the most lethal malignancies worldwide, and histopathological examination remains the clinical gold standard for diagnosis. In the histopathological examination, collaborative perception of fine-grained and coarse-grained lesions in histopathological samples is crucial for CRC diagnosis. However, existing methods often struggle to simultaneously model discriminative cues across granularities because of fine-grained glandular disorganization and coarse-grained morphological overlap among tissue categories. To tackle these issues, we propose a novel Multi-granularity Collaborative Cascaded-perception Network (MCCNet), which learns cross-granularity discriminative representations to overcome the limitations of single-granularity modeling. For fine-grained glandular disorganization, we design an Adaptive Glandular Offset Convolution (AGO-Conv). The convolution adaptively learns sampling offsets by injecting prominent edge gradients to actively focus on disorganized glands, and dynamically adjusts the sampling radius by a continuous domain constraint mechanism, thereby preventing out-of-bound glandular sampling. For coarse-grained similar lesions, we construct a Grouped Residual Linear-Attention (GRLA) module. GRLA linear approximate exponential kernel by segmented decomposable kernel mapping, and the discriminative inter-class representations across multiple subspaces are further preserved by subspace grouping and deep residual paths, thereby alleviating inter-class similarity among different tissue categories. To enable dynamic cross-granularity feature coupling, a Multi-Granularity Cascaded Feature Fusion (MGCFF) module is proposed that recalibrates the discriminative responses along channel and spatial dimensions via cascaded hierarchical representations and feature recalibration units, and further eliminates low-response background noise by multi-scale gating mechanism, thereby mitigating cross-granularity semantic conflicts. Extensive experimental results on the Chaoyang, Kather-5K, EBHI, and Private dataset show that MCCNet consistently outperforms existing methods.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The United States Preventative Task Force recommends initiating colorectal cancer (CRC) screening at age 45, but screening rates among 45-49 y-olds has been lower than older age groups. Reasons for low screening rates among younger individuals are not clear. Using Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System data from 2022 to 2024, we investigated factors associated with CRC screening among adults aged 45-49; stratified analyses were conducted among the insured and uninsured. Among screened individuals, associations with undergoing endoscopy versus another screening modality were studied. We characterized preventative care behaviors including seeking primary care, time since last checkup, and completion of other age-appropriate cancer screening. Of 50,132 individuals, 21,566 (42.6%) underwent CRC screening. Those with primary care physicians had higher odds of screening (odds ratio = 1.71; 95% confidence interval = 1.47-1.98, ref: no primary care physician), but increasing time since one's last visit was associated with decreasing odds of screening at all time intervals (5+ y ago: odds ratio = 0.29; 95% confidence interval = 0.23-0.38, ref: <1 y). Lower income, rural residence, no insurance, and lower educational attainment were associated with lower odds of screening. CRC screening was completed in only 41.3% of women who had mammograms and 48% who were screened for cervical cancer. Uptake of CRC screening lags in adults aged 45-49, with differences in socioeconomic factors and preventative care utilization. A majority of eligible but unscreened individuals accessed other age-appropriate cancer screening tests, directing focus to patient- and provider-specific factors as potential targets for intervention.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Lymph node metastasis identification has important clinical implications for treatment decision-making in rectal cancer (RC). To evaluate the diagnostic performance of the CT-based Node Reporting and Data System 1.0 (Node-RADS) for lymph node metastasis risk in treatment-naive RC patients, and to investigate the correlation between the Node-RADS score and clinicopathological factors. A single-center retrospective study was performed to RC patients (Aug 2020-Dec 2025) who underwent radical resection surgery and preoperative contrast-enhanced CT examination. Lymph node status was assessed using Node-RADS score ranging from 1 to 5. Sensitivity, specificity, and Youden's index were calculated for different Node-RADS cut-off values. The overall diagnostic performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curves and the area under the curve (AUC). The associations between Node-RADS score and clinicopathological parameters were analyzed. A total of 459 RC patients were evaluated, including 174 pN + and 285 pN-. Node-RADS scores ≥ 3 and ≥ 4 have the satisfactory diagnostic performance, with sensitivity/ specificity/Youden's index of 87.36 %/58.25 %/0.46 for Node-RADS scores ≥ 3 by Reader 1, 89.08 %/54.04 %/0.43 for Node-RADS scores ≥ 3 by Reader 2, 74.14 %/78.95 %/0.53 for Node-RADS scores ≥ 4 by Reader 1, and 72.99 %/75.44 %/0.48 for Node-RADS scores ≥ 4 by Reader 2, respectively. The AUC of Node-RADS scores were 0.831(95 %CI:0.793-0.864) and 0.806(95 %CI:0.767-0.841) by Reader 1 and Reader 2, respectively. Node-RADS score correlated with pathological T stage, N stage, and lymphovascular invasion. The inter-reader agreement for Node-RADS score were substantial, with weighted kappa values of 0.650. The CT-based Node-RADS demonstrates stability and satisfactory diagnostic performance for identifying patients with lymph node metastasis in treatment-naive RC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Timely and effective diagnostic testing, such as CT and MRI scans, supports early diagnosis, improves survival, and can reduce costs. However, it remains unclear whether rising diagnostic test volumes lead to changes in consultations, surgeries and other hospital outcomes. This study examines the relationship between diagnostic tests and outpatient consultations, surgeries, waiting times, length of stay and mortality. Using Hospital Episode Statistics (HES), we examine patients with breast cancer, lung cancer, bowel cancer and prostate cancer from January 2018 to December 2024. Monthly diagnostic tests are obtained from NHS England and linked to HES at the provider level. We apply fixed effects panel data models and an instrumental variable (IV) method, using the openings of Community Diagnostic Centres (CDCs) as an instrument for diagnostic tests. We find that higher diagnostic activity is associated with more pre-surgical outpatient consultations among patients who subsequently undergo breast, lung and bowel cancer surgery, and higher surgery volume for bowel cancer. IV elasticities at the mean suggest that diagnostic activity translates into less than proportionate increases in surgery volumes for breast (elasticity = 0.64) and bowel cancer (0.99). Consultation elasticities are larger - 1.01 for breast, 0.91 for lung and 1.26 for bowel, indicating that increases in testing may generate slightly more downstream outpatient activity than inpatient surgery, particularly for bowel cancer. We find no clear effects on waiting times, length of stay or one-year mortality among surgical patients.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Aspirin (Asa) and metformin (Met) have shown preventive efficacy in colorectal cancer (CRC). Preclinical data suggest convergence on NFκB/PI3K-mTOR signalling and potential synergy. The ASAMET phase II trial tested this hypothesis in patients with resected stage I-III CRC. In a 2 × 2 factorial, multicentre, double-blind study (EudraCT 2015-004824-77; NCT03047837), 51 patients were randomized to placebo, Asa 100 mg qd, Met 850 mg twice daily, or AsaMet for 12 months. Biopsies of normal colonic mucosa and fasting blood samples were obtained at baseline and 12 months. NFκB (primary endpoint), Ki67, EGFR, and pS6K were assessed by immunohistochemistry. After 12 months, compared with placebo, Met reduced global NFκB by -9.04 (95% CI, -17.55 to -0.54; p = 0.04), whereas Asa alone was inactive (-3.58; 95% CI, -12.15 to 4.99; p = 0.41), and AsaMet showed a non-significant reduction (-8.88; 95% CI, -18.86 to 1.10; p = 0.08). Pooled analyses confirmed a Met-driven effect (Met vs non-Met: -7.29; 95% CI, -13.79 to -0.79; p = 0.03), with no impact of Asa (p = 0.73). Ki67 and pS6K were unchanged globally; however, AsaMet increased right-sided Ki67 (12.48; 95% CI, 0.45 to 24.51; p = 0.04). No treatment modulated pS6K. Toxicity was manageable, and no serious adverse events occurred. Met reduces NFκB expression in normal colorectal mucosa of CRC survivors, supporting its potential as a low-toxicity preventive agent. Aspirin did not favourably affect mucosal biomarkers. These findings support tissue-based endpoints and further evaluation of metformin for CRC prevention.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Steatotic liver disease is underdiagnosed despite guideline recommendations for risk-based case-finding. Colorectal cancer (CRC) screening colonoscopy engages a prevention-oriented, healthcare-seeking population in whom liver disease may go undetected. We assessed the feasibility, acceptance, and yield of non-invasive liver assessment integrated into screening colonoscopy visits. This prospective cross-sectional study enrolled adults aged ≥50 years attending screening colonoscopy. Individuals with known chronic liver disease were excluded. Participants underwent hepatic ultrasound and point shear wave elastography. Liver stiffness measurements (LSM) were interpreted using prespecified thresholds of 1.30, 1.50, and 1.70 m/s (∼5, 7, and 9 kPa, respectively). We assessed whether risk-factor-based criteria would have identified participants with elevated stiffness, and evaluated the Fibrosis-4 index (FIB-4) against LSM thresholds. Of 692 adults offered participation, 610 enrolled (88.2% acceptance); one was excluded for decompensated heart failure. Reliable LSM was obtained in 578 of 609 (94.9%). Ultrasound-defined steatosis was identified in 55.5%. LSM exceeded 1.30 m/s in 25.3%; 9.0% and 5.0% met thresholds consistent with significant fibrosis (≥1.50 m/s) and compensated advanced chronic liver disease (≥1.70 m/s), respectively. Among participants with LSM ≥1.50 m/s, exposure profiles were metabolic in 63.5%, mixed metabolic-alcohol in 21.2%, and alcohol-related in 15.4%. Risk-factor criteria were met by 76.6% and captured 46/52 participants with LSM ≥1.50 m/s. At this threshold, FIB-4 showed modest discrimination (AUROC 0.682); sensitivity decreased from 0.706 using a single threshold to 0.529 using age-adjusted thresholds. Opportunistic liver assessment integrated into screening colonoscopy was feasible, well accepted, and identified previously undetected steatosis and elevated LSM.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The COVID-19 pandemic prompted the Veterans Health Administration (VA) to implement programmatic mailed fecal immunochemical test (FIT) screening for colorectal cancer. This paper describes VA's programmatic mailed FIT development, implementation and initial outcomes. VA adapted mailed FIT processes from a Centers for Disease Control and Prevention-sponsored Mailed FIT Implementation Guide, performed regional pilots, created a national Mailed FIT Implementation Team (MFIT), and issued formal policy. The MFIT then provided training and disseminated tools to support VA mailed FIT programs. Programmatic mailed FIT has been implemented in 89.5% of eligible facilities. Between December 1, 2022 and September 30, 2025, 643,933 FIT were ordered and 40.2% were returned. Of those, 89.1% were testable and 10.9% were cancelled, primarily due to missing sample collection date (63.2%) or receipt >15 days after collection (31.5%). Of the 230,427 FIT results, 7.4% were abnormal and colonoscopy was completed in 54.4%. Among 5846 VA colonoscopies, adenomas were detected in 68.0%, and adenocarcinoma was found in 2.3%. Linear regression analysis demonstrated a direct correlation between increasing mailed FIT adoption and the proportion of Veterans who are up to date with screening (r=0.65, p=0.003). VA has successfully developed and disseminated strong practices for population-level CRC screening outreach with programmatic mailed FIT. This practice is associated with moderate levels of adherence and significant improvements in the overall proportion of Veterans who are up to date with screening. Further dissemination of mailed FIT programs, process improvement, and sharing of best practices is ongoing.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Prior to the implementation of standardized screening guidance, multiple diagnostic entry pathways identified anal dysplasia in MSM living with HIV. To describe diagnostic pathways leading to anal dysplasia identification in men who have sex with men (MSM) living with HIV over a 30-year period, before standardized anal cancer screening guideline implementation. This longitudinal retrospective cohort study included cisgender men who have sex with men (MSM) living with HIV who received care at an urban HIV clinic from January 1, 1993, through December 31, 2023. A comprehensive manual electronic medical record review identified documented cases of anal dysplasia. Participants were categorized by diagnostic entry pathway: cytology-first, direct diagnostic evaluation without preceding cytology, or incidental detection during unrelated procedures. Demographic and clinical characteristics were described. Among 347 eligible participants, 47 (13.5%) had documented anal dysplasia. Of these, 25 (53%) were identified through direct diagnostic evaluation, 17 (36%) following anal cytology, and 5 (11%) incidentally. Demographic and HIV-related clinical characteristics did not differ significantly between the cytology-first and direct diagnostic evaluation groups. Among participants in the cytology-first group, 15 (88%) had abnormal cytology results; of these, 9 (60%) completed follow-up evaluation with colorectal surgery, including 7 (78%) within 1 year. Limitations include retrospective design, single-center setting, and incomplete documentation. Before standardized screening guidance, anal dysplasia in HIV-positive MSM was identified through multiple diagnostic entry pathways. These findings establish a baseline for evaluating future implementation of guideline-concordant screening in HIV care settings.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Black patients with cancer experience worse relative survival, yet it remains unclear how far shifting diagnoses towards earlier stage would reduce mortality. We analysed Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) data (2004-2022) for U.S. Black and White patients aged 15-89 years with eight common cancers, using a 2021-2022 period-analysis window. We estimated age-standardised survival under observed and counterfactual stage distributions in which Black patients had the White stage distribution. We quantified the proportion of the racial survival gap mediated by stage and deaths postponed beyond specified follow-up times. Among 1,299,386 eligible patients, Black patients were diagnosed at similar or younger ages and had more distant-stage disease for most sites, except rectal cancer in Black women aged < 75 years. At 5 years, stage accounted for large shares of the Black-White disparity in breast, colon, corpus uteri, lung, and oral cavity and pharynx cancers. The mediated proportion was low for rectal cancer in men, pancreatic cancer, and ovarian cancer, with weak evidence for ovarian cancer at age 75 + years and pancreatic cancer in women. The negative indirect effect for rectal cancer in younger women indicated suppression. Deaths postponed varied by follow-up time and cohort size. Stage equalisation could yield meaningful short-term mortality reductions for several sites, but stage-focused strategies are not universally beneficial. Equity-oriented policies should pair earlier diagnosis with interventions to improve downstream care pathways.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
This study aimed to compare the effects of different treatment methods on the postoperative results and long-term prognosis of patients with 1-2 cm rectal neuroendocrine tumors (R-NETs), and provide evidence-based guidance for the treatment decision-making of this specific tumor size. The retrospective cohort study of this single-center included 736 patients with pathologically diagnosed R-NETs who were treated from January 2013 to August 2024. According to the treatment received, the patients were divided into endoscopic resection group (ER), local surgery group (LS) and radical surgery group (RS). The primary endpoint was recurrence free survival (RFS). A total of 736 R-NETs patients were enrolled. For the controversial 1-2 cm tumor, there was no significant difference in the long-term RFS between the LS group and the ER group (P = 0.280), and the postoperative hospitalization days of the LS group was relatively short (median 2 days vs. 3 days, P < 0.001). Sensitivity analysis using propensity score matching (PSM) further confirmed these outcomes in postoperative hospitalization days (P < 0.001). For 1-2 cm R-NETs, recurrence events were rare in both treatment groups, and local surgery was associated with a shorter postoperative hospital stay.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Transanal total mesorectal excision (taTME) was introduced to improve distal dissection in low rectal cancer, but some previous studies have concerns about increased local recurrence during taTME. This study compared the long-term oncologic outcomes of taTME and robotic TME (R-TME) in neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (nCRT)-treated advanced rectal cancer. We analyzed patients with advanced rectal cancer who received nCRT followed by minimally invasive TME using either taTME or robotic TME between 2008 and 2018. These patients were classified according to surgical approach: taTME and R-TME. The 5-year disease-free survival (DFS), local recurrence-free survival (LRFS), and distant recurrence-free survival (DRFS) were primary end point. Subgroup analyses were performed by yp stage, yT stage and tumor height (AV < 5 vs ≥ 5 cm). Additional propensity score matching was performed to reduce treatment selection bias. A total of 306 patients were included, of whom 94 underwent taTME and 212 underwent R-TME between 2008 and 2018. There were no significant differences in OS, DFS, LRFS, or DRFS between two groups. After 1:1 propensity score matching, 88 matched pairs were generated, and matched analyses also showed no statistically significant association between surgical approach and OS, DFS, LRFS, or DRFS. In subgroup analyses stratified by yp stage, yT stage, and by unfavorable factors (male, BMI ≥ 25 kg/m In nCRT-treated advanced mid and low rectal cancer, taTME showed no statistically significant difference in long-term oncologic outcomes compared with R-TME, and no statistically significant increase in local recurrence was observed, including in ultra-low rectal cancer (AV< 5 cm). These findings suggest that taTME may be considered a reasonable surgical option in selected patients.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Perturbations in gut microbiome composition and altered levels of related metabolites may be related to colorectal cancer (CRC). This study assessed whether pre-diagnostic, circulating, microbiome-related metabolite concentrations were associated with CRC risk. We undertook a nested case-control study of 739 participants in the Colon Cancer Family Registry Cohort (312 cases, 427 controls). Median follow-up time from blood draw to diagnosis was 7 years. Pre-diagnostic plasma concentrations of 70 metabolites were quantified by targeted liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. Odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated for metabolite concentrations and CRC risk using multivariable conditional logistic regression models. Stratified analyses were conducted by sex, Lynch syndrome diagnosis, and age at tumor onset. The primary bile acids, cholate and chenodeoxycholate, were positively associated with CRC incidence, overall and among females. The odds of CRC were higher in individuals in the highest compared with the lowest quartiles of cholate (ORQ4vQ1=1.61, 95% CI=1.05-2.49) and chenodeoxycholate (ORQ4vQ1=1.60, 95% CI=1.03-2.50). Two short-chain fatty acids (caproate, valerate) and three metabolites involved in phenylalanine and tyrosine metabolism (cinnamoylglycine, phenylpropionate, 4-ethylphenylsulfate) were suggested to be associated, positively and negatively, respectively, with incident CRC but these associations did not withstand correction for multiple comparisons. In stratified analyses, some differences were observed according to sex, Lynch syndrome diagnosis, and age at tumor onset. Circulating microbiome-related metabolites, including bile acids and short-chain fatty acids, may be associated with CRC risk. These findings provide insight into potential pathways linking the gut microbiome to colorectal carcinogenesis.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Background Body Roundness Index (BRI) is an anthropometric measure that combines waist circumference and height. It reflects central adiposity more accurately than body mass index (BMI). Evidence linking BRI to long-term cancer risk, particularly in postmenopausal women, remains limited. Methods We examined associations between BRI and incident site-specific cancers (n=33,892) in 144,865 postmenopausal women aged 50-79 years at enrollment into the Women's Health Initiative and followed for a median of 17.9 years. BRI was assessed at baseline in all participants and at year 3 in 60% of participants. Cox proportional hazards models estimated associations between BRI and cancer incidence, adjusting for sociodemographic, reproductive, and lifestyle factors. Results Higher BRI levels were associated with increased risks of kidney, endometrial, liver, esophageal, thyroid, colorectal, stomach, pancreas, bladder, breast, and lung cancers, and with non-Hodgkin's lymphoma, particularly diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. Adjustment for BMI attenuated associations for endometrial, breast, and kidney cancers but strengthened those for liver, lung, and esophageal cancers. Results were consistent across sensitivity analyses and models incorporating repeated BRI measurements. Age-stratified (< /≥ 63 years) models indicated stronger associations for kidney cancer among younger women and a significant positive association for melanoma among older women. Conclusions Among postmenopausal women, higher BRI was associated with increased risk of cancer at multiple sites independently of BMI. These findings support an important role for central adiposity in cancer risk beyond overall body size. Impact In postmenopausal women, BRI may improve estimation of site-specific cancer risk beyond BMI by capturing central adiposity.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Lynch syndrome, caused by pathogenic variants in mismatch repair genes increases the risk of colorectal cancer, which remains elevated even under active colonoscopy surveillance. A deeper understanding of the underlying mechanisms driving CRC development under colonoscopy surveillance in individuals with LS is crucial for evaluating its effectiveness. The goal of this study is to better understand the differential patterns of CRC development focusing more specifically on MLH1 and MSH2 carriers. Patients with Lynch syndrome were identified through the Familial Gastrointestinal Cancer Registry in the Zane Cohen Centre at Mount Sinai hospital, Toronto. This study proposed a general model integrating colonoscopy screening visits, adenoma counts, and CRC occurrence (a joint model) and which accounts for their interdependencies when modelling CRC risk. More frequent colonoscopy screenings resulting in an increased number of adenomas detected effectively reduces CRC risk in those with a pathogenic variant in MSH2, potentially due to a risk-reducing effect. MLH1 carriers did not experience the same benefit. After 10-year follow-up, among individuals with adenomas, CRC risk was much higher in MLH1 compared to MSH2 carriers, 7.9% [95% CI = 3.9-15.8%] vs. 4.0% [95% CI = 1.6-9.6%] in males and 4.2% [95% CI = 2.2-8.2%] vs. 1.6% [95% CI = 0.7-3.5%] in females. Our study identified differences in MLH1 and MSH2 cancer development which may suggest distinct mechanisms impacting CRC. The inverse relationship between adenoma detection and CRC risk in MSH2 carriers enhances our understanding of the adenoma-carcinoma sequence, while the lack of association in MLH1 carriers suggests alternative carcinogenic pathways requiring further study.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Large-scale proteomics may reveal circulating biomarkers of colorectal cancer (CRC) years before diagnosis, yet cross-cohort reproducibility and anatomic site-specificity remain unclear. We conducted nested case-control studies in three prospective cohorts with banked blood and cancer follow-up (median 7 years), totaling 851 incident CRC cases matched 1:1 to controls, with 1,801 pre-diagnostic plasma proteins from Olink panels. Twelve proteins showed significant paired differences between CRC cases and controls (FDR <0.1), with modest effect sizes. These included previously implicated CRC-biomarkers (e.g., higher GDF15 and TFF2) as well as less established associations (e.g., lower LEPR and BCAN). Paired protein differences are significantly distinct in colon vs. rectal cancer pairs (P = 0.005), driven by genes enriched in leukocyte activation, cell activation, and extracellular components. In stratified analysis, for colon cancer, 11 out of 12 proteins were lower in cases (FDR <0.1), including BCAN with 0.83 (0.74-0.94) odds ratio (OR, with 95% CI) per 1-unit increase in quantile-normalized NPX level, with cross-cohort consistency (I2 <0.01). For rectal cancer, 25 out of 28 proteins were higher in cases, including HDGF (OR 1.75 [1.15-2.66], I2 <0.01). HDGF could partially mediate BMI-rectal cancer risk (25.0%, FDR=0.044). Overall, we found that pre-diagnostic plasma proteomics identified proteins and pathways with modest effect sizes and clear differences between future risk of colon and rectal cancer. These findings provide insight for future mechanistic validation of pre-diagnostic plasma proteins as CRC biomarkers and motivate site-specific biomarker discovery that distinguishes colon from rectal cancer.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
PDE4DIP/Myomegalin was originally identified as a Golgi- and centrosome-associated protein that interacts with phosphodiesterase 4D, but subsequent work has placed it within a broader network of organelle-associated signaling and cytoskeletal regulation. This review examines PDE4DIP/Myomegalin as a coiled-coil-rich scaffold linking compartmentalized cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP)/protein kinase A (PKA) signaling, Golgi-centrosome organization, microtubule architecture, and disease-associated pathway remodeling. At the centrosome, long PDE4D-binding myomegalin forms retain PDE4D3 and restrict local PKA activity, thereby influencing Hedgehog signaling. At the Golgi, AKAP9/AKAP450 provides a major scaffold, while selected myomegalin forms support Golgi-derived microtubule organization and endoplasmic reticulum-Golgi trafficking. In KRAS-mutant colorectal cancer models, PDE4DIP promotes tumor growth and MEK inhibitor resistance through Golgi-associated NF1/RAS pathway remodeling. In non-small cell lung cancer, PDE4DIP cooperates with AKAP9 to maintain Golgi localization and stability of PKA regulatory subunit II alpha; PDE4DIP loss activates PKA/cAMP response element-binding protein signaling and suppresses tumor growth. Cardiovascular studies link myomegalin isoform 4 to sarcomeric PKA signaling, co-occurring PDE4DIP and DES variants to conduction phenotypes, and PDE4DIP dysregulation to left ventricular noncompaction-associated cellular changes, although the evidence remains context dependent. Neurological and retinal disease associations remain largely exploratory. Recent work links a PDE4DIP-AKAP9 interaction to cytoskeletal integrity and RAS-ERK/AKT signaling in podocyte injury. Overall, PDE4DIP/Myomegalin is best understood as an organelle-associated organizer whose effects depend on the experimentally reported form, binding partners, and subcellular address rather than on a single linear pathway.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To investigate the computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) features and clinical characteristics of primary anorectal malignant melanoma (ARMM). This retrospective analysis was conducted on the clinical, imaging and pathological data of 12 patients with pathologically confirmed ARMM admitted to The First Affiliated Hospital, Zhejiang University School of Medicine between March 2021 and December 2024, and the relevant literature was reviewed and summarized. All patients underwent CT and MRI examinations. Among the 12 patients, 5 were male and 7 were female; their ages ranged from 37 to 78 years, with a median age of 65 years. The clinical manifestations were diverse, with bloody stool being the most common (58.3%), followed by anal pain (16.7%) and polypoid vegetation prolapsing from the anus (16.7%). Typical anal pigmentation with pruritus was rare (8.3%). Gross pathological examination revealed a polypoid tumor in 7 cases and an ulcerative or infiltrative growth pattern in 5 cases. Immunohistochemical staining results showed that 12 cases were positive for human melanoma black-45 (HMB-45) and Melan-A, and 9 cases were positive for S-100. On imaging, plain CT scan showed that the tumors were predominantly isodense or slightly hyperdense, with a maximum diameter of approximately 2-5 cm. The enhancement patterns varied, but the tumors predominantly demonstrated marked heterogeneous enhancement. On MRI, most lesions were isointense on T1WI (10/12); 11/12 lesions were slightly hyperintense on T2WI, and hyperintense on diffusion-weighted images (DWI). After enhancement, most tumors exhibited marked heterogeneous enhancement. Most of the ARMM lesions in this group demonstrated atypical MRI signal characteristics, making diagnosis challenging. When an anorectal tumor exhibits iso- or hypointensity on T1WI and hyperintensity on T2WI, ARMM should be considered in the differential diagnosis. The CT manifestations lack specificity, and clinical symptoms may mimic those of benign lesions. ARMM may show involvement of the perirectal fat plane on imaging and regional lymph node metastasis and generally shows limited sensitivity to radiotherapy and chemotherapy, contributing to low therapeutic efficacy and poor prognosis. The definitive diagnosis of ARMM depends on histopathological examination, with immunohistochemical staining for S-100, HMB-45 and Melan-A can provide supportive information for the diagnosis of ARMM.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a major cause of cancer-related morbidity and mortality worldwide, and computed tomography (CT) plays an important role in its clinical evaluation and staging. However, CT interpretation may be influenced by lesion conspicuity, acquisition characteristics, and reader experience. Artificial intelligence (AI)-based image analysis may provide a reproducible adjunct to conventional radiologic assessment. This study evaluated a cloud-based automated machine-learning image-classification model for distinguishing malignant from non-malignant abdominal CT images. Images were obtained from the publicly available ColonCancerCT-2025 dataset, which contains CT imaging and clinical information from 40 patients, including 12 malignant and 28 non-malignant cases. For the present analysis, 3,827 CT images were included. The images were divided into training, validation, and test sets in an approximately 80:10:10 ratio, comprising 3,062 training images, 383 validation images, and 382 test images. Patient-level separation among these partitions could not be confirmed from the retained study workflow. A single-label binary image-classification model was developed using Google Cloud AutoML (Google LLC, Mountain View, CA, USA). Model performance was evaluated using average precision, precision, recall, precision-recall analysis, confidence-threshold behavior, and a normalized confusion matrix. A confidence threshold of 0.50 was used for the primary performance assessment. At this threshold, the classifier achieved an overall average precision of 0.998, with precision and recall of approximately 99%. Class-specific average precision was 0.998 for malignant images and 0.999 for non-malignant images. The normalized confusion matrix demonstrated correct classification of 97% of malignant images and 100% of non-malignant images. Representative correctly classified images received prediction probabilities of 0.947 for the malignant class and 0.960 for the non-malignant class. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of cloud-based automated image classification for colorectal CT analysis; however, the limited number of patients, lack of confirmed patient-level separation between dataset partitions, absence of independent external testing, and image-level rather than examination-level evaluation substantially limit conclusions regarding clinical generalizability. Larger patient-level, multi-institutional studies are required before such a model can be considered for clinical decision support.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) surgery remains associated with substantial postoperative morbidity despite implementation of enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS). Prehabilitation improves surgical outcomes, but evidence remains inconsistent. This study evaluated whether multidisciplinary prehabilitation reduces postoperative complications and whether treatment effects vary according to baseline physical function. This single-centre randomized clinical trial was conducted at a tertiary referral hospital in Stockholm, Sweden (28 October 2021-23 April 2025). Adults with histologically confirmed CRC scheduled for elective resection were randomized 1 : 1 to multidisciplinary prehabilitation (medication review, nutritional counselling, supervised exercise, and targeted risk optimization) or standard care (ERAS). Analyses followed a modified intention-to-treat (mITT) principle. Prehabilitation was initiated within 3 days of enrolment. The primary outcome of interest was postoperative complications (Clavien-Dindo grade ≥ I). Secondary outcomes included severe complications (Comprehensive Complication Index), reoperations, length of hospital stay (LOS), postoperative weight loss, physical performance and function (6-minute walk test, Timed Up and Go test, and 30-second chair stand test), health-related quality of life (EORTC QLQ-C30), mental health (Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale), and correlation with the Disability Rating Index (DRI) score. Among 328 randomized patients, 242 underwent CRC surgery and were included in the mITT analysis (120 control, 122 intervention). Postoperative complications occurred in 46.2% of patients, with no significant difference between the intervention and control groups (47.5% versus 45.0%, respectively). Severe complications occurred in 19.0% of patients and were numerically less frequent in the intervention group, but the difference was not statistically significant. LOS and reoperation rates were similar. The intervention group had lower postoperative weight loss and modest improvements in physical performance and patient-reported physical function at 30 days. In exploratory analyses, a significant interaction was observed between treatment allocation and baseline DRI score, indicating greater reduction in severe complications among patients with higher levels of preoperative disability (P = 0.011). Multidisciplinary prehabilitation did not reduce postoperative complications after CRC surgery. However, exploratory analyses suggest that patients with greater preoperative disability derive greater benefit, supporting targeted prehabilitation strategies in higher-risk populations. Registration number: NCT04909567 (https://clinicaltrials.gov/).

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Measures of physical fitness are essential for case mix adjustment when comparing surgical outcomes between patient groups, surgical approaches, and healthcare providers. Commonly used measures include clinician-reported American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) grade and Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status, as well as the Secondary Care Administrative Records Frailty (SCARF) index, derived from routinely collected administrative hospital data. This study compared how these measures of physical fitness, perform for case mix adjustment of postoperative colorectal cancer mortality. All patients diagnosed with colorectal cancer (CRC) between April 2017 and March 2022 in the English and Welsh National Health Service who underwent surgery were included. The primary outcome was 90-day postoperative mortality. Using an established risk-adjustment model, different combinations of ASA grade, performance status, and the SCARF index were added to create eight models for 90-day mortality risk adjustment. Model performance was compared with a full model including all three measures of physical fitness. The basic model included no measures of physical fitness. The scaled Brier score (SBS) measured overall model performance and the C-statistic measured discriminatory ability. Among 91 957 patients, 90-day mortality was 2.8%. A model including both ASA grade and performance status achieved equivalent performance (SBS 0.092; C-statistic 0.833 (95% confidence interval (c.i.) 0.825 to 0.841)) to the full model (SBS 0.092; C-statistic 0.834 (95% c.i. 0.827 to 0.842)). The basic model with only performance status was slightly inferior (SBS 0.076; C-statistic 0.822 (95% c.i. 0.814 to 0.830)) to the basic model with only ASA grade (SBS 0.084; C-statistic 0.827 (95% c.i. 0.819 to 0.835)). Performance status and ASA grade together accurately adjust for physical fitness when risk adjusting postoperative mortality in patients with CRC. When only one measure is available, performance status or ASA grade alone is suitable to support risk-adjusted hospital benchmarking.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
This study assesses the association between colorectal cancer (CRC) screening and a validated, housing-based measure of individual-level socioeconomic status (SES, called HOUSES hereafter) within rural communities and determines whether HOUSES-integrated geospatial analysis can be used to tailor interventions. We used CRC screening data from a subset of Mayo Clinic Midwest patients living in cities without ready access to routine care in the Mayo Clinic Health System in 2019 to represent rural communities. At the individual level, we assessed the association between CRC screening rates and the HOUSES index, adjusting for age, sex, race/ethnicity, comorbidity, distance from home address to clinic, and area deprivation index, using a multilevel mixed-effects logistic regression model. Additionally, we conducted geospatial analysis to examine the correlation between hotspots of 1) lower CRC screening rates and 2) lower SES of the subject population (HOUSES quartile 1). Among 34,489 individuals (median age 64.0 years, 52.4% female), those with the lowest SES (HOUSES Q1) had 37% lower odds of being CRC screening adherent than those with the highest SES (HOUSES Q4) (adj. OR [95% CI]: 0.63 [0.58-0.69]). In the 14 identified HOUSES Q1 hotspots, there was a significant correlation in counts of HOUSES Q1 and low CRC screening (correlation coefficient=0.81). Lower SES was significantly associated with lower CRC screening among rural populations. HOUSES-enabled geospatial analysis identified geographic hotspots with lower CRC screening rates for targeted interventions to address disparities in CRC screening in rural communities. HOUSES may be a useful digital tool for cancer preventive care and research.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Immunotherapies, including oncolytic viruses (OV), are promising therapies that can enhance anti-tumor immune responses. However, preclinical success of immunotherapies in mouse models has not always translated to clinical benefit in cancer patients. This study compared preclinical efficacy and mechanism of action for ASP9801, a vaccinia virus expressing IL-7 and IL-12, using mouse models of colorectal cancer (CRC) in vivo and in human organotypic tumor slice models ex vivo. The murine surrogate for ASP9801 significantly reduced tumor volumes in treated and abscopal tumors in two different CRC models in vivo (MC38 and RO100). Treatment efficacy was accentuated when combined with anti-PD1 treatment, and single-cell RNA sequencing analysis revealed depletion of tumor cells and increased T cell infiltration and activation in both treated and abscopal tumors. However, human tissue analysis ex vivo (E-slices) using PDX models and patient samples showed that ASP9801 is not effective in CRC, consistent with clinical trial results. On the other hand, ASP9801 was highly effective in GBM, indicating indication-specific efficacy of ASP9801, and how E-slice assays can be used to identify treatment-sensitive indications. This study demonstrates the superiority of E-slices over mouse models for predicting clinical response and its utility in planning clinical trials.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Sex differences in immunity shape cancer risk, autoimmunity, and responses to immunotherapy, yet the sex-chromosome genes that regulate antitumor T cell function remain incompletely defined. Here, we identify the Y chromosome-encoded KDM5D histone demethylase as a male-specific suppressor of CD8+ T cell antitumor immunity. In murine colorectal cancer (CRC) models, male CD8+ T cells displayed reduced cytokine production, proliferation, cytotoxicity, TCRβ abundance, and proximal TCR signaling relative to female CD8+ T cells. CRISPR-RNP-mediated KDM5D depletion in male CD8+ T cells enhanced effector function, increased TCRβ expression, augmented TCR signaling, and improved tumor control after adoptive transfer. Transcriptomic and functional analyses further linked KDM5D to cholesterol biosynthesis and exhaustion-associated programs, with KDM5D depletion reducing SREBP2/XBP1-associated cholesterol and exhaustion signatures. Correspondingly, human CRC single-cell analyses supported the clinical relevance of this axis, showing enrichment of exhausted and cholesterol-associated CD8+ T cell states in male tumors. Pharmacologic inhibition of cholesterol biosynthesis with lovastatin partially attenuated select exhaustion-associated markers in male CD8+ T cells and delayed tumor growth in vivo. Together, these findings define KDM5D as a sex chromosome-encoded regulator of male CD8+ T cell dysfunction and point to cholesterol-exhaustion programs as a potential therapeutic vulnerability in male CRC.

Evidence suggests chronic distress influences ovarian cancer (OC) etiology and metabolomic profiles. Here, we evaluated the association of a metabolite-based distress score (MDS) and OC risk. We included two matched case-control studies nested within the Nurses' Health Studies (N=584) and the Prostate, Lung, Colorectal, and Ovarian Cancer Screening Trial (N=348). Metabolites were measured 3-27 years before diagnosis using liquid-chromatography tandem mass spectrometry. We examined the association of quintiles of MDS and 19 constituent metabolites with OC risk using unconditional logistic regression and stratified by tumor histotype, menopausal status, and age at diagnosis. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Oral drug delivery systems show great promise for colorectal cancer (CRC) therapy but are limited by poor gastrointestinal stability, insufficient colon localization, and low tumor targeting. Here, we report an oral biomimetic hydrogel platform, SAM/Au-TiO2@Gel, for colon-localized and tumor-targeted sonodynamic therapy of CRC. Au deposition enhances the sonodynamic reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation capability of TiO2, while Staphylococcus aureus membrane (SAM) coating improves tumor targeting and uptake. Inulin hydrogel enables stable oral delivery and prolonged colonic retention. SAM/Au-TiO2@Gel achieved ∼10-fold higher tumor accumulation after oral administration and superior antitumor efficacy under ultrasound with good biosafety. Moreover, the treatment induced immunogenic cell death, promoted dendritic cell maturation and CD8+ T-cell activation, and was associated with changes in intestinal microbiota composition suggestive of partial restoration. Together, this platform provides a promising noninvasive strategy for overcoming barriers in oral CRC therapy and enabling precise sonodynamic treatment.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Chemo-immunotherapy is limited by the poor bioavailability, nonspecific distribution, and systemic toxicity of free drugs. Here, we develop a reactive oxygen species (ROS)-responsive prodrug strategy by conjugating paclitaxel (PTX) and the TLR7/8 agonist resiquimod (R848) with a phenylboronic ester (PBE) moiety to generate two ROS-activatable prodrugs, PTX-PBE and R848-PBE. These prodrugs spontaneously coassemble into carrier-free nanoparticles (PR NPs) with ultrahigh loading efficiency and tunable drug ratios. PBE modification improves systemic stability while enabling ROS-triggered drug release in the tumor microenvironment, allowing PTX-mediated immunogenic cell death and R848-mediated innate immune activation. In colorectal cancer models, PR NPs suppress tumor growth, reduce systemic toxicity, and remodel the tumor immune microenvironment by promoting antitumor immune responses. This prodrug engineering strategy provides a high-loading, activatable, and carrier-free platform for chemo-immunotherapy with potential for cancer treatment.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Effective screening for colorectal cancer (CRC) remains limited by the invasiveness of colonoscopy and the insufficient sensitivity of conventional liquid biopsy approaches. Here, we present Machine Learning-Assisted, Ago-Mediated Droplet Fluorescence Analysis with a Knowledge-Enabled Agent (MADAK-Agent), an integrated analytical platform that combines an Argonaute-mediated cascade amplification module with a monodisperse droplet-assisted, object-resolved post-amplification fluorescence measurement workflow and a knowledge-enabled interpretation interface. We developed a dual-channel cascade system coupling the exponential amplification reaction (EXPAR) with Clostridium perfringens Argonaute (CpAgo)-mediated cleavage, enabling the conversion of trace circulating miR-21 and miR-92a into distinct fluorescent signals. Following EXPAR-CpAgo cascade amplification, the reaction products were compartmentalized into monodisperse microdroplets using a coaxial flow-focusing microfluidic chip. Droplet-level fluorescence quantification yielded calculated limits of detection (LODs) of 45.6 aM for miR-21 and 59.2 aM for miR-92a. Compared with bulk fluorescence readout, the LODs were improved by 5.20-fold for miR-21 and 3.09-fold for miR-92a. Automated droplet segmentation and feature extraction were achieved using a Cellpose-based analysis module, reducing operator-dependent variability. Based on the extracted droplet features, a support vector machine (SVM) classifier achieved area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values of 0.901 for miR-21 and 0.848 for miR-92a in a cohort of 60 clinical serum samples. To enable evidence-grounded interpretation, we further implemented a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)-based question-answering (QA) agent with dual operating modes. Both the QA agent and the image analysis module are deployable as web-based and local tools, supporting flexible and privacy-preserving use. MADAK-Agent establishes a unified and deployable framework for sensitive droplet-based miRNA detection with integrated analysis, interpretation, and reporting.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Molecular diagnostic technologies based on liquid biopsy are increasingly vital for clinical tumor molecular profiling. Compared to highly fragmented and easily degradable cell-free DNA (cfDNA), extracellular vesicles (EVs) offer distinct advantages by protecting nucleic acids from degradation. Enrichment of tumor-derived EVs using specific surface markers significantly enhances the relative abundance of mutant nucleic acids, establishing a foundation for highly sensitive mutation detection. To fully leverage this enrichment strategy, we developed the MIRACLE platform, an integrated system combining microfluidic magneto-controllable reversible affinity capture with matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry (MALDI-TOF-MS) for efficient, multiplexed detection of tumor-derived EV DNA mutations. The platform utilizes anti-EpCAM-functionalized magnetic beads to construct a reversible capture interface within a herringbone-structured microfluidic chip, achieving over 98% capture efficiency of tumor-derived EVs under turbulence-enhanced conditions. Following EV lysis, a 7-plex multiplex single base extension assay coupled with MALDI-TOF-MS analysis enables simultaneous and accurate identification of seven mutation sites with single-nucleotide resolution. Furthermore, the platform achieved a detection limit of 0.05% for tumor-derived EVs within a background of wild-type EVs. Validation using plasma samples from 26 colorectal cancer patients demonstrated 96.2% accuracy and 93.3% sensitivity, successfully detecting key mutations including G12V, G13D, and G12D. The tumor EV enrichment-guided mutation detection strategy established in this study provides a precise, multiplexed, and clinically applicable approach for molecular profiling in liquid biopsy.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
This single-surgeon, single-institution study aims to show the association between perioperative variables and surgical technique in colorectal surgery, assess discrepancies in patient management relative to established guidelines, and identify underlying causes for improvement. Because the findings reflect one surgeon's practice at one hospital, they are intended as a reproducible audit methodology for single providers rather than as generalizable clinical guidance. A total of 171 patients underwent colorectal surgery at The Brooklyn Hospital between 2017 and 2024, including 73 robot-assisted, 62 open, and 36 laparoscopic procedures. The primary analysis examined the relationship between surgical technique and diagnosis. Secondary, exploratory analyses evaluated associations between surgical technique and 14 preoperative variables, and surgical technique and 14 postoperative variables. We assessed associations using chi-square tests, with likelihood-ratio chi-square tests when more than 20% of expected cell counts were below 5, along with correspondence analysis. To account for the five planned comparisons, we set statistical significance at α =0.01 using a Bonferroni correction. The most common surgical indications were ascending colon cancer (27 cases), diverticulitis (25 cases), and colostomy reversal (20 cases). The technique-diagnosis association was statistically significant (χ² = 102.83, df = 28, p < 0.0001, Cramér's V = 0.51): laparoscopic surgery was most frequently associated with volvulus surgery, robotic technique with ascending colon cancer and colovesicular fistula surgeries, and open surgery with ileostomy reversal surgery. The technique-preoperative association was not statistically significant (χ² = 32.71, df = 26, p = 0.17); the exploratory associations included laparoscopic technique with male sex and NSAID use, and robotic technique with elective procedures and prior radiation. The association between surgical technique and postoperative outcomes was significant on likelihood-ratio testing (G = 41.38, df = 26, p = 0.028), but did not meet the Bonferroni-adjusted significance threshold. Correspondence analysis showed that laparoscopic surgery was associated with surgical site infection, while robotic surgery was associated with shorter hospital stays and earlier return of bowel function. This study explores one surgeon's practice in the key relationships between surgical techniques and patient characteristics, highlighting their impact on surgical outcomes. It identifies distinct trends in using laparoscopic, robotic, and open surgeries. This practice follows established practice, utilizing preoperative collaboration in optimizing surgical care. The methodology of this analysis, although pertaining to one practice, can be applied to any surgeon's data to audit practice patterns and identify areas of improvement.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Hepatobiliary oncology is at an inflection point. Parallel advances in surgical technique, locoregional therapy, systemic treatment, and understanding of tumour biology have expanded the boundaries of curative-intent care yet have also exposed a critical reality that technical resectability is not synonymous with oncologic resectability. Technically successful resection or liver transplantation may be futile when tumour biology is aggressive, leading to early recurrence and limited survival benefit. Modern hepatobiliary surgical and transplant oncology must therefore move beyond anatomy-driven decision-making towards biologically informed strategies that incorporate tumour behaviour, treatment response, and temporal disease stability. The Asia-Pacific Transplant Oncology Symposium (APTOS) 2024 examined how Eastern and Western paradigms intersect across hepatocellular carcinoma, cholangiocarcinoma, and colorectal liver metastases, identifying pathways towards integration. Eastern and Western programmes have historically approached hepatobiliary oncology through distinct and longstanding philosophies. Eastern centres, frequently operating within living donor liver transplantation-dominant systems characterized by organ scarcity and the ethical principle of double equipoise, have traditionally leveraged high operative volume and technical expertise in complex resections. These environments have favoured surgery-first approaches when resection appears technically feasible, alongside response-driven conversion strategies aimed at expanding operability. Western centres, shaped by deceased-donor allocation frameworks and trial-oriented oncology models, have more consistently prioritized biological selection and longitudinal validation of disease control before proceeding to curative-intent intervention, particularly in borderline-resectable disease. These differences are driven by infrastructural and ethical factors, including donor availability, transplant systems, and biomarker integration, rather than surgical capability. This article is an expert statement reflecting the opinion of an international multidisciplinary faculty of hepatobiliary surgeons, transplant surgeons, hepatologists, and medical and clinical oncologists from Eastern and Western centres. It is a narrative expert perspective and not a formal consensus or guideline. This expert statement proposes that the next phase of hepatobiliary oncology requires harmonized, biology-driven definitions of resectability, transplantability, and futility. Comparative evaluation of regional strategies is essential to clarify how treatment sequencing affects recurrence and survival, an effort that is time-sensitive as advances in systemic therapy may soon obscure strategy-specific effects. Rather than competing models, Eastern procedural expertise and Western biology-centred frameworks should be viewed as complementary, supporting context-dependent or sequential approaches that integrate surgery with biology-guided systemic or locoregional therapy. Aligning these paradigms within ethical stewardship of donor organs can establish globally coherent, biology-driven standards that maximize durable survival while minimizing futile surgery and transplantation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Femoral neuropathy is an uncommon but potentially disabling complication that is well described after gynecologic and colorectal surgery, yet remains poorly characterized following extensive pelvic oncological procedures, despite comparable or greater cumulative risk. We describe a 62-year-old man with type 2 diabetes who developed left-sided femoral neuropathy after open cystoprostatectomy, sigmoid colectomy, cutaneous ureterostomy, and pelvic lymphadenectomy for urachal adenocarcinoma. Postoperatively, he presented with hip flexion and knee extension weakness, anterior and medial thigh/leg hypoesthesia, and an absent patellar reflex. Neurophysiological studies supported the diagnosis of femoral neuropathy and identified an underlying chronic axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy. A multifactorial injury combining compression, traction, and ischemia related to surgical positioning and exposure, retractor use, and intraoperative hypotension was presumed. Despite structured rehabilitation, partial motor and sensory deficits persisted at the two-year follow-up. This case highlights the importance of awareness and prevention of iatrogenic femoral neuropathy, particularly in high-risk procedures and patients with comorbidities. We present a summary of practical preventive measures and a structured diagnostic and management pathway to support earlier recognition and more consistent care, while also highlighting recurring gaps in perioperative documentation and preoperative neurological assessment that limit diagnostic certainty.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The Danish Colorectal Cancer Screening Programme has achieved a high adherence, in the 88-90% range, to diagnostic colonoscopy following a positive immunochemical faecal occult blood test (iFOBT). However, a small subgroup does not proceed to colonoscopy. This study investigated factors associated with non-adherence to diagnostic colonoscopy in the North Denmark Region (NDR). In 2020, 278 had a positive iFOBT in the NDR and did not undergo subsequent colonoscopy. We conducted a two-part study consisting of 1) a journal audit assessing comorbidity, inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), hospitalisations and colonoscopy history, and 2) a questionnaire exploring self-reported reasons for non-adherence. Among 256 eligible individuals, 169 (66%) completed the questionnaire. The journal audit revealed that 25% of non-adherent individuals had an ASA score ≥ 3, 65% had a Charlson Comorbidity Index score ≥ 2 and 10% had known IBD. Furthermore, 20% had undergone a colonoscopy within the preceding two years. Questionnaire responses identified recent colonoscopy (n = 29) and haemorrhoids (n = 30) as frequent reasons for non-adherence. Many respondents reported non-medical reasons, including perceiving themselves as healthy, lacking understanding of the programme or finding colonoscopy unpleasant. Non-adherence to diagnostic colonoscopy after positive iFOBT is often not medically justified. The findings indicate a need for improved patient education. Enhanced general practitioner involvement may help address logistical and informational barriers. None. Not relevant.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Tumor-associated macrophages in colorectal cancer predominantly exhibit an immunosuppressive M2 phenotype that contributes to tumor progression and resistance to immune checkpoint inhibition. Repolarizing M2 macrophages toward a proinflammatory M1 phenotype represents a promising immunotherapeutic strategy. While interferon-γ promotes M1 macrophage activation, the effect of combining interferon-γ with granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor remains underexplored. THP-1-derived M2-like macrophages were treated with interferon-γ (0-500 ng/mL) and granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (0-1,000 ng/mL) in a dose-matrix experiment (n = 4). M1 and M2 markers and programmed cell death-ligand 1 were quantified by quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction at 24 hours. Secreted interleukin-6, tumor necrosis factor-α, and interleukin-10 were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. HT-29 colorectal cancer cells were treated with macrophage-conditioned media and assessed for E-cadherin, N-cadherin, vimentin, and Ki-67. Statistical analyses included t tests and analysis of variance. Interferon-γ strongly induced M1 gene expression, whereas granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor alone demonstrated modest effects. Combined interferon-γ (50 ng/mL) and granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (500 ng/mL) amplified interleukin-6, C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 10, and tumor necrosis factor-α gene expression 5.4-fold, 2.9-fold, and 3.1-fold, respectively, beyond interferon-γ alone. Two-way analysis of variance showed no significant interaction, suggesting additive rather than synergistic enhancement. Combination treatment increased the secretion of interleukin-6 and tumor necrosis factor-α and reduced interleukin-10. Conditioned media from combination-treated macrophages increased E-cadherin and reduced N-cadherin, vimentin, and Ki-67 in HT-29 cells. Granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor augments interferon-γ-driven proinflammatory macrophage responses with protein-level changes and functional effects on colorectal cancer cells. The resulting macrophage secretome was associated with a less mesenchymal, less proliferative colorectal cancer-cell phenotype. Concurrent programmed cell death-ligand 1 upregulation provides a preclinical rationale for evaluating cytokine-mediated macrophage reprogramming in combination with programmed cell death protein 1/programmed cell death-ligand 1 checkpoint blockade in colorectal cancer.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Background Return to work is an important survivorship outcome for working-age cancer survivors. Still, occupational trajectories after adjuvant chemotherapy for colon cancer are not always systematically documented in routine oncology care. This study aimed to describe documented occupational trajectories after adjuvant chemotherapy for colon cancer and to explore occupation-level physical demand and break/restroom autonomy as descriptive occupational dimensions. Methods This single-centre retrospective observational study was based exclusively on routinely collected clinical records. Working-age patients with histologically confirmed colon adenocarcinoma, active work attachment before diagnosis, and completion of adjuvant chemotherapy between January 2024 and December 2025 were included. No questionnaire-derived data, Work Ability Index scores, or quality-of-life instruments were used. The primary analysis was descriptive and focused on ascertainable occupational trajectories documented in routine oncology records. Patients with return to work mentioned without an exact date, insufficient occupational information, disability retirement, unemployment, or documented recurrence before return were not treated as uniformly right-censored observations. Results Among 62 eligible patients, two did not interrupt work during treatment and were described separately. Among the 60 patients who interrupted work, 34 had a documented return-to-work date. The observed median time from completion of adjuvant chemotherapy to documented dated return among these 34 patients was 115 days. Eight additional patients had return to work mentioned in the records without an exact date. Among the 26 patients without a dated return-to-work event, three were documented as still on medical leave or without return at the last occupational note, four entered disability retirement before documented return, eight were unemployed without documented return, eight had undated return mentioned, two had insufficient post-chemotherapy occupational information, and one had documented recurrence before return. Occupational coding was feasible in 45 patients; 26 of these had a documented return date. In descriptive exploratory analyses, 22 of 34 patients in higher-autonomy occupations and four of 11 patients in low-autonomy occupations had a documented dated return-to-work event. Conclusions Occupational trajectories documented in routine oncology records after adjuvant chemotherapy for colon cancer were heterogeneous and incompletely captured. The absence of a dated return-to-work entry should not be interpreted as confirmed non-return in all patients. The exploratory occupational analysis did not establish physical demand or break/restroom autonomy as determinants of return to work. These findings support more systematic documentation of occupational status in survivorship care and prospective studies using validated individual-level occupational measures.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Late-stage cancer incidence is being considered as an earlier endpoint in cancer-screening trials, but its trial-level association with cancer-specific mortality may depend on evidence selection and endpoint harmonization. We evaluated the robustness of this association to source-verified additions. We reconstructed the PubMed corpus underlying a 41-comparison review. Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview was used only to prioritize reports for blinded human reassessment. Reviewers determined eligibility, linked reports from the same trial, harmonized endpoints, and verified comparison-level data. We recalculated unweighted Pearson correlations overall and by cancer type after adding earliest-compatible trial comparisons. Among 1209 candidate records, 996 PDFs were assessed. Thirty-three reports absent from the source review were prioritized; 26 were eligible, representing 18 trials, and 8 provided compatible comparisons. Adding these comparisons increased the dataset from 41 to 49 and attenuated the overall correlation from 0.73 (95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.55 to 0.85) to 0.59 (95% CI = 0.37 to 0.75). Updated correlations were 0.49 (95% CI = -0.26 to 0.87) for breast, - 0.23 (95% CI = -0.71 to 0.40) for colorectal, and 0.83 (95% CI = 0.54 to 0.95) for lung cancer. One sparse-event comparison influenced the colorectal estimate. The overall association was sensitive to evidence composition, and cancer-specific stability varied. Late-stage incidence should be evaluated by cancer type and with prespecified sensitivity analyses for evidence selection and endpoint definitions. Model-assisted prioritization cannot replace human eligibility review, trial reconciliation, and source verification.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Surgical video interpretation is a promising medical artificial intelligence application. However, no existing video annotation method preserves the spatiotemporal complexity of surgeon reasoning. Here we show that verbal reasoning and visual attention can be converted into structured, machine-actionable records of intraoperative behaviours. Our method decomposes transcribed verbal commentary into video-anchored semantic feedback chunks, which are classified via a large language model, with spatial grounding to surgical scenes via eyegaze or cursor tracking. We demonstrate method validity and scalability on structured and unstructured annotation tasks. For quality feedback on full-length colorectal procedures, the method reached near-human fidelity for chunking (cosine similarity: 0.95±0.01) and semantic classification across observations (Cohen's κ: 0.71±0.07) and evaluative triggers (Cohen's κ: 0.67±0.14), with excellent usability ratings. For structured critical view of safety assessment in laparoscopic cholecystectomy, implicit annotation yielded excellent agreement with explicit reviewer ratings (Cohen's κ: 0.83, 0.49 and 0.81 across three criteria). We anticipate this method will advance surgical data science by enabling scalable construction of meaningfully annotated surgical video datasets.
